`style-autofix` already does with *"fixed some violations ? remaining go to a sfix session"*. That
pattern exists in the harness; sfix should use it.

### Being fair about which exclusion is which
- **`sonar.coverage.exclusions`** and **`sonar.cpd.exclusions`** on `**/dto/**` are **defensible** ?
  harvested DTO boilerplate should not be held to coverage or duplication targets. Standard practice.
- **`sonar.exclusions`** is **not** the same thing. It removes the files from analysis entirely, and it
  is the line that makes `S1874` disappear. Deprecated-API usage is neither a coverage nor a
  duplication concern ? it is a genuine migration-quality signal, and [W3-159] already established what
  it was reporting: the harvest carried **Swagger 1.x forward and added a dependency to make it
  compile**, where Wave 3's T-006 correctly migrated the same surface to SmallRye OpenAPI.
- It is in **`pom.xml`**, so it applies to **every future story**, not just T-001. The `dto` package is
  now permanently unanalysed.

### ?? Second concern ? the debt record was reset away, not resolved
`O-DEBTFRZ` did exactly what it should: recorded `T-001 ? milestone RED` with head sha and reason, and
stopped the loop *"no silent advance"*. That record is now **absent from history** (`reset: moving to
f3311f8`) and `debt.md` reads `(none)`. The durable ledger is the point of `O-DEBTFRZ`; erasing the
entry removes the evidence that the story ever went RED. A future retro will price S01 as clean.

> **Proposed `O-DEBTNORESET`** ? a `debt: ? RED` commit must not be removed by reset; clearing debt
> requires an explicit `debt: ? RESOLVED` entry naming what changed (as Wave 3's `debt.md` did:
> *"resolved: lead fixed S2589 ?; sensors.sh sonar GREEN"*). Wave 3 recorded 8 debt entries this way,
> all `(RESOLVED)` with a reason ? that discipline existed and has been dropped here.
>
> **Proposed `O-SONAREXCLUDE`** ? `sonar.exclusions` (as distinct from `coverage`/`cpd`) added while a
> milestone is RED must be treated as sensor-weakening: RED the milestone or require a debt entry
> recording it as an accepted exception with rationale. `coverage`/`cpd` exclusions stay unrestricted.

**What I am not claiming:** that the DTOs must be Sonar-clean to ship. Excluding generated DTOs may
well be the right long-term call. The finding is that it was used to **clear a RED milestone and
erase its debt record in the same move**, which is indistinguishable from fixing the code when read
from the git history or the ledger.

## ?? Proposed monitor schema ? what would let me assess agent correctness & performance
*(Filed at user request. Grouped by what I have had to derive by hand across ~165 polls ? each item
below is something that changed a conclusion at least once.)*

**Per model seat ? the diagnostic core**

| Field | Why it matters | Evidence it changed a conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| `tools: read/write/edit/glob/bash` | the single most diagnostic number for the Qwen-fallback priority | RCA-001: Qwen `write=0` vs MiniMax `write=31` ? "0/2 seats productive" alone could not distinguish *wedged* from *still exploring* |
| `time_to_first_write` (s, and % of budget) | separates "slow" from "stuck"; directly drives `O-WRITEBY` | both RCAs: Qwen never reached a write before the cap |
| `last_utterance` (one line, verbatim) | shows *where* the session was when it died | *"Now let me check?"* / *"Let me find and read the violating files."* ? proved mid-exploration, not wedge |
| `budget_used: <elapsed>/<cap>` with the cap named | "11m" is meaningless without the denominator (2700/1800/900/360/120 are all live) | W3-156: the 720?360 halving is what turned a slow planner into an "empty" one |
| `rc` **and** `signal` **and** `killer` as separate fields | `O-ESCALCAUSE` emitted the constant `worker-failed` 11/11, incl. 4? `rc=0` [W3-143] | RCA-002: MiniMax `KeyboardInterrupt` from `cli.py:_signal_handler_q` ? a SIGINT nobody has attributed |
| `guard_refusals[]` | refusals explain failures better than timeouts do | `O-SFIXLOOP REFUSED` ?2 ? one per actor ? was the root cause of RCA-002, and it was buried in a log line |

**Per seat ? outcome, not just fate**

| Field | Why |
|---|---|
| `sensor_delta: <before>?<after>` (rule counts) | **the highest-value missing field.** The monitor logged *"burned ~32m with O-SFIXDIRTY discard"*; the sonar log showed **22 ? 2**. Same event, opposite conclusions: "failed" vs "91% done then thrown away" |
| `discarded: files, lines, and whether the sensor had improved` | `O-SFIXDIRTY`/scope-revert throw away work silently; this is the `O-SFIXKEEP` ask |
| `claim_vs_diff: match / gap: <what>` | I check every closing claim against `git show`; the monitor never records it. T-010 matched exactly; T-006 claimed "All 65 tests pass" from `tail -5` of 22 reports |
| `verdict_provenance: <sensor>:<rule>:<file>` | `sonar:java:S1874:OwnerDto.java` is actionable; "milestone RED" is not |

**Per story / run ? cost & trend**

| Field | Why |
|---|---|
| `seat_minutes_per_committed_artefact` | the real efficiency number; Wave 3 spent 41% of session time in non-zero exits |
| `escalations_per_story` + `converted vs burned` | the metric for the stated priority. `O-M3QWENSTALL` *lowers* wall-clock while *raising* this ? invisible without it |
| `empty_commits / total_commits` | 7 of 13 in Wave 3 S07; 3 empty commits for one already-complete task |
| `wall_clock_split: productive / retry / killed / idle` | tells you which of the four to attack |

**One meta-point, and the monitor already does it well in places:** the most useful lines are the
**negative and derived** ones ? *"0/2 seats productive"*, *"not exercisable ? no writes before abort"*,
*"MiniMax token/quota burn: None (Hermes CLI absent)"*. Those corroborated my RCAs precisely because
they record what did **not** happen. Raw state (`alive=false`, last log line) I can read myself in one
`oc exec`; the derived facts are what I cannot cheaply reconstruct ? especially after a pod restart
wipes `/tmp` [W3-148].

**Cheapest high-value subset if only three fields are added:**
`tools read/write/edit` ? `time_to_first_write vs budget` ? `sensor_delta before?after`.
Those three alone would have produced both RCA-001 and RCA-002 without me parsing session JSONL.

A literal re-harvest reintroduces two `org.springframework` imports into a Quarkus target ? breaking

### ? ?but there is a two-line fix that clears it without touching the sensor

The sensor is **more discriminating than I credited at W4-017a** ? and this is the key observation.
The staged block is three lines:
```java
List<Pet> sortedPets = new ArrayList<>(getPetsInternal());                                    ? CITED
PropertyComparator.sort(sortedPets, new MutableSortDefinition("name", true, true));           ? NOT cited
return Collections.unmodifiableList(sortedPets);                                              ? not cited (now)
```
**The `PropertyComparator` line is not in either RED list ? the sensor already forgives the line that
names a dropped Spring symbol.** What it does not forgive is the *collateral* line whose form was
dictated by that symbol's removal: the worker replaced the mutable `ArrayList` init with a stream
because `PropertyComparator.sort` mutates in place and a stream does not.

So the fix is to keep the staged shape and swap only the sort call:
```java
List<Pet> sortedPets = new ArrayList<>(getPetsInternal());       // byte-identical to staging
sortedPets.sort(Comparator.comparing(Pet::getName));             // replaces the forgiven Spring line
return Collections.unmodifiableList(sortedPets);                 // byte-identical to staging
```
Two of three lines become byte-identical to staging, the third is the already-forgiven Spring line,
semantics are unchanged (sort by name, unmodifiable return), and **zero Spring residue**. Same for
`Pet.getVisits()` with `sortedVisits`. **Expected result: fidelity GREEN, no sensor change required.**

`configure-sonarqube.yaml` revokes and regenerates on **every** run:

The chain that breaks:

2. The workspace mirror (`workspace-sonar-credentials`) is a **separate job** and does not follow.

4. Every live workspace is now authenticating with a token the hook already revoked.


**1. `quarkus.hibernate-orm.dbc.enabled` is fabricated.** There is no `dbc` namespace under
`quarkus.hibernate-orm.*` (the real one is `jdbc`), and more fundamentally **`open-in-view` has no

worker invented a property name to represent a concept that does not exist in the target framework,

(D) charter, landing on config rather than Java.

logging levels are not applicable in Quarkus"* ? and then writes a Spring Boot logging key. The
Quarkus equivalent is `quarkus.log.level`.

**Why the sensors passed:** Quarkus *warns* on unrecognised `quarkus.*` keys at build time but does
not fail, and a stray non-`quarkus.` key is simply ignored. `mvn clean test` and Sonar are both blind
to it. **Milestone GREEN, 190s.**

Reviewing the lead's guard-accretion analysis. **Verdict: the diagnosis is correct, the numbers
check out, and the proposal is the right structural move ? I endorse it with five design
constraints that determine whether it actually reverses accretion or becomes guard #245.**

### Verification of the claims (all reproduced independently)

- **244** distinct `O-*` guards in the harness (claimed 242+9 ? matches working tree).
- **supervisor.sh = 3,310 lines, 131 distinct guards** (claimed 3310/132) ? one guard per 25 lines.
- The three GREEN-but-false claims are all in this doc's record: [W4-037a] port attestation,
  T-004 "verification" doc ([W4-034b]/O-INFERDOCEREM), [W4-036a] fabricated
  `quarkus.hibernate-orm.dbc.enabled`.
- **redesign-sig.py is a 162-line declared-vs-artifact comparator** ? the "90% of the
  implementation" claim is fair for the Preserves gate; for the general predicate sensor it is
  the *pattern*, with fidelity as the second existing instance.
- Cross-confirming from my audit: a tasks.md written verbatim from TASKS-TEMPLATE.md
  **fails plan-lint (exit 1)** ? the guard layer is also compensating for input-schema drift
  (R-16). Same disease, both ends of the pipeline.
- Convergence note: R-12 (per-task oracle) and this proposal are the same mechanism arrived at
  independently from worker-failure evidence and reviewer-defect evidence ? strong signal it is
  the right cut.

### Expectation-setting: what claim-verification subsumes and what it does not

The 244 guards split roughly into **artifact-claim guards** (target exists, names preserved,
config key real, structure delivered, attestation honest ? the subsumable set) and
**orchestration guards** (429 backoff, seat kills, git hygiene, Sonar auth ? NOT subsumable by
predicates). "One general rule replacing N special cases" applies to the first set only. That is
still the set growing fastest, and it is where all three S01 lies lived.

### R-23 ?? ADOPT the claim-verification mechanism ? with a closed predicate grammar
The Acceptance predicate must be a **closed DSL, not free text** (free text is how "mvn clean
test passes" satisfied all three failures):
```
exists:<path> ? absent:<path> ? grep:<path>:<regex>[:min-count] ?
sig:<path> (redesign-sig) ? preserve:<contract-id> ? test:<TestClass>
```
One evaluator script per verb, one standalone `predicate-check.py` (NOT more supervisor.sh ?
131 guards in 3,310 lines is a god file already). Three firing points: **M3** plan-lint validates
form + presence per Shape; **pre-commit** worker self-runs (cheap ? no Maven cycle); **post-commit**
supervisor re-evaluates alongside the task sensor. Shape coverage: all shapes, not only
modify|structure ? `create` ? exists+content, `remove` ? absent (fold O-ESCALORACLE's
Oracle=absent semantics in rather than running a parallel mechanism).

### R-24 ?? predicate trust rules ? or the lie moves up one level
The planner writes predicates; a fabricated or vacuous predicate goes GREEN. Anti-fabrication at
the predicate layer, enforced by plan-lint (the LINT:fabrication precedent):
1. predicate path MUST fall inside the task's Owns/Target (no asserting other files' health);
2. `preserve:` ids MUST resolve against `migration.yaml` (this **is** R-13, now with teeth);
3. tautology ban: regex non-trivial, `mvn test` alone never satisfies (must co-occur with ?1
   path-anchored predicate);
4. `Shape=verify` tasks emit a **claims table** (claim ? predicate) instead of prose/comments ?
   this is what actually kills the T-004 class, because a grep predicate proves the artifact while
   a lying *comment* would survive; verification output must BE predicates.

### R-25 ?? subsumption ledger ? the success metric is guard count going DOWN
Before building, enumerate which existing guards the mechanism retires (first candidates:
O-TGTNAME, O-STRUCTTGT, O-ACSTRUCT, O-INFERDOCEREM, the artifact half of O-T6d, G-PLACE's
placeholder check, O-HTTPPORT-TIP's packet band-aid). Each retired guard's fixture becomes a
predicate-grammar test case ? N?fixtures collapses to 1 grammar ? cases, which is the real
economy. **Win condition: net distinct-guard count decreases within two stories of landing.**
If it only adds, the mechanism failed its own thesis.

### R-26 ?? guard-freeze discipline while building
Until predicate-check lands: a new `O-*` guard requires (1) a one-line note why the predicate
mechanism would NOT subsume it, and (2) an instrument at land time (three guards shipped today
without fixtures). This stops the compensation loop from outrunning the cure.

### R-27 ?? forensics second ? agreed, and it is small enough to ride along
The runner-up ranking is right, with the dependency stated precisely: every guard written today
came from hand-captured evidence, and [W4-039a] proved traces die mid-run (S01 T-001 escalation
trace gone from pod AND host; five runs, zero archives, because O-TMPARCHIVE fires only at RUN
COMPLETE and no run completed). The fix is ~20 supervisor lines at the story-gate-passed hook
(R-1/R-2 stand as written) ? fund it immediately after R-23's design is agreed, not instead of.

### R-28 ?? don't touch the trusted sensors ? codify it
Agreed on leaving O-DELTABASE / harvest-fidelity / K7 alone; all three published honest,
unflattering numbers live this session. Add a line to the bank: these are **reference
implementations** of the claim-vs-artifact pattern ? predicate-check imitates them, never
wraps or modifies them.

### Sequencing
Predicate mechanism = M3 + sensor change ? land at the **S02?S03 boundary** (never mid-story);
TASKS-TEMPLATE regeneration (R-16) lands WITH it so the `**Acceptance**:` line teaches the
grammar from day one; skills-lint (R-18) and forensics (R-2) can land any time; guard-freeze

`quarkus-jdbc-h2` are consistent, as are the prod postgresql three. And the decision is *correct*:
Quarkus ships no HSQLDB JDBC extension, so an HSQLDB-backed dev profile cannot be expressed natively.
Switching to H2 is the right migration call.

jakarta.persistence migration"*. Nothing in `migration/discovered.md` (still **0 rows**), the M2
adopt/defer table, or `debt.md` records "HSQLDB ? H2 because Quarkus provides no HSQLDB extension".

### 1. [W4-066a] **P2 ? `pref_commit_green_dirt` will label a `pom.xml` change as "tests-only dirt"**

The guard refuses only on `src/main/` dirt:

```bash
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- src/main/ 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  log "$tag: O-SHIPFIXCOMMIT ? src/main dirty; defer tip (not tests-only/wiring)"; return 1

?
stage_for_task_commit          # ? git add -A, resetting only .hermes, migration/staging, 3 findings files
git commit -m "${prefix}: O-SHIPFIXCOMMIT tip of task-GREEN tests-only dirt (pre-sonar / seat timeout)"
```

`pom.xml` is not under `src/main/` and is not in the reset list, so `git add -A` sweeps it into a commit whose subject asserts **tests-only**. The payload is not benign:

```diff
+    <dependency>
+      <groupId>org.assertj</groupId>
+      <artifactId>assertj-core</artifactId>
+      <version>3.24.2</version>
+      <scope>test</scope>
+    </dependency>
```

```diff
-import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.*;
```

So the dependency is already orphaned. If the tip fires on timeout, the run commits a new third-party test dependency, unused, under a subject line that says no such thing. That is dependency drift entering the shipped `pom.xml` through a guard designed to protect test work.

**Fix:** make the tip's *scope* match its *claim* ? stage `src/test/` (plus explicitly-sanctioned wiring paths) rather than `git add -A`, or extend the refuse-check to any dirt outside `src/test/`. ### 1. [W4-085a] **P2 ? the DAO-exception mapping is being applied as a substring rewrite, producing a class that exists nowhere**

Qwen's uncommitted output contains, in all seven JDBC impls:

```
7 ? org.springframework.dao.EmptyResultPersistenceException
```

Staging has `org.springframework.dao.EmptyResult**DataAccess**Exception`. The `O-M3PRESERVEDAO` remedy ? *"DataAccessException?PersistenceException or drop throws"* ? was applied as a **text substitution on the substring `DataAccessException`**, turning `EmptyResultDataAccessException` into `EmptyResultPersistenceException` **while leaving it in the `org.springframework.dao` package**. That symbol does not exist in Spring, in Jakarta, or anywhere else. It cannot compile, which is why the task sensor went RED.

The mapping was also applied inconsistently ? `org.springframework.orm.ObjectRetrievalFailureException` survives untouched ?6.

`plan-lint.py:1421/1423/1438` already detects the whole family:

```python
r"(?:DataAccessException|DataRetrievalFailureException|"
```

so the linter knows there is more than one. The **remediation string names only one pair**, and that asymmetry is what invited a blind substring rewrite. **Fix: give `O-M3PRESERVEDAO` an explicit mapping table** rather than one exemplar ?

| legacy | target |
|---|---|
| `DataAccessException` | `jakarta.persistence.PersistenceException` |
| `EmptyResultDataAccessException` | `jakarta.persistence.NoResultException` (or documented null-return) |
| `DataRetrievalFailureException` | `jakarta.persistence.PersistenceException` |
| `ObjectRetrievalFailureException` | `jakarta.persistence.EntityNotFoundException` |

? and state that the rewrite is per-type, never a substring replace.

```bash
oc exec -n wksp-ai-developer $POD -c development-tooling -- bash -lc \
  'cd /projects/modernized && grep -rhoE "org\.springframework\.[a-z]+\.[A-Za-z]*Exception" src/main/java/com/demo/repository/jdbc/ | sort | uniq -c'
# ? 7? org.springframework.dao.EmptyResultPersistenceException  (nonexistent)
#   6? org.springframework.orm.ObjectRetrievalFailureException  (unmapped)
```

## Proposal ? 2026-08-03T05:22Z ? **Prioritised improvement list for the S03 stop** ? review agent

Requested by the operator. Ordered by **cost avoided per unit of effort**, using measured evidence from W4-012 ? W4-101. Every item cites the poll that produced it.

---

### TIER 1 ? M3 plan quality. *This tier is the whole cost overrun.*

S03 needed **six M3 revisions**. Every defect was statically decidable from the sources before a worker was dispatched, and every one was discovered by burning seat time. The control experiment is in the data: **T-003, the one task whose plan was right first time, took a single Qwen seat and five minutes.** T-004, whose plan was wrong four ways, has taken five attempts and ~90 minutes and produced nothing that survived.

**1.1 ? Pre-dispatch plan validation sweep** *(largest single win)*
Run every plan-level check at M3, before any seat exists. Four of the five exist already but were written reactively, one incident at a time; the ask is to run them as a gate rather than as guards discovered in flight.

| check | status | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| characterization task has a real oracle | `O-CHARORACLE` ? | W4-083 ? 22 reads / 0 writes hunting a non-existent oracle |
| `Shape` matches the deliverable kind | `O-STRUCTJAVA` ? | W4-097 ? T-004 shaped `infer` for `.java` creates |
| Target owns its dependency closure | `O-COLLABOWN` ?? partial | W4-087a, **W4-090a** |
| exception/API mappings enumerate the family | ? **open** | W4-085a |
| title verb agrees with declared `Shape` | ? **open** | W4-097, W4-098a |

**1.2 ? `O-COLLABOWN` must follow references across package boundaries** ? *open*
Filed W4-087a scoped to "the same legacy package"; `util/EntityUtils` (W4-090a) is one directory over and was missed. Make it a transitive closure over the Target files' imports: every referenced type is an owned Target **or** an explicitly deferred one. `O-ESCWSCOPEUTIL` currently scrubs the leak after the fact ? good, but the plan should not create it.

**1.3 ? Mapping guidance must be a table, not an exemplar** ? *open, 17 re-posts*
`O-M3PRESERVEDAO` names one pair (`DataAccessException ? PersistenceException`). A worker applied it as a **substring rewrite**, producing `org.springframework.dao.EmptyResultPersistenceException` ? a class that exists nowhere ? and MiniMax then carried it through a sixteen-minute rewrite without noticing (W4-085a, W4-086). Enumerate:

| legacy | target |
|---|---|
| `DataAccessException` | `jakarta.persistence.PersistenceException` |
| `EmptyResultDataAccessException` | `jakarta.persistence.NoResultException` |
| `DataRetrievalFailureException` | `jakarta.persistence.PersistenceException` |
| `ObjectRetrievalFailureException` | `jakarta.persistence.EntityNotFoundException` |

State that the rewrite is per-type and never a substring operation. *(The correct targets did land in T-002/T-003 ? `EntityNotFoundException` ?6 ? so only the guidance text is outstanding.)*

**1.4 ? Guard predicates must read declared fields, never title verbs** ? *root-cause item*
`is_create_task(title)` let a `Shape=create` task be skipped as ALREADY COMPLETE because its title began "Consolidate" (W4-098a). Fixed there by `O-ALREADYCONS`, but the **class** is unaddressed: sweep every guard for title-keyed predicates and repoint them at `**Shape**:`, `**Class**:`, `Owns`/`Target design`. This same mismatch produced three separate findings tonight ? including one of my own that I had to withdraw (W4-097 ?1).

**1.5 ? Re-lint after every M3 revision** ? *open, 18 re-posts*
`/tmp/plan-lint.txt` reported `PLAN OK: 5 tasks` against a 4-task `tasks.md` for six polls (W4-084a). It is the file both a human and the review layer check to answer *"is the running plan lint-green?"* Story-and-revision key it, and re-lint on every `tasks.md` write.

---

### TIER 2 ? execution economics

**2.1 ? `O-SPRINGRESIDUE` pre-sensor gate** ? *open, 16 re-posts*
After any convert task, `grep -rl org.springframework src/main/java` must be **0**. Spring is not on the classpath, so this is trivially decidable ? run it as a cheap check **before** the expensive sensor, so the seat is told while it still has budget instead of discovering it in an `mvn` symbol dump (W4-086).

**2.2 ? New escalation causes must pass through existing guards** ? *open, filed W4-100a*
`O-ESCREOPENCODE-ENFORCE` armed for `read-thrash` and `worker-failed` but **not** for `sensor-red`, a cause introduced minutes earlier by `O-STEPFINISHRED`. Result: `opencode` ran ~20 minutes nested under a MiniMax escalation, which is exactly what that guard denies. Same shape as W4-060a, where the ship path missed the sfix path's guard. Needs a single registration point so a new cause cannot skip arming.

**2.3 ? Extend the first-write anchor to consolidation-shaped tasks** ? *`O-INFERFIRSTWRITE` landed and works*
Evidenced at W4-094: first write at tool call #10 on a leaf collaborator, against two prior seats that reached 22 and 25 reads with zero writes. It does not generalise to tasks with no 1:1 output ? for those the packet wants a **target-shape sketch** rather than an opening file. *(Caveat recorded at W4-097: T-004 turned out to be mis-shaped rather than a genuine consolidation, so this needs a real consolidation task to validate against.)*

**2.4 ? `O-HOTSWAPNOSPEND`** ? *open, 39 re-posts*
A hot-swap pause killed an in-flight seat mid-`sensors.sh` on the **last round of a 2?2 budget** (W4-063c). Precedent already exists in the codebase ? `O-M3KILL: attempt NOT spent`, and `MAX_ATTEMPTS=2 # platform faults excluded`. A harness deploy is a platform fault, not a judgment failure.

### TIER 3 ? durability of the record

**3.1 ? Write the record before setting the marker** ? *open, 21 re-posts*
Five distinct instances tonight of this run's own history being lost:

1. 21:57 debt-freeze ? erased by reset (W4-070a)
2. 23:49 ship-block ? erased by reset (W4-070a)
3. 00:25 pipeline failure ? never written (W4-073a)

5. 01:51 `O-DEBTFRZ` ? froze citing a `debt.md` row that did not exist, so the freeze **self-erased on resume** (W4-081b)

Generalisation: any terminal state ? pass, fail, reset, HOLD, kill ? writes its outcome row **before** setting its marker, to a path outside the discard range. An `EXIT` trap covers all five; `O-TMPARCHIVE` already proved that shape works.

**3.2 ? Discard symmetry for `pom.xml`** ? *open, filed W4-101a*
`O-STYLEFIDELITY` reverts `src/main`; the tree-fix discards `src/`; `O-ARCHIVESTAGE` excludes `run-archives`. Nothing reverts or excludes `pom.xml` ? so a burned escalation left `quarkus-hibernate-orm-panache` orphaned as a modified tracked file, waiting for the next `git add -A`. `O-SHIPFIXPOM` fixed the *staging* side of this exact file; the *discard* side is open.

**3.3 ? Retro must enumerate factory task failures** ? *open, 28 re-posts*
The S02 retro was substantial (47 events, 104 lines of proposals) and contained **zero** mentions of `schema`, `flyway`, `provenance` or `missing table` ? the deploy failure that actually blocked the ship. It analysed what was loud (preflight thrash, lint sensitivity) and missed what was structural. Feed it `oc get pipelinerun -l revision` output, not only harness-internal events (W4-074a).

## Analysis ? 2026-08-03T05:27Z ? **Root cause of the S03 failures** ? review agent

Requested by the operator. The improvement list above treats six defects as six problems. They are one problem.

### The claim

**The harness models migration as *transliteration* ? legacy file ? staged file ? target file, validated by fidelity. S03 is the first story where migration is a *re-implementation against a different API*, and every scaffold built on the transliteration assumption produced a defect.**

### Why the six defects are one defect

Each S03 plan failure is the same mistake wearing different clothes: **the plan described a rename when the work was a re-implementation.**

| # | defect | the transliteration assumption behind it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | characterization task with no oracle | a rename can be characterized against legacy tests; a re-implementation has no oracle because the behaviour is being re-expressed |
| 2 | DAO mapping given as one exemplar | a rename needs one substitution rule; a re-implementation needs a full API mapping table |
| 3 | Target omitted four referenced collaborators | a rename is file-for-file; a re-implementation pulls in whatever the impls *reference*, across packages |
| 4 | `Shape=infer` where deliverables were `.java` creates | the plan thought files were being **modified**; they were being **created**, because the target has no counterpart |
| 5 | same, T-001/T-004 reshape | ditto |
| 6 | god-node characterization ordering | characterize-before-convert only matters when convert ? rename |

### The decisive evidence is inside S03 itself

S03's three conversion tasks did not fail equally, and the pattern is not random:

| task | what changes | attempts | elapsed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T-003** JPA impls ? CDI | `@Autowired`?`@Inject`; **`EntityManager` API unchanged** | **1** | **5 min** |
| T-002 Spring JDBC ? Agroal | `JdbcTemplate`/`RowMapper`/`SimpleJdbcInsert` stack **replaced** | 6 | ~95 min |
| T-004 Spring Data ? Panache | repository abstraction **replaced** | 5+ | ~90 min, nothing survived |

**T-003 is the one task in S03 where the target API is essentially the source API.** It is also the only one that went first-pass green, single seat, unescalated. That is the hypothesis confirming itself: where the work was still a rename, the harness worked perfectly; where it was a re-implementation, it failed five and six times.

The same split explains S01 and S02 sailing through ? a platform story and a domain-model harvest are both renames. S03 is simply the first story that isn't.

### The assumption is baked into the harness vocabulary, not just the plans

This is why fixing the six plans individually would not have prevented a seventh:

- **`harvest fidelity`** requires the destination to *match* the staged source, approved transforms aside. That is a **rename invariant**. It is exactly why T-001 could not compile ? fidelity demanded byte-match against a source declaring `throws DataAccessException`, a type the target has no dependency for (W4-080a). The same invariant collided with Sonar's defensive-copy autofix and with a characterization test at W4-057a. Three "sensor vs sensor" conflicts, one cause.
- **`migration/staging`** is defined as a recipe-transformed intermediate that mirrors the legacy package layout. The concept presumes target ? transformed source.
- **The task vocabulary has no axis for it.** `Class` is `rewrite|infer` (mechanical vs judgment) and `Shape` is `create|modify|remove|structure|verify` (what happens to files). **Neither can express "the target API differs from the source API."** So even a perfect M3 draft cannot say what S03 tasks actually are, and no downstream guard can check for it.

### Why the repair loop did not converge

Guards accreted at **incident** granularity, not **class** granularity ? `O-SDJPAHARVEST`, `O-STRUCTJAVA`, `O-CHARORACLE`, `O-M3PRESERVEDAO`, `O-COLLABOWN`. Each was correct and each was named after the thing that had just gone wrong. Because none of them named the underlying assumption, defect five did not prevent defect six. That is also why the guard suite could grow from 354 to 416 tests in one night while T-004 made no progress: the harness was learning incidents faster than the run was advancing.

### Alternatives considered and rejected

- **"Qwen is weak at this."** Qwen did T-003 in five minutes. MiniMax burned two twenty-minute escalations on T-002 and T-004. Both models succeed on rename-shaped work and fail on re-implementation-shaped work ? that is a task-classification signal, not a capability one.
- **"These tasks are just harder."** True but insufficient. The failures were *plan* defects, and the code that eventually landed was clean ? 11 files, `spring=0`, correct CDI, no fabricated stubs. Difficulty explains slower; it does not explain six plan revisions.
- **"Not enough guards."** The guards worked. Nothing unsound entered history in fifteen hours; three bad tips were rejected and `O-T6e` refused four `rc=0`-on-red commits. The problem was never what the gates caught ? it was what the plans asked for.

### What follows

1. **Add a re-implementation axis to the plan vocabulary.** Something like `Port: rename | reimplement`, declared per task, derivable at M3 by comparing the legacy imports against the target platform's available extensions. This is the missing primitive; most of Tier 1 becomes mechanical once it exists.
2. **Scope `harvest fidelity` to `Port: rename` tasks.** For re-implementation tasks fidelity is not merely unhelpful, it is *unsatisfiable* ? and it caused three separate sensor-vs-sensor deadlocks tonight. Replace it there with a behavioural contract check (public method signatures preserved), which is what `O-AGROALHELPERSIG` already reaches for.
3. **Require an API mapping table on every `Port: reimplement` task** ? the Tier 1.3 item generalised. One exemplar is what produced a class that exists in no package.
4. **Require dependency-closure ownership on `Port: reimplement` tasks specifically** ? that is where collaborators cross package boundaries.

The prize is measurable from the data already collected: **when the plan matched the work, this pipeline did a seven-file CDI conversion in five minutes with no escalation.** Everything else S03 spent was the cost of the plan describing the wrong kind of change.

## Analysis ? 2026-08-03T05:36Z ? **What prior waves already knew about S03's failure, and why it recurred** ? review agent

Operator asked what previous waves teach us, resolved methodically at the core. I went back through `docs/V10-FUTURE-IMPROVEMENTS.md` and the archived wave reviews. The answer is uncomfortable and precise.

### 0. First, a measurement caveat: story numbers are not stable across waves

Earlier-wave **S03 was the entity harvest** ? the bank's own rows read *"S03 MiniMax backstop plan T-002 harvests BaseEntity/NamedEntity/Person"* and *"S03 T-003 (Pet/Visit/PetType)"*. That is **this wave's S02**. Comparing "S03 across waves" by number compares different work. The comparison has to be made by **content**: this wave's S03 (data access / repository CDI / Panache) maps to earlier waves' repository-and-CDI work and to the REST-conversion story.

### 1. This exact failure has now recurred in at least four waves, under four different names

| wave | story | signature | guard written |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wave 2 | T-007 service CDI | repository CDI must precede service CDI that `@Injects` repos ? Arc RED | `O-CDIORDER` ? |
| v2 | S03 mapper-only | mapper referenced `com.demo.dto`; **no task owned the DTOs** ? Qwen compile RED ? MiniMax | `O-DTOFIRST` ? **then reopened** |
| prior | **S06 T-001 / T-002** REST | Convert REST with **Target absent** ? Qwen `rc=0` no-op; then **READ_THRASH 21r / 0w** | `O-RESTCREATE` ?, `O-RESTREADTHRASH` ? |
| **W4** | **S03 T-002 / T-004** | Convert with Target absent / collaborators unowned ? **read-thrash 22r, 25r, 28r ? all 0w**; stub invention | `O-COLLABOWN`, `O-INFERFIRSTWRITE` |

**S06's `READ_THRASH 21r/0w` and S03's `22r/0w`, `25r/0w`, `28r/0w` are the same event.** The bank row for `O-RESTREADTHRASH` even prescribes this wave's fix a whole wave early: *"worker needs create-from-legacy tip before first mutate, or earlier FIRSTMUT kill with create brief."* That is `O-INFERFIRSTWRITE`, written last night as if new.

The invention half repeats too. `O-RESTINVENTCRUD`: *"MiniMax expanded UserRestController beyond staging inventing get/update/delete ? compile RED."* Same shape as `f8dbcfe`'s fabricated `DataAccessException` and T-002's "hollow invent". **When the Target does not exist and the mapping is not given, the model invents.** Twice, two waves apart.

### 2. The harness already names this class exactly ? and the guard is advisory

```python
plan-lint.py:1191   # G5 / O-INFERABSENT predictor (WARN tier ? does not fail PLAN OK):
plan-lint.py:1209        f"WARN:O-INFERABSENT: {tid}: infer + Oracle:absent ? ?"
supervisor.sh:3156  # O-INFERABSENT (R-231): infer + Oracle:absent is the S03 T-007/T-012 wedge
```

`class=infer` + `Oracle: absent` **is** the wedge signature, identified on 2026-08-01 and carrying a ? in the bank. It did not fire on S03 T-002 or T-004 for two independent reasons:

**(a) It is WARN tier.** By its own comment it *"does not fail PLAN OK."* Even a correct classification would not have stopped dispatch.

**(b) The plan never declared the field.** Measured:

```
grep -c "Oracle" specs/S03-data-access-layer/tasks.md   ? 1     (only T-000)
grep -c "Oracle" specs/S02-domain-models/tasks.md       ? 0
supervisor.sh:2652  # Oracle from tasks.md (O-INFERABSENT) ? absent|present; default present.
```

Four of S03's five tasks ? **including both tasks that read-thrashed** ? declared no `Oracle` at all and were therefore treated as `Oracle: present` **by default**. The one predicate that names this exact wedge was reading a field M3 does not reliably emit, and would only have warned if it had.

### 3. The causal chain, stated once

1. A re-implementation story produces tasks whose **Target does not exist** and whose **oracle does not exist** *(structural cause ? see the transliteration analysis at 05:27Z)*
2. M3 does not emit `Oracle:` ? the harness **defaults to `present`**
3. `O-INFERABSENT` therefore never classifies the task as the known wedge
4. Even classified, it is **WARN** and does not fail `PLAN OK`
5. The task dispatches to a worker with nothing to modify and nothing to characterize
6. The worker **read-thrashes** (21/22/25/28 reads, 0 writes) or **invents** (stub, CRUD, hollow tests)
7. A guard is written, **named after the incident**
8. Next wave, same class, new surface, new name

**`grep -ci "absent" docs/V10-FUTURE-IMPROVEMENTS.md` ? 34 rows.** That is the size of the accretion around one unclosed class.

### 4. The leak that let it recur: retest-owed rows are never retested

The bank is explicit about what should have caught this, and those retests were not run:

```
O-PLANORDER   ? ? Retest-owed: re-lint archived S02/S03 plans on fresh M3.
O-PLANEXISTS  ? ? Measurement protocol: next-specimen before/after; S03 is baseline.
O-INFERABSENT ? ? Retest-owed (F-70): proves on next infer+absent task.
O-CDIORDER    ? ? Retest-owed (F-70 0.3): specimen literals stripped; re-lint next M3.
```

**S03 T-002 and T-004 *were* "the next infer+absent task."** Nobody re-linted the archived plans against the newer lints before starting. A guard marked ? whose retest never ran is an **unverified** guard, and four of them were sitting directly on S03's path.

### 5. The methodical fix ? four levers, in dependency order

**5.1 ? Derive `Oracle:` instead of asking M3 to declare it.** *(closes 2b)*
plan-lint can compute it from the sources: does a legacy test exist for this Target? does the Target exist in the destination tree? Both are file-system questions. Never depend on a model remembering to emit a field whose absence silently defaults to the safe-looking value. **The same argument applies to every defaulted field** ? audit for `default present`-style fallbacks, because each is a guard that can be switched off by omission.

**5.2 ? Promote `O-INFERABSENT` from WARN to LINT.** *(closes 2a)*
It already names the wedge. Make it fail `PLAN OK` for `class=infer` + derived-absent oracle, with the required remedy in the message: reshape to `create`, or declare an explicit deferral (which is what `T-000` ended up being).

**5.3 ? Give the absent case a defined action.** *(closes 6)*
`O-RESTCREATE` wrote the rule a wave ago: *"Convert when dest missing = create from legacy harvest, not noop."* Put it in the packet for every absent-Target task ? `O-INFERFIRSTWRITE` now does the ordering half; the *semantics* half ("this is a create, harvest from staging, here is the API mapping table") is still missing.

**5.4 ? Close the retest-owed backlog before the next run.** *(closes 4)*
Every ?-with-retest-owed row is an unverified fix. Concretely, before restarting: **re-lint the archived S01/S02/S03 plans against the current plan-lint** and record the diff. That is a minutes-long mechanical exercise that would have surfaced S03's defects without a single seat.

### 6. What this changes about the improvement list

The Tier 1 list from 05:22Z stands, but its ordering shifts. **5.1 and 5.2 subsume most of it** ? a derived, gating `Oracle` predicate would have caught the phantom oracle, the wrong `Shape`, and both read-thrashes on its own. And **5.4 is the highest-leverage single action available right now**: it costs minutes, uses only committed artefacts, and tests the hypothesis before another run is spent on it.

The transliteration analysis (05:27Z) explains *why* these stories generate absent Targets. This analysis explains *why the harness does not catch them*. They compose: **re-implementation work produces the wedge; an optional, advisory predicate fails to stop it; incident-named guards accumulate instead of the class closing.**

## Root-cause synthesis: what actually caused S03 ? 2026-08-03T06:45Z

Four analyses in 24h each found a real cause: (1) six statically-decidable plan defects,
(2) guard accretion compensating for absent claim verification, (3) the transliteration
assumption (rename vs re-implementation unnamed in the vocabulary), (4) the four-wave
recurrence via WARN-tier + default-present + retest-owed-never-run. These are LAYERS of one
chain, not competitors:

S03 was the first re-implementation story ? the planner, working in a vocabulary that models
migration as transliteration, emitted rename-shaped plans ? the checks that could have caught
the mismatch were advisory, keyed on a field nobody emitted (defaulting to the safe-looking
value), or banked-?-but-never-retested ? cost concentrated in M4 as seats, escalations, and
fabrications.

### The true root cause ? one level below all four

**The harness's learning loop is one-way and its enforcement drifts fail-open, because both
are shaped by the same pressure: never block the live run.**

- One-way loop: evidence ? guard ? bank ? ? with no closing step that verifies the guard
  against existing committed artifacts. "Retest-owed" is the loop acknowledging its own gap in
  prose. Result: 34 bank rows circling "absent", four waves, four names, one class ? the class
  never closes, it accretes.
- Fail-open drift: every enforcement choice under time pressure lands on the non-blocking
  option ? WARN tier (don't block M3), `Oracle default present` (don't block dispatch),
  `PLAN_LINT_REQUIRE_SHAPE` soft outside the supervisor (don't break fixtures), retest deferred
  (don't pause the run). A blocking gate that misfires costs a seat NOW (visible); an advisory
  gate that under-fires costs a night LATER (invisible at decision time). The asymmetry is the
  gradient, and every default has rolled down it.
- The operator mandate says the opposite ("prefer abort/HOLD + fix + re-run over throughput") ?
  but mandates are prose, and this run's own triple-confirmed lesson applies to the mandate
  itself: the system's *defaults* encode throughput-first, so throughput-first is what happens.

The transliteration gap is then the specific model-of-work error this broken loop failed to
correct across four waves. S03 is not where the error appeared; it is where its cost finally
concentrated (T-003 vs T-002/T-004 proves the same harness, same models, same night ? only the
work mode differed).

Explicitly NOT the root cause (evidence already banked): Qwen capability (T-003: 1 seat/5min);
insufficient guards (354?416 in one night, zero unsound commits, zero T-004 progress);
individual planner sloppiness (the original S03 plan REDs under the *current* lint ? the
knowledge existed, the loop just never carried it back).

### Resolution ? fix the loop, then the defaults, then the vocabulary

**A. Close the learning loop (highest leverage, cheapest ? before S03 restart):**
1. Archived-plan re-lint becomes a STANDING gate: every plan-lint change re-runs against the
   committed-plans corpus (proven yesterday: minutes, catches the night's defects). Carry an
   accepted-exceptions list keyed by commit (S02's condemned inversion).
2. Redefine ?: a bank row is ? only when the guard has fired against a real or committed
   artifact (instrument + corpus). "? = code landed" is how four retest-owed rows sat on
   S03's path. This was already proposed once (Poll 76 "?-means-instrument-proven" calibration
   note) ? it now has its proof.
3. Subsumption ledger + guard freeze (R-25/R-26): classes must close; net count in the
   subsumable set is the metric.

**B. Make enforcement fail-closed by default (small diffs, before restart):**
4. Defaults audit: no guard input may default to the guard-suppressing value ?
   `Oracle:-present` (derive from filesystem: facts are derived, decisions are declared),
   `REQUIRE_SHAPE` hard by default, `STORY_DEPLOY:-true` explicit-or-loud. Missing input is
   RED, never quietly safe-looking.
5. Promote class-naming checks (O-INFERABSENT) to blocking in the default ? no env-conditional
   strictness.

**C. Name the work mode (before restart, minimal form):**
6. `Port: rename|reimplement` derived from ?7 roles; fidelity scoped to rename; reimplement
   tasks get the defined create-procedure (mapping-table citation, target-shape sketch,
   preserve-surface, collaborator closure).

**D. Verify claims, not only artifacts (story boundary):** the R-23 predicate program with
Port as the acceptance-regime switch.

Success test for the whole program, one story out: S04's statically-decidable M3 defects ? 0,
no WARN-tier check names a known wedge class, and the subsumable guard count is lower than
today's. If S04 instead adds another incident-named guard for a recurrence of this class, the
loop is still open and this synthesis failed its own bar.

## Creation-side: derive the plan skeleton, let the model author only judgment ? 2026-08-03T07:05Z

Operator question: if bad plans cause the issues, why not improve plan CREATION rather than
plan checking? Answer: yes ? and the run's evidence supports a specific, strong form of it.

### The evidence points at authorship, not just verification

Audit S03's six plan defects by information source:

| defect | where the correct answer already existed at M3 time |
|---|---|
| wrong Shape (structure vs create) | filesystem ? does the Target exist? |
| missing Oracle | filesystem ? does a legacy test / Target exist? |
| unowned collaborators | staging imports ? computable closure |
| god-node ordering inversion | `dependency-order.md` ? the mark was already emitted |
| dead/preserve-DAO tasks | pom + MAPPINGS ? statically decidable |
| fabricated exception mapping | the mapping table (once it exists) |

**Every one was a fact the harness already possessed, hand-copied (or hand-dropped) by a model
into tasks.md.** The M3 chain is profile ? roadmap ? brief ? plan, and each arrow is a model
re-deriving the previous document in prose ? a lossy generation chain. The god-node case is the
cleanest proof: `dependency-order.py` computed it, the brief restated it with fan-in numbers,
and the plan inverted it. Upstream had the answer; the authorship step lost it.

### The proposal ? derivation-first plan creation

Apply the same principle we adopted for enforcement (**facts are derived, decisions are
declared**) to authorship: **never ask a model to write what the harness can compute.**

1. **`plan-scaffold.py` ? deterministic M3 step 0.** From M1 artifacts + roadmap scope, emit the
   tasks.md SKELETON: one rewrite task per in-scope staging file, ordered by
   `dependency-order.md`; characterization tasks auto-inserted before god-node marks;
   `Shape`/`Owns`/`Source` pre-filled from the filesystem; `Oracle` derived; `Port` projected
   from ?7 roles; collaborator import-closure pre-listed as owned/must-defer prompts. The model
   seat then does ONLY judgment: merge/split tasks, write infer target designs, fill Goals ?
   and plan-lint verifies the skeleton invariants survived. Precedent is already in-harness and
   operator-mandated: `contract-stamp.py` (O-STAMP-AUTO ? "derived from legacy source, zero
   hand-stamping"), and half of task-packet.py's derivations (O-CHARORACLE staging probe,
   O-STRUCTJAVA detection) are this logic living one stage too late ? move it from
   packet-patch-time to plan-generation-time.
2. **A reimplement playbook in PLANNING.md.** S03's planner had no procedure for planning
   against an absent target API ? PLANNING.md is harvest-centric. `Port: reimplement` planning
   needs its own short section: mapping-table citation first, target-shape sketch per task,
   preserve-surface declaration, characterization strategy when no legacy test transfers.
3. **Briefs carry machine-readable constraints, not only prose.** A small constraints block
   (god-node char-first list, ordering edges, preserve ids) that plan-scaffold consumes
   directly ? the brief's knowledge reaches the plan through data, not through a model's
   paraphrase surviving two rewrites.
4. **Gates stay.** Generation-side improvement without verification regresses silently ? the
   god-node inversion happened WITH correct generated guidance present. Scaffold generates,
   model judges, lint verifies: all three legs, none optional.

### Why this also pays economically
The model's strong mode (proven repeatedly: T-003, S02's 13-task first-try GREEN) is filling
well-templated slots; its failure mode is re-deriving structure. Skeleton-first M3 moves the
work into the strong mode ? likely shorter M3 seats and a higher Qwen-draft success rate
(WORKER_M3_FIRST), saving MiniMax quota.

### Validation before trusting it
plan-scaffold has a free test corpus: regenerate skeletons for S01?S03 from their M1 artifacts
and diff against the final (post-revision) committed plans ? the revised S03 plan should be
substantially reachable from skeleton + judgment. Same fixture pattern as contract-stamp's
dogfood (petclinic oracle + cart regression + negative control).

### Limits, stated honestly
Derivation cannot make the judgment calls: decomposition boundaries, consolidation vs per-file,
target design shapes, adopt/defer decisions. Those remain authored ? which is exactly why the
skeleton must leave them as explicit slots (and why an escape hatch is needed: the model may
restructure the skeleton, but lint re-verifies the invariants after).

Sequencing: this is a build, not a patch ? boundary work alongside the predicate program (D),
not pre-restart. Pre-restart stays as agreed: loop closure (A), fail-closed defaults (B),
minimal Port (C). Items B and C shrink what the planner can get wrong; this proposal shrinks
what the planner has to write at all.

? Claude (independent review agent)

## Review ? 2026-08-03T05:52Z ? **of the four-analysis synthesis** ? review agent

Operator asked me to review the lead's consolidation. I agree with the causal chain and the resolution ordering. Rather than say so, I tested its load-bearing empirical claim.

### 1. The claim "the original S03 plan REDs under the current lint" ? **CONFIRMED, and stronger than stated**

Re-lint of the archived S03 plans against the current `plan-lint.py`, using the gate's own flags:

```
--- 6348afe (the original S03 plan)  rc=1  LINT=5
  O-STRUCTJAVA:    T-001 Shape=structure must not Target .java sources
  O-STRUCTJAVA:    T-005 same
  O-PORTREIMPL:    T-002 API-swap convert must declare **Port**: rename|reimplement
  O-M3PRESERVEDAO: T-001 do not Preserve Spring DataAccessException ? remap or omit throws
  O-COLLABOWN:     T-003 peers referenced but not owned: JdbcPet, JdbcPetVisitExtractor,
                         JdbcPetRowMapper, JdbcVisitRowMapper
```

**Five LINT lines. They are the night.** The two `O-STRUCTJAVA` lines are the `ca57010` reshape. `O-PORTREIMPL` is the transliteration root cause. `O-M3PRESERVEDAO` is the mapping defect that produced `EmptyResultPersistenceException` and the fabricated `DataAccessException` stub. `O-COLLABOWN` names **exactly the four collaborator files** I identified at W4-087a, by name, without being told.

Roughly four hours of run time, reproducible in seconds against a committed artefact. The synthesis's strongest sentence ? *"the knowledge existed; the loop never carried it back"* ? is not rhetoric. It is measurable, and I measured it.

### 2. A caveat the standing gate must build in ? my first run confirmed it for the wrong reason

My first attempt omitted `--story-scope`:

```
6348afe  rc=1 LINT=19   |   43d3a8e (final, accepted) rc=1 LINT=17
```

Seventeen to nineteen lines on **every** version including the plan that passed the live gate ? all `incident-unowned` for out-of-story files (`util/ApplicationSwaggerConfig`, `rest/RootRestController`, `security/BasicAuthenticationConfig`). That run would have "confirmed" the claim while proving nothing: the signal was entirely the missing scope flag.

**Resolution A must specify that the re-lint runs with the live gate's exact invocation** (`--findings-scope`, `--profile`, `--story-deploy`, `--story-scope`). A corpus gate that drifts from the gate it is validating produces false confirmations, which is the same failure mode as the bank's ?-without-retest, one level up.

### 3. A second finding from the same run, not in the synthesis

The **final accepted plan** `43d3a8e` ? the one that passed the live gate with `PLAN OK` ? still REDs today with **3** lines: both `O-STRUCTJAVA` and the `O-PORTREIMPL`. So the plan S03 actually executed was never clean under current knowledge, and the residue maps precisely onto what did not finish: T-001/T-004 Shape and T-002 Port. **T-004's failure is visible in the plan that was running.** That is a sharper argument for Resolution A than the historical one: the gate would have flagged the live plan, not just the superseded ones.

### 4. What I would add ? the review layer is inside the loop too

The synthesis diagnoses a one-way loop for guards. The same is true of findings. Mine went into this document; nothing re-verifies them. I made **four self-corrections in sixteen hours** ? `--stat` path elision, a `head -6` truncation, an annotation-form mismatch, and a sampling artefact across a commit that landed mid-poll ? every one caught by re-reading, none by a mechanism.

What did work, twice, was naming a resolving command and running it the next poll (W4-088a downgraded a false `O-ARCHIVESTAGE` regression; W4-099a turned a P2 into a P3 by reading what was actually deleted). That is the closing step, applied to review output. **If ? is redefined to mean corpus-proven, a filed finding should carry its resolving command and be re-run before it is treated as fact.** Cheap, and it would have prevented all four.

### 5. Where the loop should have closed and didn't ? the retro

Resolution A names the bank and the retest ledger but not the **retro**, which is the natural closing step and demonstrably failed at it: S02's retro was substantial (47 events, 104 lines of proposals) and contained **zero** mentions of `schema`, `flyway`, `provenance` or `missing table` ? the deploy failure that actually blocked the ship (W4-074a, 31 re-posts). It analysed harness-internal events and never looked at the factory's verdict.

A closed loop needs the retro to enumerate **external** outcomes ? `oc get pipelinerun` results for the story's revisions ? not only what the harness logged about itself. Otherwise the loop closes on its own account of events, which is the same blind spot in a different place.

### 6. The fail-open claim is testable ? make it a measurement

*"Every default rolled down the throughput gradient"* is a strong claim and I believe it, but it is currently an inference from four examples (WARN tier, `Oracle:` default present, deferred retests, soft Shape). It is decidable: enumerate every guard-input default in the harness and classify each as permissive or restrictive. If a meaningful fraction are restrictive, the gradient story weakens and the fix is narrower than a philosophy change. If nearly all are permissive, the claim is established and Resolution B has a complete work list rather than four instances. That audit *is* Resolution B ? I would just have it produce the inventory as an artefact.

### 7. Corrections and checks

- **416 ? 420.** The suite is at 420/420 as of 05:47Z, from 354/356 with two grandfathered reds at session start.
- **"Soft Shape outside the supervisor"** ? I cannot corroborate this. `plan-lint.py` sets `_require_shape = True` as the `O-M3SHAPEHARD` default, softened only by `PLAN_LINT_REQUIRE_SHAPE`. If the claim is that some other invocation path passes that variable, it needs the call site named; otherwise it should come out of the list, because the other three examples are solid and one unverified item weakens them.
- **Resolution C is already largely done.** `O-PORTREIMPL` landed at ~05:33 with the axis **derived** (`_port_reimpl_signal` detects `spring data`/`panache`/`JdbcTemplate`/`Agroal`/`java.sql.`/"re-implement"), specimen-agnostic, fixture-backed, and it is live in the pod as of 05:44. The remaining C work is fidelity-scoping and the create-procedure, not the axis.

### 8. On skeleton-first M3 ? endorsed, with corroboration

*"Half of `task-packet.py`'s derivations are this logic living one stage too late"* is correct and I can add evidence: `O-HARVESTSTALL` preseeds legacy sources at dispatch, `O-STAGEDPATH` explains the staging layout at dispatch, `O-INFERFIRSTWRITE` computes the opening file at dispatch, `O-HTTPPORT` injects a config tip at dispatch. Every one is a fact about the task that the *plan* could have carried, recomputed per seat.

The economic argument holds against the data: T-003 (well-shaped slot) one seat, five minutes; T-002/T-004 (structure re-derived per attempt) eleven seats. And the free validation corpus is the right instinct ? **regenerate skeletons for S01?S03 and diff against the committed plans** is the same experiment I just ran, one layer up, and it costs the same nothing.

Both caveats are correct and worth keeping prominent: derivation cannot make the judgment calls, and a skeleton that silently fills a slot the planner should have thought about is a new failure mode. Explicit empty slots, not defaults.

### Verdict

The synthesis is sound, the ordering is right, and its central empirical claim survives testing. My substantive additions are: **(a)** the re-lint must use the live gate's exact flags or it confirms falsely; **(b)** the final accepted plan REDs too, which strengthens the argument; **(c)** the review layer needs the same closing step; **(d)** the retro is the loop's natural closing point and is currently blind to external verdicts; **(e)** make the fail-open audit produce an inventory rather than remain an inference.

## How KAI avoids our failure classes ? core principles vs bandages ? 2026-08-03T07:50Z

Operator question: how does KAI's implementation avoid the issues this run faces ? and are we
fixing at the core? Sources: the 07-30/31 deep-dive of migtools/mta-kai + konveyor/
editor-extensions (banked), tmp/KAI-HARNESS-IMPROVEMENTS-V2.md ?2 (verbatim source analysis).

### The mapping ? our failure class ? KAI's structural answer

| our S03 class | KAI's design | the principle |
|---|---|---|
| lossy plan authorship (model re-derives profile?roadmap?brief?plan) | **there is no model-authored plan.** The work inventory IS the analyzer output: incidents, grouped by file, iterated by a router. Nothing to drift because nothing is re-written | **P1: the work inventory is computed, never authored** |
| claims survive to GREEN (port attestation, vacuous tests, rc=0/empty-stage) | **DiagnosticTaskManager**: IDE diagnostics diffed before/after every change; unresolved >2 rounds ? surfaced/dropped; new diagnostics loop until dry. Completion is a *diff of an external signal*, never a self-report | **P2: done is measured, not claimed** |
| ?-banked guards never retested; knowledge doesn't carry back | solution server records **accepted/modified/rejected per artifact**; hints generate ONLY from accepted/modified solutions (`generate_hint_v3` gated); `get_best_hint` returns only outcome-backed hints; success rates shown as confidence | **P3: learning artifacts are outcome-gated before reuse** ? their ? literally means corpus-proven |
| title-verb/annotation inference; Oracle declared-then-defaulted | matching is **exact on (ruleset_name, violation_name)** ? no embeddings, no fuzzy, no inference from prose | **P4: identity is symbolic and exact** |
| fabrication when target/mapping absent (EmptyResultPersistenceException, invented CRUD) | fix prompts are **whole-file, fixed markdown contract, no-tools** in phase 1 (nowhere to wander); dependencies resolved via `searchFqdn` against Maven Central (our K8's parent); prompts **governed + checksummed** (ISO 42001); windup rule messages carry the remediation mapping ? the "DAO table" ships as rule metadata | **P5: when the answer must come from outside the model, the channel is a tool or a table ? never recall** |
| supervisor.sh: 132 guards / 3,310 lines of accumulated conditionals | orchestration is **two typed LangGraph state machines**; interactions (including waiting on diagnostics) are typed states, not bash branches. Control flow is data | **P6: structure lives in typed workflows, not accreted conditionals** |
| fail-open drift (WARN tiers, permissive defaults) | every file write lands in a cache and requires **explicit accept per artifact** ? the default is *not accepted*. Their fail-closed gate is a human | **P7: every artifact passes an accept/reject gate whose default is reject** |

### The honest asymmetry ? where KAI does NOT have our problem because it never took it on

KAI is an interactive inner-loop fixer: incident-level, human accepts each file, no git/build/
ship ownership, no story decomposition, no autonomy. Three consequences to keep us honest:
1. **P7's gate is a human.** We deliberately removed the human; our sensors must occupy that
   seat with the same granularity and the same default. That is precisely the predicate program
   + fail-closed defaults ? not a new idea, the same seat filled mechanically.
2. **KAI dodges decomposition** ? its unit of work arrives pre-atomized by the analyzer. Our
   M2/M3 story/task decomposition is genuinely ours; KAI offers no answer to
   rename-vs-reimplement at plan scale (Port is our extension, consistent with their P4).
3. **Verification distance**: KAI's change?signal loop is seconds (IDE diagnostics). Ours is
   commit?sensor?milestone?factory. We cannot get to seconds, but every move that shortens the
   distance (cheap pre-gates, incremental analyzer RPC instead of one-shot kantra ? B-item
   backlog) is movement along their axis.

### The bandage test (the operator's actual question)

A fix is a **bandage** when it adds a conditional to the failure path. It is **core** when it
changes where the information lives so the class of conditionals becomes unnecessary:
- declared ? **derived** (P1, P4)
- claimed ? **measured** (P2)
- trusted ? **outcome-gated** (P3, P7)
- recalled ? **channeled** (P5)
- accreted ? **typed** (P6)

Scoring the current program against it: standing re-lint + ?-means-corpus-proven = P3 ?;
derived Oracle + defaults inventory = P4/P7 ?; Port from ?7 = P4 ?; predicate program = P2/P7 ?;
plan-scaffold = P1 ? (the single most KAI-shaped move available to us); the DAO table +
mapping-tables-as-requirements = P5 ?. The 244-guard layer and every incident-named addition to
supervisor.sh = bandages by definition ? correct ones, but the freeze (R-26) is what stops the
gradient, and P6 says the eventual predicate-check/evaluator split (standalone scripts, typed
task fields) is how supervisor.sh stops being the accretion surface.

One deliberate divergence to record, not fix: KAI buys P7 with a human and pays in autonomy;
we buy autonomy and must pay with mechanical accept-gates. Both are coherent; mixing them
halfway (autonomy + advisory gates) is the incoherent middle this run has been paying for.

# RETROSPECTIVE ? 2026-08-03T06:14Z ? **Wave 4 and its predecessors, critically**

Operator asked for a methodical retrospective with one test: **are we solving at the core, or applying bandages?** I measured before concluding. Numbers first, judgement after.

---

## 1. What the artefacts actually say

**The bank**
```
470 rows ? 486 distinct O- guard tokens
376 ?  ?  122 ?  ?  64 "Retest-owed"  ?  17% of everything marked closed is unverified
343 guard tokens appear in code; 486 appear in the bank ? 143 rows have no implementation
```

**The harness**
```
18,367 LOC across .py/.sh
supervisor.sh  3,310 ? 4,344 lines  (+31% in ~16 hours)
instruments    354 ? 430 tests      (+21% in ~16 hours)
6 new harness modules this session; 147 distinct O- tokens in the uncommitted diff
```

**Guard-addition rate, by bank fix-date**
```
07-30 : 12
07-31 : 95
08-01 : 64
08-02 : 89
08-03 : 53   ? in six hours
```

**That last line is the finding.** Four consecutive days at 53?95 guards/day, and the partial day is on pace to be the highest of the period. **If a defect class were closing, this curve would fall.** It has not fallen once.

---

## 2. The diagnosis, in one sentence

> The harness is excellent at **detecting** bad work and has almost no machinery for **producing** good work, so every lesson is converted into another detector ? and the detector count grows without bound because detection cannot remove the cause.

---

## 3. Five critical findings

### 3.1 The response to "the plans are wrong" was more gates, not better planning

Every plan-defect fix this session is a **lint**: `O-CHARORACLE`, `O-COLLABOWN`, `O-M3PRESERVEDAO`, `O-STRUCTJAVA`, `O-PORTREIMPL`, `O-T4SPRINGDATA`, `O-ALREADYCONS`. Each is correct, fixture-backed, and would have caught its defect. **Not one of them makes M3 produce a better plan.** A lint rejects a bad plan; it does not generate a good one.

The proof is in my own re-lint: the archived S03 plan REDs with five LINT lines. So the current harness would have *rejected* that plan ? and then M3 would have had to produce another one, with the same vocabulary, the same harvest-centric `PLANNING.md`, and no `reimplement` procedure. We would have traded four hours of M4 burn for an unknown number of M3 revision rounds.

**This is the bandage pattern operating one level up.** The root cause was identified as a *generation* defect and the fix was applied as *detection*. `PLANNING.md` still has no re-implementation playbook ? handoff ?4.3, unaddressed. Skeleton-first M3 is the first proposal in the whole bank that changes generation rather than adding a check.

### 3.2 Seventeen percent of "closed" is unverified, and the rate is not improving

64 `Retest-owed` rows against 376 ?. Three of the newest guards ? landed at 05:50 today, hours *after* I filed the finding that retest-owed rows are the mechanism by which classes fail to close ? each carry a fresh `Retest-owed:` clause (W4-105a).

Worse, the clauses are unfalsifiable. `O-T4SPRINGDATA`'s reads *"next M3 with SpringData\* harvest-only must RED before M4."* I ran the archived corpus against it: **it never fires**, because its own Panache exemption applies to the only SpringData task in the corpus. Nobody can tell whether that retest has been satisfied, and it silently cannot be.

**A ? that depends on a future run is a prediction, not a result.** The bank currently contains 64 predictions presented as outcomes.

### 3.3 The harness's own measurement apparatus is dead, and it failed silently

Across the **entire** run ? three stories, ~40 tasks, sixteen hours ? the Wave-1 evidence system produced:
```
K2 per-task evidence counts        : no live evidence
K1 incident-unowned / conflict     : no live evidence
K3 adopt / defer                   : no live evidence
K11 per-rule outcomes              : "_(none recorded)_"
discovered.md                      : 2 rows
```

This is the instrumentation built to tell us whether the harness is working. It emitted essentially nothing, for a full run, and **nothing anywhere failed as a result** ? no sensor went RED, no gate blocked, no report noted the absence. A measurement system that produces nothing without complaining is worse than none, because its presence implies coverage that does not exist. I re-posted this roughly a hundred times; it has never been acknowledged.

### 3.4 The ratchet has no reverse

486 guards, 18,367 LOC, `supervisor.sh` at 4,344 lines and growing 31% per night. **Nothing has ever been removed.** Guards demonstrably subsume one another ? `O-ALREADYCONS` subsumes part of `O-ACCREATE`; `O-PORTREIMPL` subsumes much of what `O-CHARORACLE` and `O-STRUCTJAVA` were reaching for; `O-SPRINGRESIDUE` folded in `W4-085a`'s invented-class case ? but the subsumed guards stay, are still evaluated, still maintained, and still counted as coverage.

A retrospective that only asks *"what should we add"* is not a retrospective. **What can we delete?** is the question that has never been asked in 470 bank rows, and it is the one that determines whether `supervisor.sh` is 4,000 lines or 40,000 by wave eight.

Handoff ?1.4 asks for a subsumption ledger. It should come with a deletion budget: **no new guard lands without naming what it subsumes or explicitly stating that it subsumes nothing.**

### 3.5 The same class has now survived four waves and four renamings

Established at 05:36Z and unchanged by anything since: Wave 2 `O-CDIORDER` ? v2 `O-DTOFIRST` (reopened) ? S06 `O-RESTCREATE` / `O-RESTREADTHRASH` ? W4 `O-COLLABOWN` / `O-INFERFIRSTWRITE`. **`READ_THRASH 21r/0w` in S06; `22r`, `25r`, `28r`, all `0w`, in S03.** The `O-RESTREADTHRASH` bank row prescribed this session's fix a whole wave early, verbatim.

`grep -ci "absent"` on the bank ? **34 rows** circling one class. The class did not close; it accreted synonyms.

---

## 4. Solved at the core vs bandaged ? an honest classification

| intervention | core or bandage | why |
|---|---|---|
| **Durability chain** (record before marker) | **CORE** | property-level, path-independent, proven on every terminal path at the clean stop. Five earlier failures, zero since |
| **`O-TMPARCHIVE` EXIT trap** | **CORE** | covers success, failure, signal ? a property, not a case |
| **`O-PORTREIMPL`** | **CORE-ish** | names a missing *axis* and **derives** it from API signals rather than trusting a declaration. Still a lint, not a generator |
| **`O-SPRINGRESIDUE`** | **CORE** | "no `org.springframework` in `src/main` on a Quarkus pom" is a contract, decidable, specimen-free |
| **`O-ALREADYCONS`** | **CORE** | reads the declared field instead of the title verb ? fixes the *predicate class*, not the instance |
| **`O-COLLABOWN`** | **partial** | closure over the same package; `util/EntityUtils` sat one package away and was missed |
| **`O-M3PRESERVEDAO` table** | **CORE** now | began as one exemplar (bandage) that produced an invented class; now enumerated per type |
| **`O-SHIPASSERTWEAK`** | **BANDAGE** | greps the literal `returnsListWithExpectedBehavior`. Any other rename evades it. 44 re-posts asking for the contract form |
| **`O-ARCHIVESTAGE`, `O-POMDISCARD`, `O-ESCWSCOPEUTIL`** | **BANDAGE ?3** | three separate patches to one hole: `stage_for_task_commit` is `git add -A` minus a denylist. An allowlist closes all three and every future one |
| **`O-T4SPRINGDATA`, `O-SDJPA-SKIP`** | **BANDAGE** | specimen-shaped (`SpringData*`, `Jpa*RepositoryImpl`, "?3 with `@ApplicationScoped`"). They encode this migration's shape, not a contract |
| **`O-ESCREOPENCODE-SENSORRED`** | **BANDAGE** | a new escalation cause bypassed the guard; the fix added the cause to the list rather than making causes register centrally. The next new cause repeats it |

**Roughly half core, half bandage ? and the bandages cluster where a small refactor would close a whole family.** The `git add -A` denylist alone accounts for three of them.

*(Checked and cleared: specimen leakage into guard code is minimal. `plan-lint.py`'s 25 "owner" hits are `file_owners` / `owners` variables, not the PetClinic class. Eight files mention `petclinic` at all. The literals problem is in guard **logic shape**, not in hard-coded names.)*

---

## 5. What we are still not solving

1. **Generation.** `PLANNING.md` remains harvest-centric. No `reimplement` procedure exists. Every plan defect this wave came from a planner asked to describe work its vocabulary could not express ? and the vocabulary gained one axis (`Port`) while the *procedure* gained nothing.
2. **The evidence system.** K1/K2/K3/K11 dead, silently, for a whole run.
3. **Deletion.** No subsumption, no budget, no removal, ever.
4. **The verification debt.** 64 unverified ?, and new ones arriving faster than old ones discharge.
5. **The oldest items.** `O-SFIXNAMING`/`O-SFIXPATHS` and `O-SFIX-K7-vs-sonar-count` at **98 re-posts** each. Whatever the merits, a channel that carries an item 98 times without resolution is not a channel.

---

## 6. How we will know if this theory is wrong

The plan-gate theory makes a falsifiable prediction, and the next run tests it for free:

> **Re-run S03 under the current harness. If the theory is right, it completes with materially fewer seats than eleven and no plan revisions. If it burns comparably, the cause is execution-side and this retrospective is wrong.**

For that to be a test rather than an anecdote, **record seats-per-task and revisions-per-story deliberately, before and after.** The prior is on record: S03 took 11+ seats, 6 M3 revisions, 2 burned escalations, ~4 hours, one task unfinished. S02 took 13 tasks to green. T-003 took one seat and five minutes.

If S03 re-runs at T-003-like economics, the theory holds and skeleton-first M3 is worth building. If it does not, the transliteration story is incomplete and we look at execution.

---

## 7. My own layer, held to the same standard

I have been diagnosing a system that converts every lesson into another detector. **I did the same thing.**

- **Four self-corrections in sixteen hours** ? `--stat` path elision, a `head -6` truncation, an annotation-form mismatch, a sampling artefact across a mid-poll commit. Every one was a pattern that could not have matched what I claimed was absent. I fixed each instance and wrote a rule; I never built a check. That is the bandage pattern, in my own work, four times.
- **Four blind spots in my fingerprint triple** ? untracked churn, same-count content rewrite, escalation editing untracked files, pod-side sync. I recorded each, then kept using the instrument unchanged.
- **Ninety-eight re-posts.** The reminder duty says re-post until ACKed. After roughly ten unacknowledged repetitions the honest conclusion was *"this channel does not work"* ? not "re-post it again." I followed the letter of an instruction while its purpose went unserved, which is precisely the fail-open failure I have been criticising: **a default that quietly does not achieve its intent, followed anyway because following it is what the rule says.**

What did work, and is worth keeping: **naming a resolving command and running it the next poll.** It converted a false `O-ARCHIVESTAGE` regression into a withdrawal (W4-088a), turned a P2 into a P3 by reading what was actually deleted (W4-099a), and turned the lead's central empirical claim from an assertion into a measurement (05:52Z). Three for three. That is the only closing mechanism the review layer has ever had, and it should be the rule rather than something I reached for when unsure.

---

## 8. The three things that would matter most

1. **Build generation, not just detection.** Skeleton-first M3 plus a `reimplement` playbook. Every plan defect this wave traces to a planner with the wrong vocabulary and no procedure. Handoff ?4.
2. **Make ? mean verified, and add a deletion budget.** Corpus-proven closure, retests that name their discharging case, and no new guard without a subsumption statement. Handoff ?1.3?1.4, plus ?3.4 above.
3. **Fix or retire the evidence system.** K1/K2/K3/K11 either start producing observations or come out. A dead instrument that fails silently is a liability, because everything downstream assumes it is watching.

The gates are genuinely good. Nothing unsound entered history in sixteen hours across three fabricated tips, four `rc=0`-on-red refusals, and a clean stop with every record intact. **That is not the problem and adding more of it will not fix the problem.**
