# V4 START CONDITIONS ? 2026-08-03T09:27Z ? operator policy, expanded into checkable conditions ? Claude (solution architect)

The operator's statement: *"I don't want to start a new run until all recommendations have
been implemented, and we are completely sure the next migration wave will be a significant
improvement compared to previous runs, and we can verify the migration plan, specifications,
and task definitions for their quality and completeness early in the run before
implementation starts."*

Expanded below into conditions the agents can execute against and the LRR script (R2) can
assert. Two refinements made explicit, because the literal form would fail its own intent:
**"all recommendations"** becomes *every recommendation is in exactly one of two states ?
verified-landed or explicitly-deferred* (some items are boundary work BY DESIGN; the only
forbidden state is silence). **"completely sure"** becomes *defined, measured, and bounded* ?
certainty about outcomes is not available to anyone; what is available is: known failure
classes provably closed, improvement numerically defined before the run, and a bounded worst
case. That is what "sure" can honestly mean, and it is stronger than confidence ? it is
falsifiable.

## SC-0 ? Supply chain (precondition of everything)
The improvement wave exists in git, the golden scaffold is published from it, and pod parity
is proven 3-way (repo == golden == v4 pod), including the new modules (`oracle_derive.py`,
`m3-all-lint.sh`). *Verified by:* LRR asserts fingerprints; Opus independently confirms
pod-side. [= R1; ADR-10 test-what-you-fly]

## SC-1 ? Recommendation disposition: two states, no third
Every open recommendation across this doc (R-A*, A-*, ARCH-*, LOG-*, W4-* P1/P2, readiness
R1?R9) is either:
  (a) **LANDED** ? with its instrument, and corpus-proven where a corpus exists (ADR-6), or
  (b) **DEFERRED** ? named in the committed change manifest's NOT-UNDER-TEST section with a
      one-line reason and its parking target (next boundary / predicate program / etc.).
*Verified by:* the manifest (R3) enumerates both lists; Opus sweeps the doc for any item in
neither (their reminder-duty machinery already tracks the population). Operator reads ONLY
the deferred list and vetoes any deferral they disagree with. [= R3/R8; ADR-10]

## SC-2 ? "Significant improvement" is defined, measured, and bounded BEFORE the run
  (a) **Defined:** the frozen prediction table is committed (hash in this doc) ? improvement
      IS its thresholds: time-to-first-plan-defect ?30min; reimplement-class ?4 seats
      (rename-class UNCHANGED ? the control); 0 statically-decidable defects reaching M4;
      plans 3/3 lint-clean; M3 revisions ?3; S03-equivalent ships.
  (b) **Measured:** the run emits METRIC lines as rows resolve (LOG-5), so the score is read
      from the primary window, not reconstructed.
  (c) **Bounded:** tripwires stop a non-improving run inside its first story ? M3 revisions
      >1 reopens plan review; any READ_THRASH triggers packet+plan audit before redispatch;
      seats-per-task at 2? the kind-prediction ? HOLD (O-SEATBUDGET / O-STORYKIND ?
      incidents). Worst case is one story's budget, never 15 hours.
  (d) **Closed classes stay closed:** every v3 failure class with a corpus case cannot recur
      silently (plan corpus 11 cases; execution corpus per R4 ? or its absence is an SC-1
      deferral the operator has seen).

**(D) nothing to grade.** Instruments **502/502** stable (`6d8e236c92b7` both sides). Three checklist items moved. One new P1 that **currently prevents any wave start**.

### [W4-126a] P1 ? `O-ENVNOCLOBBER` broke `load_env` on the host; the entire gate layer is dead

```
bash scripts/track-b/v9-preflight-outer-start.sh   ?  PREFLIGHT_RC=1
  ? O-EXECCORPUS PASS (2 case(s))
  ? O-EXECCORPUS gate GREEN
  scripts/lib.sh: line 18: _preserves[@]: unbound variable      ? dies here
bash scripts/track-b/v10-hermes-parity.sh          ?  rc=1, ZERO bytes of output
```

The `O-ENVNOCLOBBER` fix (W4-121a, `lib.sh` mtime 09:01Z) declares `local _preserves=()` and expands `"${_preserves[@]}"`. Under `set -u` on **bash 3.2** an empty array expansion is an unbound-variable error:

```
host: GNU bash 3.2.57(1)-release (arm64-apple-darwin25)      ? macOS default, where the gates run
pod:  GNU bash 5.1.8(1)-release (x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu)    ? unaffected
```

**Blast radius: 17 scripts call `load_env`** ? including `v9-preflight-outer-start.sh`, `v10-hermes-parity.sh`, `v10-prep-fresh-rerun.sh`, `v10-golden-fresh.sh`, `v10-idle-clock.sh`, `v9-ship-only.sh`. The preflight runs all the way through `O-EXECCORPUS gate GREEN` and then dies, so the failure is **late and easy to misread as success** if only the early output is watched. The parity gate fails with *no output at all* ? which is how I found it: it had printed `MISSING_KEY:?` two polls ago and now prints nothing.

The harness inside the pod is unaffected (bash 5.1), so this is purely the **host gate layer** ? but that is the layer that decides whether a wave may start.

**Fix:** bash-3.2-safe empty-array expansion ? `"${_preserves[@]+"${_preserves[@]}"}"`, or guard with `[ ${#_preserves[@]} -gt 0 ]`.
**Repro:** `bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; source scripts/lib.sh; load_env; echo SURVIVED'`
**Closes when:** `bash scripts/track-b/v9-preflight-outer-start.sh` reaches `PREFLIGHT GREEN`, and `v10-hermes-parity.sh` produces output again.

This is worth saying plainly: the fix was correct in design ? `load_env` was the right altitude, and per-script workarounds were the wrong one. The regression is a portability detail, not a reversal of the architecture. But it demonstrates the **production-invocation instrument policy** I filed at Assessment II ?2: `O-ENVNOCLOBBER` has no instrument that runs a real gate end-to-end on the host, so a change to shared library code took out seventeen callers silently.

### [W4-127a] P2 ? the parity digest is over-inclusive and will false-RED indefinitely

Now that parity actually compares, it refuses on a **real digest mismatch** ? but every differing file is non-semantic. I enumerated all 250 files on both sides:

```
golden 250 files ? pod 250 files ? 4 differ:
  .hermes/harness/.published-fp
  .hermes/harness/defaults-inventory.md          ? :113  _Generated: 2026-08-03T09:26:20Z_
  .hermes/harness/guard-manifest.md              ? :149  _Generated: 2026-08-03T09:26:43Z_
  .hermes/harness/tests/fixtures/plan-corpus/manifest.env   ? diff is ONE trailing blank line (113d112)
```

- **Two are generated artifacts that embed a generation timestamp.** Any regeneration on either side makes parity RED forever after, with no semantic change. `defaults-inventory.sh` and `guard-manifest.sh` both stamp `_Generated: <ts>_`.
- **One is a publish stamp that another tool explicitly excludes** ? `.published-fp` says of itself: *"Compare with live tree digest (stamp file excluded from hash)"*. `v10-golden-fresh.sh` excludes it; `v10-hermes-parity.sh`'s `find` excludes only `__pycache__`, `*.pyc`, `.DS_Store`. **Two hashing schemes over the same tree, disagreeing on what counts.**
- **One is a blank line.**

**Why this matters more than it looks.** `O-HERMESPREFLIGHT` must be GREEN before every wave start (R1/R2). As built it can only be GREEN if both sides are byte-synced *after* the last regeneration of any stamped artifact ? which no workflow guarantees. A gate that cannot practically go green is the gate that gets bypassed, and the bypass here is `V9_SKIP_HERMES_PARITY=1`, which disables the only real staleness check. This is the fail-open pattern arriving by the back door.

**Fix:** exclude derived/stamped artifacts from the parity digest (`.published-fp`, `defaults-inventory.md`, `guard-manifest.md`) ? they are generated from code that *is* hashed, so coverage is not lost ? or strip `_Generated:` lines before hashing, or drop the timestamps. Align the exclusion list with `v10-golden-fresh.sh` so one definition governs both.
**Repro:** `bash scripts/track-b/v10-hermes-parity.sh; ` then compare per-file md5 across the two trees.
**GROK: R1 cannot close until this is resolved ? the mismatch it currently reports is not staleness.**

*Failure meaning:* whole-set lint RED is the system WORKING (defects caught pre-seat ? record

manual plan read finds a defect the gates missed ? a false-GREEN gate, worse than any RED,

# M2 FAILURE ANALYSIS ? next boundary ? 2026-08-03T11:00Z ? why M2 fails, and the one fix that removes most of it ? review agent (Opus, read-only)

Operator question: what would stop us failing at M2 next time. Answered from the two waves' lint output,
not from opinion. **Nothing here is to be actioned mid-flight** ? the harness is frozen under the change
manifest until this wave ends.

## The failure classes repeat across waves

```
v4 attempt 1 (10:53Z)   13 coverage  (2 dual-owner ? 8 orphan mandatory ? 3 recipe-executed claimed)
                         5 briefs    (S02?S06 missing)

v3 (archived trail)      coverage    orphans ?11, recipe-executed wrongly owned by S01/S02
                         briefs      S05/S06 missing
                         deploy      last story S06 must deploy
                         non-mandatory  K3 adopt/defer absent ?3
                         fabrication invented methods/annotations in S03/S04/S06 briefs
```

Same classes, both waves. And the v3 trail records the death mode: *"`repeated_exact_failure_block`
after **5** identical terminal retries; residual only `LINT:non-mandatory` ?3 ? seat stopped changing
strategy."* The model did not fail to *understand* the lint; it failed to converge on bookkeeping.

## The diagnosis: M2 never got the fix M3 got

Sort the classes by what they actually require:

| Class | Judgment or bookkeeping? | Computable from what M1 already produced? |
|---|---|---|
| `coverage` dual-owner / orphan | **bookkeeping** | yes ? `findings-inventory.md` lists every mandatory rule |
| `coverage` recipe-executed claimed | **bookkeeping** | yes ? inventory already classifies `recipe` |
| `briefs` missing file | **bookkeeping** | yes ? one brief per story in the roadmap |
| `deploy` last story | **bookkeeping** | yes ? one boolean |
| `non-mandatory` K3 absent | **bookkeeping** (the *decision* is judgment; the *table* is not) | yes ? the non-mandatory set is enumerable |
| `fabrication` invented code | **judgment** | no ? correctly a gate |
| `substance` ceremonial scope | **judgment** | no ? correctly a gate |

**Five of seven classes are bookkeeping over data M1 already computed**, and they are what kills the run.
`findings-inventory.py` header states it outright: *"class from the MAPPINGS rule-join table (recipe /
rewrite / infer / OPEN DESIGN), decided target, incident sites"* ? the partition inputs exist before M2
starts. The model is being asked to re-derive by hand, in prose, a partition the harness already holds.

That is precisely the problem `m3-all-compose.py` solved for M3 ? *"task IDs from roadmap scope
partition; Owns filled from scope (K1 seeds); Class/Shape/Port/Oracle/Assumes field lines always
present"* ? and confirmed at W4-123: a field that is always present cannot be omitted. **M2 has no
equivalent.** `ls .hermes/harness/m2-*.py` ? nothing.

## Recommendation 1 (primary) ? `m2-compose.py`, skeleton-first for M2

Symmetric with `m3-all-compose.py`, deterministic pass after M1 PROFILE, before the M2 seat:

- **Partition mandatory findings** across the story skeleton from `findings-inventory.md` +
  `dependency-order.md` ? each mandatory rule assigned exactly once; `recipe`-classified rules excluded
  by construction. Kills dual-owner, orphan, and recipe-executed-claimed **at the source**.
- **Emit one brief stub per story** with the required `BRIEF_SECTIONS` headings present and empty.
  Kills `LINT:briefs`.
- **Emit the Non-mandatory decisions table** pre-listing every non-mandatory rule with blank
  adopt/defer. Kills `LINT:non-mandatory` (the model still supplies the *decision* and reason).
- **Set `deploy: true` on the last story.** Kills `LINT:deploy`.
- **Leave to the model**: story boundaries and rationale, REDESIGN target contracts from profile ?7,
  the real legacy quotes, `kind`, seat-budget, and the adopt/defer decisions themselves.

Residual lint surface becomes `fabrication` + `substance` + the A1/A3/A5 gates ? all genuine judgment,
which is what a gate should test. This is the same move as everywhere else this wave: **the information
already exists; it is being asked for in the wrong place.**

## Recommendation 2 ? the retry prompt references the lint instead of carrying it

`outer-loop.sh:644` (attempt 2): *"the findings are in `/tmp/roadmap-lint.txt` (**read it with your file
tools**)"*. The model must choose to read the file. v3's death mode ? five identical failing calls ?
is consistent with a seat retrying without re-reading. **Inline the actual lint output into the retry
prompt** (it is ~18 lines here, bounded). Cheap, and removes a whole failure mode.

Worth noting what is already good: that same prompt now teaches each class explicitly, including the
new ones (`LINT:O-PORTDERIVE`, `LINT:O-STORYKIND`, `LINT:O-SEATBUDGET` with `kind?incidents`). The
*teaching* is right; only the *delivery* is by reference.

## Recommendation 3 ? the attempt budget is inverted

```
M2 SEQUENCE   2 attempts ? fail_run "M2 SEQUENCE failed its lint twice"   (kills the run)
M3 SPECIFY    M3_WORKER_ATTEMPTS=2 + M3_ORCH_BACKSTOP=2  ? up to 4
```

The **global** artefact ? the one whose failure ends the wave before anything else is exercised ? has
half the budget of the per-story one, and no backstop actor. M3's pattern (worker attempts, then a
different actor as backstop) is the right shape. But note the ordering: **with Recommendation 1 the
budget question largely dissolves**, because the bookkeeping classes stop consuming attempts. More
attempts alone would not have saved v3 ? it had five and looped.

## What this predicts for the current wave

If attempt 2 clears coverage + briefs, M2 commits and we learn whether the A1/A3/A5 gates fire (W4-138a).
If it REDs, the run dies at v3's exact failure point ? and the above is the fix list, in that order.
Either outcome is informative; only the second is expensive.

**GROK: next boundary, not now.** **ARCHITECT: Recommendation 1 is the M2 counterpart of ADR-8's
skeleton-first decision ? worth an ADR of its own if you agree the asymmetry is unintended.**

### [W4-146a] P2 ? the NOT-spent retry has no cap; a quota outage becomes a silent livelock

```
outer-loop.sh:638  M2_429_BACKOFF_SECS="${M2_429_BACKOFF_SECS:-900}"
              726  log "O-M2-429: MiniMax rate-limited ? attempt ${ATTEMPT} NOT spent; backoff ..."
              727  phase_retry "M2 SEQUENCE ? quota; sleeping ..."
              728  sleep "${M2_429_BACKOFF_SECS}"
```

**No counter, no maximum.** If the endpoint stays rate-limited the loop is `seat ? 429 ? sleep 900s ? seat ? 429 ? ?` forever: the run never fails, never progresses, and never alerts. The same unbounded shape exists at M3 ? `outer-loop.sh:979` `O-M3QUOTA: MiniMax rate-limited ? NOT spent; backoff 15m` ? so this generalises beyond M2.

**Why this is worth raising while the fix is working.** `O-M2-429` correctly converts *"burn an attempt on a platform fault"* into *"don't burn it"*. Uncapped, it also converts a **fast, loud failure into an indefinite quiet one** ? and for an operator that is a worse failure mode, because `fail_run` writes `/tmp/outer-loop-done` and stops, whereas this emits reassuring heartbeats and backoff messages indefinitely. My own idle check would eventually classify it (fingerprints flat + outer-loop UP + nothing advancing = classification (b), possible stall), so the **review layer** would catch it ? but the harness would not, and that is the wrong place for the safety net.

**Current state is not yet pathological:** 2 events, ~45 min elapsed, budget intact. I am flagging the *absence of a bound*, not the observed behaviour.

**Recommended shape (next boundary, not mid-flight):** cap NOT-spent retries (3 is plausible against a 15-minute backoff ? 45 min of tolerance), then exit with a **distinct cause** ? `outer-failed: quota exhausted` must not be recorded as `M2 SEQUENCE failed its lint twice`. That distinction is attribution: *a wave that dies on quota is not a wave that dies on plan quality*, and the change manifest cannot tell them apart if the harness does not.

**GROK: next boundary.** **ARCHITECT: this is the ADR-5 override principle meeting its own limit ? a platform fault should not spend an attempt, but it also cannot be unbounded; the cap is where "not spent" stops being free.**

2. **Stop now and restart when quota is known-good.** Clean, costs nothing already earned ? `m2-compose` writes are on the pod working tree and the roadmap survives. The archive is written on EXIT.
3. **Stop and land the W4-146a cap first** (3 NOT-spent retries ? `fail_run` with cause `quota exhausted`, distinct from `failed its lint twice`). Costs one small harness change; converts this class of event from silent to loud, permanently.

**My recommendation: 3, then 2** ? the cap is small, it is the fix this wave has now evidenced twice over, and restarting into a capped harness means the next quota outage announces itself in 45 minutes instead of never. **But if quota is expected to recover shortly, option 1 costs nothing and the roadmap is 5 lints from green.** That is the operator's call, not mine.

## Step 1 ? the cap (GROK)

**Site A ? M2, `outer-loop.sh` ~723-730** (current shape, verbatim):
```bash
# O-M2-429: hermes_rc=0 after rate-limit is NOT seat success ? do not burn attempt
if grep -qE "429|Too Many Requests|Rate limit|rate.?limit" \
    "/tmp/outer-m2-sequence-a${ATTEMPT}.log" 2>/dev/null; then
  log "         O-M2-429: MiniMax rate-limited ? attempt ${ATTEMPT} NOT spent; backoff ${M2_429_BACKOFF_SECS}s"
  phase_retry "M2 SEQUENCE ? quota; sleeping ${M2_429_BACKOFF_SECS}s (O-M2-429)"
```

**Site B ? M3, `outer-loop.sh` ~978-982**, identical shape with a hardcoded `sleep 900`:
```bash
if grep -qE "429|..." "/tmp/outer-m3-${SID}-${seat_tag}.log" 2>/dev/null; then
  log "         O-M3QUOTA: MiniMax rate-limited ? NOT spent; backoff 15m"
  phase_retry "M3 SPECIFY ${SID} ? quota; sleeping 900s"
  sleep 900
  continue
fi
```

**Required behaviour:**
1. A counter incremented in the 429 branch, capped by `M2_429_MAX="${M2_429_MAX:-3}"` (M3 sibling likewise).
2. On exceeding the cap: `fail_run` with a **distinct cause** ? e.g. `quota exhausted after N rate-limited seats (O-M2-429CAP)`. It **must not** be recorded as `M2 SEQUENCE failed its lint twice`; that conflation is what would make wave 2 read like wave 1 in the manifest when the two are nothing alike.
3. **Reset the counter on any seat that completes without a 429.** Without this, unrelated rate-limits accumulated across a long run would eventually fail a healthy wave ? a cap that mis-fires is worse than none.
4. Lift M3's hardcoded `900` into a variable alongside `M2_429_BACKOFF_SECS`, for symmetry and testability.
5. One instrument: cap reached ? `fail_run` fires with the distinct cause; and a non-429 seat resets the counter.

3 ? 900s ? **45 minutes of tolerance** before the run declares quota exhaustion ? enough to ride out a transient window, short enough to alert rather than hang.

### [W4-151a] P2 ? the skeleton's own output fails bookkeeping lints it should have satisfied

Post-skeleton residual, by class:

```
6 ? LINT:briefs         "brief has no code excerpt (In scope must quote legacy lines)"   ? JUDGMENT ?
5 ? LINT:O-STORYKIND    "missing field 'kind'"                                            ? DERIVABLE ?
3 ? LINT:non-mandatory  K3 adopt/defer absent                                             ? mixed
2 ? LINT:stories        "S04/S05: findings '-' is only for HARVEST stories"               ? BOOKKEEPING ?
```

**The 6 brief lints are correct and expected** ? the skeleton writes stubs with the required headings and the model must supply real legacy quotes. That is exactly the judgment/bookkeeping line working.

**The other two classes are not:**

- **`S-FND` ?2** ? the skeleton assigned bare `findings: '-'` to S04 and S05, which the lint permits only for HARVEST/characterization stories. **Compose's own deterministic output violates a deterministic lint.** It has the inventory; it can assign findings or mark the story HARVEST, and it should never emit a value its sibling checker rejects.
- **`O-STORYKIND` ?5** ? `m2-compose` deliberately leaves `kind` to the model (*"Leave judgment to the model: ? kind ?"*). But `roadmap-lint` **derives** whether `kind` is required by checking OPEN DESIGN ownership and ?7 REDESIGN scope ? it computes the precondition in order to demand the field. That is the identical pattern to `seat-budget: N != expected N`, which compose *does* now compute. **If the checker can determine that a story needs `kind`, compose can determine which `kind` it needs** ? `reimplement` for OPEN-DESIGN-owning stories, `rename` otherwise, `mixed` only where both, with the model refining and justifying rather than originating.

Doing both would take the residual from 16 to **9**, leaving only genuine judgment: 6 brief excerpts + 3 K3 decisions. **GROK: next boundary, not mid-flight.** **ARCHITECT: this is ADR-4 (derived-not-declared) applied to compose's own output ? the rule that a generator must not emit what its checker rejects.**

Operator asks whether outer-loop logging needs updating for the latest changes. **Yes ? three gaps,
all specific to `O-M2COMPOSE` / `O-M2429CAP`, judged against wave 3's actual log rather than in the
abstract.** Next boundary, not mid-flight.

## What already works and must not be regressed

The wave-3 log narrates the new machinery better than wave 1 did: compose gets its own `> START` /
`OK GATE` pair, the 429 path prints `(1/3)` so the countdown is visible rather than an unbounded run of
identical lines, and `session ? gate` is still stated explicitly at every seat end. The glyph column,
the models line, and per-seat `Actor:` attribution all survive.

## [LOG-1] P2 ? `O-M2COMPOSE` prints debug output, not information

```
[12:45:27]   O-M2COMPOSE skeleton: O-M2COMPOSE: done mode=skeleton roadmap_written=True briefs_wrote=6 briefs_refreshed=0
[12:45:27] OK GATE   M2 SEQUENCE compose ? GREEN ? O-M2COMPOSE: done mode=skeleton roadmap_written=True briefs_wrote=6 ?
```

Three problems in one line: the token is **duplicated** (`O-M2COMPOSE skeleton: O-M2COMPOSE:`), `roadmap_written=True` is a raw Python boolean, and the whole string is echoed **twice** ? once as narration, once inside the GATE line. Nothing here tells a demo user what compose actually did.

**What it should say** ? every number is already computed inside `m2-compose.py`:

```
O-M2COMPOSE  skeleton ? partitioned 47 mandatory findings across 6 stories ? 6 brief stubs written
             deploy on S06 ? K3 table seeded (3 rules) ? 0 recipe-executed claims
```

That is the difference between *"the tool ran"* and *"the tool did the bookkeeping so the model doesn't have to"* ? which is the whole point of the change and currently invisible.

## [LOG-2] P1 ? the lint residual is never narrated, and it is the number that shows progress

This is the significant one. The gate prints RED or GREEN but **never how far from green**. In wave 2 the residual fell **15 ? 12 ? 5** across three compose fill passes ? the single most important result of that wave ? and **none of it appeared in the log**. I found it only by reading `/tmp/roadmap-lint.txt` directly. A demo user watching wave 2 saw three identical 429 cycles and would reasonably conclude nothing was happening, while the harness was measurably converging.

**Add residual to every gate and every compose line:**

```
O-M2COMPOSE  fill ? roadmap repaired ? lint 16 ? 9  (?5 O-STORYKIND, ?2 S-FND)
X GATE   M2 SEQUENCE roadmap-lint ? RED ? 9 findings (6 briefs ? 3 non-mandatory) ? /tmp/roadmap-lint.txt
OK GATE  M2 SEQUENCE roadmap-lint ? GREEN ? 0 findings; commit abc1234
```

One integer per line turns an opaque retry loop into a visible convergence. It also makes the derivation-first thesis legible in the demo: *the machine-derived classes go to zero and stay there; the judgment classes are what the model is being paid to do.*

## [LOG-3] P3 ? quota waits have no human units and no running total

```
R RETRY  M2 SEQUENCE ? quota; sleeping 900s (O-M2-429 1/3)
```

`900s` rather than `15m`, and nothing accumulates. Wave 2 spent **45 minutes of its 53** asleep and the log never said so. Suggested:

```
R RETRY  M2 SEQUENCE ? MiniMax quota; sleeping 15m (429 1/3 ? 15m waited so far ? run 22m)
```

Cheap, and it directly answers the demo user's actual question ? *"is it stuck or is it waiting?"*

## Also visible in this log, pre-existing

- **Raw sub-script stdout breaks the column**: `WARN: kept existing acceptance.path?`, `contract-stamp: already current (no-op)`, `O-STAMP-GATE: OK` are emitted outside `log()`, so they carry no timestamp and no glyph. Route them through `log()`.
- **`O-LOGPROG` / `O-LOGRUN` remain unlanded** (banked ?? since W4-115). LOG-3's run-elapsed suggestion is a subset of `O-LOGRUN`; landing that guard would cover it properly.

## Priority

**LOG-2 first** ? it is one integer, it makes the wave's actual behaviour visible, and it would have changed what an observer concluded about wave 2. LOG-1 next (cosmetic but it is the headline line for the new feature). LOG-3 and the stdout routing with `O-LOGRUN` at the next logging pass.

Zero orphans, zero ghosts, zero double-claims. This is exactly what `roadmap-lint`'s coverage check exists to enforce, and it is the class of failure that killed M2 at 13:34:50 on the previous attempt. Repro:

### P1 ? 23 build-generated files imported into story scope; the tasks derived from them cannot commit

Of 111 scope paths across the six stories, **23 are under `target/`**:

```
story  files  gen  findings         kind  seats  depends
S01        6    0        23        mixed     30        -
S02       28   16         1       rename      3      S01
S03       40    0         2  reimplement     25      S02
S04        5    0         3  reimplement      5      S03
S05       14    0         0  reimplement      5      S04
S06       18    7         2  reimplement      5      S05
TOTAL    111   23
```

S02 carries 16 OpenAPI-generated DTOs (`target/generated-sources/openapi/.../OwnerDto.java` ?), S06 carries 7 MapStruct-generated impls (`target/generated-sources/annotations/.../OwnerMapperImpl.java` ?). Three independent facts make these unworkable:

```
.gitignore:2  target/                          # gitignored
tracked_under_target = 0                       # nothing under target/ is tracked
staging_dto_any = 0   staging_mapperimpl = 0   # M1 staging excluded them
legacy_java_all=125  legacy_java_src=101  legacy_java_target=23
staging_java=101     staging_under_target=0
```

M1's harvest was right: it staged the 101 `src/` files and deliberately excluded the 23 generated ones. M2 then pulled those same 23 back in. The resulting task is self-contradictory ? here is T-014 as authored:

```
#### T-014: OwnerDto ? harvest from staging
**Shape**: create
**Owns**: `target/generated-sources/openapi/src/main/java/com/demo/dto/OwnerDto.java`
**Oracle**: absent
**Goal**: Harvest OwnerDto from staging with package rename and Jakarta EE migration
```

It instructs the worker to harvest from a staging directory containing no DTOs, into a path git will not track. Both halves are impossible. The two available outcomes are the ones the per-task review exists to catch: the worker **fabricates** the class from nothing (fabricated-stub), or it writes to `target/` and `git add -A` sweeps nothing (**empty/ceremonial commit**). Neither is detectable from a GREEN sensor.

That is 16 of S02's 32 tasks and 7 of S06's 18 ? **23 tasks, 40% of the two stories' task counts**, pre-destined to produce no reviewable code.

Repro:
```
grep -c "^target/" <(grep -oE '[^ ,]+\.java' migration/roadmap.md)   # 23
find migration/staging -name "*Dto.java" | wc -l                      # 0
git check-ignore -v target/generated-sources/openapi/x.java           # .gitignore:2
```

**Root cause and fix location.** The partition draws story scope from `findings-inventory.md` incident *site paths*, and kantra legitimately scanned `target/` ? `javax-to-jakarta-import-00001` lists `target/generated-sources/annotations/.../OwnerMapperImpl.java: line 6` as a site. So the inventory is correct and the partition is faithfully consuming it; what is missing is a filter. The scope builder in `m2-compose.py` should exclude any path that is (a) git-ignored in the destination, or (b) absent from `migration/staging/`. Staging-presence is the stronger test and needs no git call: M1 already made exactly this judgment, and scope should inherit it rather than re-derive it. Suggested token `O-M2GENSCOPE`, with a matching `roadmap-lint` assertion so a regenerated roadmap cannot reintroduce them.

### P1 ? seat budgets are inverted relative to actual work, and the overrun check is enforced

`expected_budget = RATES[kind] ? ceil(incidents/10)`, `RATES = {rename:1, reimplement:5, mixed:5}` ? a function of the *incident count of assigned findings*, with no term for scope size or task count. The result inverts:

| story | scope files | tasks authored | seat-budget | debt-freeze at (?2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | 6 | **4** | **30** | 60 |
| S02 | 28 | **32** | **3** | 6 |

S01 gets 30 seats for 4 tasks; S02 gets 3 seats for 32 tasks. This is not advisory ? `supervisor.sh:1512 check_seat_budget_overrun()` runs `seat-budget.py check-overrun` and on failure escalates:

```
log "$tag: O-SEATBUDGET OVERRUN ? actual seats exceed budget?factor for ${sid} ? escalating (debt-freeze)"
record_debt "$tag" "seat-budget" "O-SEATBUDGET: actual OpenCode seats exceed kind?incidents budget?factor"
```

With `SEAT_BUDGET_OVER_FACTOR=2`, **S02 debt-freezes after 6 seats with 26 of its 32 tasks unstarted.** Even after the P1 above removes the 16 impossible DTO tasks, 16 real entity-harvest tasks remain against a 6-seat ceiling.

The inversion is structural: S02 has 28 files but only one assigned finding (`removed-javaee-modules-00020`), because the javax?jakarta work was recipe-resolved and correctly excluded from story ownership. So the entire domain layer scores as near-zero work by an incident-count metric. S01 inverts the other way ? 23 findings of which **18 are on the K6 pre-satisfied list**, so its budget is computed from work the scaffold already did.

Fix direction (Grok's call): make `expected_budget` a function of the work actually planned rather than incidents alone ? e.g. `max(incident-derived, ceil(scope_files_not_presatisfied / k))`, or recompute the budget after M3 authors the task list, when the true task count is known. The second is more honest and has a natural home: M3-ALL already runs a whole-set pass, which is the point at which task counts first exist.

### P2 ? S01's findings list is 78% pre-satisfied, so its scope reads far larger than its work

18 of S01's 23 assigned findings appear in `scaffold-presatisfied.generated.txt` (K6: "legacy rules absent from pristine dest-baseline with landed/config evidence") ? including every `javaee-pom-to-quarkus-*`, `springboot-parent-pom`, `springboot-plugins`, and all four `springboot-properties-*`. S01's authored plan handles this correctly, opening with an `O-PLANEXISTS-dead` block listing BOM conversion, extensions, plugin config and core properties as already satisfied, and reducing to 4 real tasks. So the *plan* is right and the *roadmap* overstates.

The cost is that the roadmap's findings list is not a work list, while `seat-budget` and any human reading it treat it as one. Worth making the pre-satisfied subtraction visible in the roadmap row (e.g. `findings: 23 (18 pre-satisfied, 5 actionable)`) so the two artifacts agree.

Note a semantic tension to resolve rather than a defect: `springboot-properties-to-quarkus-00000..3` are listed pre-satisfied, yet S01 T-002/T-003 legitimately create `application-{hsqldb,mysql,postgresql}.properties` (`Oracle: absent` ? they genuinely do not exist). K6 "absent from pristine dest-baseline" means the rule does not *fire* against the scaffold; it does not mean the functionality is present. Both statements are true here, but the vocabulary invites a reader to conclude the work is done.

### P2 ? S05 owns zero findings while carrying the largest behavioural rewrite

S05 is 14 files ? all ten REST controllers, `ExceptionControllerAdvice`, `BindingErrorsResponse`, and the security config ? converted from Spring MVC to JAX-RS with problem-detail error mapping. `findings: -`. The rationale explains why (`findings owned by layer-aligned stories (O-M2COMPOSEBOOK S-FND)`), and the partition is not wrong to avoid dual-ownership. But the consequences are real: K1 incident-ownership has nothing to anchor S05's tasks to, its seat-budget is computed from zero incidents (`reimplement ? 1 unit = 5`), and the M5 findings-delta will report **0 resolved for the story that changes the most behaviour**. `O-DELTABASE` will read as a no-op story. S05 needs a non-incident completion oracle ? the `migration.yaml` 400/404/503 error contract named in its `done:` line is the obvious candidate, but nothing currently binds it.

### P3 ? two lesser scope observations

**Strictly linear dependency chain.** Every story depends on its predecessor, including S06 (mappers, `EntityUtils`, aspect removal) on S05 (REST surface), where no real dependency exists. Safe, but it serialises the whole wave and makes any single stuck story a total stall ? the amplifier behind the wave-1 and wave-2 failures. Some of these could run in parallel once M4 is stable.

**`.mvn/wrapper/MavenWrapperDownloader.java` is in S06 scope** and appears as `T-001` there. It is Maven wrapper bootstrap tooling, not application code, and is neither in staging nor part of the target application. Same filter as the P1 would catch it if the rule is "must exist in `migration/staging/`".

### Bottom line

M2 executed as expected on everything the gate was designed to check, and the sequencing judgment is sound ? the story boundaries, ordering, kinds and K3 decisions are all defensible and would survive an architect's review. The two P1s are both scope-derivation defects that the lint does not currently assert on, and both are cheap to fix deterministically: filter scope by staging-presence, and make the seat budget a function of planned work. Fixing them before M4 starts matters more than usual, because their failure mode is not a red gate ? it is 23 green-looking commits containing nothing.

**Recommend these land before the PAUSE-3 operator gate**, since the plans the operator will read at that gate currently contain 23 tasks that cannot succeed.

## Architect ruling on the M2 assessment ? 2026-08-03T14:20Z ? both P1s confirmed; freeze-exception GRANTED with conditions ? Claude (solution architect)

Opus's M2 verdict endorsed in full ? and the verification method (33/33 rules cross-checked
three ways; `kind-updates=0` as PROOF the skeleton derived rather than the model
re-arithmeticking) is the standard the triangle should hold everywhere.

### The architecture reading of the two P1s

**P1-scope (23 target/ files) is a derivation-inheritance defect, and it names a principle:**
two derivers made the SAME judgment independently ? M1's staging exclusion got it right, M2's
scope builder re-derived it from raw incident sites and got it wrong. Rule going into the
register: **a judgment derived once is inherited by every downstream deriver, never
re-derived from rawer inputs** (ADR-4 corollary; the god-node/brief-constraint lesson in a
new coat). Fix shape: the scope builder filters incident sites through M1's own exclusion
predicate ? or draws scope from staging membership, which embodies it.

**P1-budget is a wrong-multiplicand defect with a structural insight:** incidents measure
*findings pressure*, not *work volume*, and the two diverge exactly where recipes already
resolved the findings (S02: 28 files, 1 finding, 3 seats, freeze at 6). Fix shape: budgets
finalize at M3-ALL when task counts exist (`kind-rate ? tasks`), with M2's number explicitly
provisional; the supervisor enforces the M3-ALL-refined figure. This also fits the pipeline's
own logic ? the budget becomes final at the same gate where the work becomes enumerable.

### Freeze ruling (the decision both P1s force)

The zero-change-budget rule meets its own exception test here: the manifest's NOT-UNDER-TEST
criterion was "does deferral affect whether the wave's result is measurable and
attributable?" ? and BOTH P1s flunk deferral by that exact test. 23 known-impossible tasks
reaching PAUSE-3 would have the operator approving plans we know cannot succeed (the gate
becomes theater); S02 debt-freezing at 6 seats on a formula bug kills the experiment's
central measurement on a cause it isn't testing. **Exception GRANTED for both, with
conditions:** (1) recorded as a manifest amendment (the freeze bends through its own
recorded-override mechanism ? ADR-5 applied to process, never silently); (2) minimal diffs
per the fix shapes above; (3) full re-compose + whole-set re-lint after landing, before
PAUSE-3; (4) Opus independently verifies both fixes + the re-lint. GROK: proceed on that
basis.

### Two registrations

- **[V4-005] S05 zero-findings / largest-rewrite** ? live evidence for ADR-9: the
  findings-resolution spine cannot measure the wave's biggest story; M5's delta will report
  0 for it. Wave-verdict measurement caveat NOW (S05 is judged on behavioral/acceptance
  evidence, not delta %); unified Work Inventory remains the durable fix.
- S01's 78%-pre-satisfied roadmap overstatement corrected by O-PLANEXISTS-dead at plan level
  ? working as designed; no action.

# ADR-15 PROPOSAL ? the Work Model: one typed source of truth, documents as views, gates as invariants ? 2026-08-03T14:35Z ? Claude (solution architect)

The operator is right that P1-scope and P1-budget deserve more than patches. Line up this
week's findings and they are ONE defect with five faces:

| finding | face |
|---|---|
| P1-scope: 23 target/ files in scope | scope builder RE-DERIVED a judgment M1 already made (exclusion set) |
| P1-budget: incidents as multiplicand | budget derived from the wrong fact, with no lifecycle (provisional vs final) |
| V4-002: "publish seat-budget: 30" | a computed fact demanded back as hand-typed markdown |
| V4-003: M1 staleness | derived artifacts carry no provenance, so freshness is uncheckable |
| V4-005: S05 measures as zero | the only first-class work items are findings; everything else is prose |

**The disease: our pipeline has no data model.** Stages exchange MARKDOWN, and every stage
re-derives what it needs by parsing prose at whatever rawness it happens to reach. Every
compose script, every lint regex, every "verbatim token match" is a workaround for that
absence. The compose family fixed authoring by deriving-then-rendering; the durable solution
finishes the thought.

## The proposal

**One typed, versioned artifact ? `migration/work-model.json` ? is the single source of
truth. Documents become views of it. Gates become invariant checks over it.**

- **M1 writes**: findings (+ engine/ruleset fingerprint), classification, the exclusion set
  (staging membership judgment ? P1-scope's fix becomes a READ), dependency edges + god-node
  marks, ?7 roles, and the **work-item union** (findings ? preserve ? acceptance ? schema ?
  test-strategy ? deploy ? ADR-9 lands here as a schema, not a new mechanism).
- **M2 writes**: the story partition (work-item ? story, exactly-once BY CONSTRUCTION),
  derived kinds, budgets marked `provisional`.
- **M3-ALL writes**: tasks (task ? work-items), Port/Shape/Oracle/Assumes as fields, budgets
  finalized `kind-rate ? tasks` (P1-budget's fix becomes a lifecycle).
- **Renderings**: roadmap.md / briefs / tasks.md are generated views with explicit
  judgment-slots the model seats fill (compose already half-does this ? it becomes the rule).
- **Gates**: partition-exactly-once, scope ? non-excluded, budget==formula(model),
  later-class leakage (reachability), Assumes closure ? invariant queries over the model,
  plus ONE consistency check that markdown views match model facts. Whole regex families in
  the lints become obsolete rather than maintained.
- **Provenance**: every model section carries its input fingerprints (V4-003's freshness
  check is `stored_fp != computed_fp`, generically, for every stage ? not an M1 special).
- **M5 reports over item TYPES**: S05 stops measuring as zero because its acceptance/behavior
  items are first-class rows the delta counts.

## Why this is the durable form (cross-domain evidence, per my evidence duty)

This is the move every mature system in the same trap made: **compilers** parse source once
into a typed IR and forbid passes from re-reading text (our stages re-parsing markdown IS
the anti-pattern); **build systems** (Bazel-class) attach input fingerprints to every derived
artifact ? staleness and inheritance solved by content addressing, exactly V4-003/P1-scope;
**KAI itself** ? its inner loop works from the analyzer's typed incident model, never from
prose (P1 of the KAI comparison: "the work inventory is computed" ? this proposal is that
principle given a persistent home). And it is the declared subsumption TARGET the guard
program needs (OAQ-2): typed fields + invariants are where retired regex guards go.

## Phasing (no big-bang; each phase pays for itself)

1. **Boundary+1**: extract facts ALREADY computed into work-model.json (inventory join,
   exclusion set, kinds, partition, budgets); compose reads the model. ~3 scripts touched;
   P1-scope/P1-budget/V4-002/V4-003 all close structurally.
2. Lints re-anchor as model invariants + one markdown-consistency check.
3. Work-item union populated (ADR-9); M5 delta by item type (V4-005).
4. Predicate program (R-23) keys off model fields.

**Falsifier**: model/schema maintenance cost exceeds the re-derivation defect rate it
prevents, measured over two waves. **Register**: filed as ADR-15 PROPOSED; ADR-14 (compose
family) recorded ACCEPTED/UNDER-TEST ? ADR-15 is its completion, not its replacement.

GROK: no mid-wave action ? Phase 1 is boundary work; your two P1 fixes under the granted
exception are unaffected (they become Phase-1 reads later). OPUS: adversarial review of the
schema risk ? the failure mode I most want challenged is "the model becomes a second thing
to drift" (my answer: views are GENERATED and consistency-checked, so drift is a RED, not a
divergence ? but test that answer).

? Claude (solution architect)

## Architecture review ? the typed `work-model.json` proposal ? 2026-08-03T16:15:37Z

Asked to adversarially attack one failure mode ? *"the model becomes a second thing to drift"* ? with the architect's answer on record: *views are generated and consistency-checked, so drift is a RED, not a divergence.*

**Verdict: the diagnosis is right, the shape is right, and the stated answer to the drift objection is not yet sufficient ? for a reason this repo demonstrated today rather than in principle.**

### The diagnosis holds, and the 4-of-5 claim is honest

I checked the claim that Phase 1 structurally closes four of the five findings. It does, and the fifth is correctly excluded:

| finding | face | closed by a typed model? |
|---|---|---|
| 23 `target/` files in scope | exclusion set is data | **yes** ? if the exclusion set is a typed field, not a regex in one script |
| seat-budget inversion | budget needs a task-count term | **yes** ? budgets computed from model cardinality |
| M1 freshness uncheckable | provenance fingerprints | **yes** ? generically, per artifact |
| S05 measures as zero | M5 reports over item types | **yes** ? non-incident work items become countable |
| ceremonial acceptance / self-answered lint | **judgment quality** | **no** |

The fifth is the one I filed against S01 (`Acceptance: plan-lint green; sensors green` on 3 of 4 tasks) and it is not a data-model problem. A schema can require an `acceptance` field to be non-empty; it cannot tell that its content restates the gate. Worth stating plainly so the proposal is not oversold internally: **the typed model closes the mechanical faces of the disease and leaves the judgment faces exactly where they are.** That is still a very good trade ? four structural closures for one schema ? but the residual is precisely the class that costs seats at M4.

### The attack: typed does not mean true

The consistency check binds *model ? document*. Every defect I have filed this week was **model ? reality**:

- scope said `target/generated-sources/.../OwnerDto.java`; reality said gitignored, `tracked_under_target=0`, and `staging_dto_any=0`
- seat-budget said 3; reality said 32 tasks
- S05 said `findings: -`; reality said ten REST controllers

A typed `path: string` is wrong in exactly the same way the markdown string was wrong, and it is *more dangerous*, because prose invites suspicion and a schema invites trust. Nothing in "generated views + consistency check" catches any of the three above ? all three would serialise cleanly, validate against the schema, and produce a green consistency check.

So the invariant queries cannot be over the model alone. They have to be **joins against observed reality**: `every scope path ? staging_manifest`, `every Owns path ? gitignore`, `budget ? f(|tasks|)`. Which means the observations themselves ? staging manifest, `git ls-files`, dest baseline ? must be typed inputs in the model with the same provenance fingerprints as findings, re-validated at each stage boundary. If that is already the intent, say so explicitly, because "single source of truth" reads as *the model is authoritative* when what is actually needed is *the model is a checkable claim about a filesystem*.

### The empirical version of the drift objection ? it happened today

The strongest counter to *"drift is a RED, not a divergence"* is that **this repo already has a generated-view-of-a-model, and it silently lost data this morning with no RED.**

`guard-manifest.md` is generated by `guard-manifest.sh` from guards in the code. Regenerated at 16:07:02Z it went from **18 rows to 16**. `O-M2COMPOSEBOOK` and `O-LOGLINTRES` both vanished; both are still live in code with 3 references each; both are load-bearing in the wave running right now. No gate went red. The four-gate battery I ran at W4-170 ? instruments 517/517, gate-instruments 13/0, coolstore, bank ? all passed with the rows already gone.

The reason is precise and it generalises: **the consistency check compared what was present and never asserted completeness.** Agreement-on-what-exists is not the same invariant as nothing-was-lost. A generated view can drop a record and remain perfectly consistent with the subset of the model it still describes.

Applied to `work-model.json`, the analogous failure is a work item that exists in M1's union, is dropped by M2's partition generator, and never appears in any story ? and the markdown?model check passes, because every story shown does correspond to a model row. That is the wave-1 orphan-finding failure returning through the front door of the system built to prevent it. The mitigation is cheap and must be in Phase 1, not deferred: **cardinality and closure invariants** ? `|items in M2 partition| == |items in M1 union| ? |exclusions|`, each with a typed reason ? plus a monotonic row-count guard on every generated view. The guard-manifest drop is the free lesson; take it before the schema exists rather than after.

### Two smaller attacks

**"Exactly-once by construction" is only true if the partition is computed, not authored.** M2 is a MiniMax seat. If an LLM writes model rows, the fabrication surface moves from prose into JSON and gains false authority ? schema-valid is not evidence-backed. The claim holds only under a hard rule: *deterministic compose writes the model; the LLM fills judgment slots in the generated view, which merge back under schema validation and never create or delete rows.* This wave already demonstrates the rule works ? `m2-compose` produced a perfect partition (0 orphans, 0 ghosts, 0 dual-owners) precisely because it was computed. Make the rule explicit in the design, because "M2 writes the story partition" currently reads as the seat writing it.

**The precedent argument is strongest at M1 and weakest at M3.** Compilers, build systems and KAI's analyzer model all have total input coverage and mechanical semantics ? a very good fit for findings, exclusions, fingerprints and roles. None of them models *plans*, which is where judgment slots live and where the acceptance-quality defect sits. So the evidence supports Phase 1 strongly, Phase 2 well, and Phase 3 by extrapolation rather than precedent. That is not a reason to stop at Phase 2; it is a reason not to expect Phase 3 to retire regex families at the same rate, and to keep the plan-tier judgment lints rather than assuming subsumption.

### Timing ? the one operational objection

Do not cut this mid-wave. We are 2 of 6 stories into M3-ALL, S01 is GREEN, S02 is in flight at `O-M3QUOTA 2/3` ? one rate-limit from `fail_run`. A schema landing now leaves S01/S02 with no model rows, and the only ways out are a backfill parser (the thing being removed) or discarding two hard-won green plans. **Land at a wave boundary.** Grok's two P1 fixes under the granted exception should proceed now exactly as the architect says ? they are small, they are gated by the corpus, and they become Phase-1 reads later.

### What I would want to see in Phase 1 before endorsing

1. Reality-join invariants, not model-internal ones ? with the observations typed and fingerprinted.
2. Cardinality + closure invariants on every generated view, and a monotonic row-count guard. `guard-manifest.md` is the proof this is not hypothetical.
3. An explicit writer rule: deterministic compose owns rows; seats own judgment slots only.
4. A named list of which regex families Phase 1 actually retires ? and which the retirement is *asserted* to cover but has not been tested against the plan-corpus. OAQ-2 subsumption should be demonstrated per-guard against L2 corpora, not declared.

With those four, I think this is the right shape and I would back it. Without (2) in particular, the drift objection stands ? and it stands on today's evidence, not on principle.

# ADR-15 v2 ? Work Model design, restructured around the review ? 2026-08-03T16:45Z ? Claude (solution architect)

Not conditions bolted onto v1 ? a redesign with the review's insights as load-bearing walls.

## The ontology: three record kinds, three write authorities

```
OBSERVATIONS  ? facts HARVESTED from reality, never authored:
                staging manifest ? git ls-files ? gitignore effect ? kantra output ?
                dest baseline ? legacy tree fp ? engine/ruleset versions
                writer: harvest scripts only ? fingerprinted ? RE-HARVESTED at every
                stage boundary (staleness = fp mismatch = RED)
DERIVATIONS   ? facts COMPUTED from observations + upstream derivations:
                classification ? exclusion set ? dependency edges ? roles ? work-item
                union ? story partition ? kinds ? budgets ? task skeletons ?
                Port/Oracle/Shape
                writer: deterministic compose only ? each row cites its input fps ?
                lifecycle states where needed (budget: provisional@M2 ? final@M3-ALL)
JUDGMENTS     ? decisions AUTHORED by seats into schema-validated slots:
                adopt/defer + reason ? story boundaries + rationale ? target shapes ?
                legacy quotes ? acceptance content
                writer: LLM seats ? may FILL slots, never create/delete rows ?
                each judgment cites the derivation rows it decides about
```

The drift objection dies here structurally: a seat cannot lose a row (no delete authority);
compose cannot silently lose a row (conservation laws below); an observation cannot go stale
silently (re-harvest + fp compare is the stage-entry step).

## Conservation laws (the guard-manifest lesson, made first-class)

Every stage transformation declares its cardinality equation, checked at the gate:
`|M2 partition| == |M1 union| ? |exclusions|` (each exclusion a typed row WITH reason) ?
`|tasks' work-item refs| covers |story's items|` ? every generated VIEW carries an expected
row-count header and a monotonic guard (a regenerated view with fewer rows than its
predecessor is RED pending an explicit removal record). "Nothing-was-lost" is an invariant
CLASS, asserted everywhere, not a per-view afterthought.

## Invariants are reality-joins by type

Model-internal checks are only well-formedness. Every load-bearing invariant joins
derivations against observations: `scope ? staging_manifest`, `Owns ? gitignored = ?`,
`budget == rate(kind) ? |tasks|`, `Assumes ? (dest baseline ? earlier stories' declared
outputs)`, leakage = reachability over observed edges. The model is **a checkable claim
about a filesystem** ? its authority is exactly as good as its most recent harvest, by
construction.

## Versioning: the model is committed, per stage, append-preferring

Each stage's write is a commit (`M1 model:`, `M2 model:` ?); amendments are new versions
citing the guard that forced them ? the revision trail the corpus rescue had to reconstruct
by archaeology becomes a native artifact. Drift review = `git diff` on JSON, not prose
forensics.

## Honest scope + pre-mortem (what this does NOT fix, and how it could fail)

Does not fix: judgment quality (ceremonial acceptance, fabricated quotes ? fabrication lint
+ predicate program keep that jurisdiction) ? MiniMax quota ? anything at M4 execution.
Failure modes owned in advance: **compose becomes a single point of failure** (mitigated: its
output must satisfy the same conservation laws + corpus replay covers it ? a compose bug is
a RED, not a silent skew) ? **schema churn tax** (mitigated: three record kinds are stable;
fields grow additively; falsifier stands) ? **model bypass** ? a future script parsing
markdown again (residual risk, named: one grep-class check that no harness script reads
roadmap/tasks.md for facts the model carries; imperfect, admitted).

Phasing and boundary-only landing unchanged. Retirement of any regex family remains a
corpus-proven event per guard (condition 4). OPUS: v2 supersedes v1 for your conditional
backing ? please confirm the four conditions read as structural here, not appended.

? Claude (solution architect)

## M2 improvement program ? grounded in a measured defect ? 2026-08-03T16:32Z

### The diagnosis, in one line

**M2 *computes* the findings partition and *authors* the file scope.** The computed half is flawless; the authored half silently lost a fifth of the work.

Measured on this wave's GREEN roadmap (`a7f5c83`), scope union vs the M1 staging manifest:

```
staging java (src/):     100
roadmap java paths:      105   (src/: 81   target/: 24)
staging files in NO story:   20
scope src/ paths not in staging:  1
paths in >1 story:            0
```

**20 staging files are in no story at all**, and the M2 gate was green. The set is not random:

```
18 ? test classes  ? the entire suite:
   rest/{Owner,Pet,PetType,Specialty,User,Vet,Visit}RestControllerTests
   service/clinicService/{Abstract,Jdbc,Jpa,SpringDataJpa}?Tests + ApplicationTestConfig
   service/userService/{Abstract,Jdbc,Jpa,SpringDataJpa}?Tests
   model/ValidatorTests, SpringConfigTests
 2 ? main source   ? repository/springdatajpa/PetTypeRepositoryOverride.java
                     repository/springdatajpa/SpringDataPetTypeRepository.java
```

The two main-source misses are diagnostic. S03's scope lists `PetRepositoryOverride`, `SpecialtyRepositoryOverride`, `SpringDataPetRepository`, `SpringDataPetTypeRepositoryImpl` ? but not `PetTypeRepositoryOverride`, and not `SpringDataPetTypeRepository`. That is a hand-enumerated directory listing with two entries missed. No amount of prompt improvement makes an LLM reliably enumerate 40 paths; this is a class of error that only disappears when the list stops being authored.

**Why nothing caught it:** `roadmap-lint`'s `coverage` check is findings-only (`roadmap-lint.py:235/273/275` ? dual-owner, orphan, recipe-executed). There is no file-level assertion, and `migration/staging` is referenced nowhere in the M2 path except two comment strings. M2 never reads M1's work set.

**Second-order consequence, already visible.** `S-GODORDER` fired three times on S02 demanding characterization tests before the BaseEntity/NamedEntity/PetType harvests. Those tests can never be planned, because all 18 test classes are outside every story's scope. The harness is asking for work it structurally excluded.

### Fix 1 ? make scope a computed partition of the staging manifest (highest value by far)

M1 already produces the authoritative work set and already made the include/exclude judgment correctly (100 `src/` files staged, 0 under `target/`). M2 should **partition that set**, not re-derive a file list from incident site paths.

```
input:   migration/staging file list  ?  dependency-order.md layer assignment
output:  every staging path assigned to exactly one story, by layer/package
model:   writes rationale, kind justification, ?7 contracts, K3 reasons ? never paths
```

What this closes *by construction* rather than by check:
- the 23 `target/` phantom paths ? impossible, they are not in staging
- the 20 dropped files ? impossible, the partition is total
- dual ownership of a file ? impossible
- `O-SCOPENOGEN` becomes redundant: a whitelist subsumes the blacklist. **This matters ? `O-SCOPENOGEN` only catches `target/` and `build/`. A hallucinated or typo'd `src/` path still passes today.** A blacklist only ever catches the failure you already saw.

This also gives `O-SEATSIZE` an honest denominator: scope-path count becomes a real measure of work rather than a count of whatever the model happened to list.

### Fix 2 ? add the file-coverage lint anyway, as the safety net

Even with Fix 1, assert the invariant. It is a direct mirror of the findings-coverage check that has worked perfectly, roughly twenty lines alongside `roadmap-lint.py:235`:

```
every staging path ? exactly one story scope    ? orphan / dual-owner / phantom
every scope path   ? staging  (or a declared config allow-list)
```

Suggested token `O-SCOPECOVER`. Grade it RED, and make the message name the missing paths ? the diagnostic above took one query and would have failed this wave's M2 gate immediately instead of at hour four.

The one scope path absent from staging is `PetClinicApplication.java` (S06). That is probably M1 deliberately excluding a class slated for removal ? but "probably" is the problem. Under Fix 2 it needs a **typed exclusion reason**, not silence.

### Fix 3 ? tests need first-class treatment in the partition

18 of the 20 dropped files are tests, so any file-partition fix has to answer "which story owns a test?" Two workable rules:

1. **Ownership by subject** ? a test file goes to the story owning its class under test, derivable from the `?Tests` naming convention already used throughout. `OwnerRestControllerTests` ? S05 with `OwnerRestController`.
2. **A characterization story ordered first** ? all tests in one story before any conversion, which matches what `S-GODORDER` is asking for and gives the wave a behavioural baseline before anything moves.

(1) keeps the layer story coherent; (2) directly satisfies the god-node ordering rule. I lean to (1) with the S-GODORDER constraint enforced *within* a story, because a single test story would be enormous and would serialise the whole wave behind it ? but this is a real design choice and it is the architect's call, not mine.

Either way, **`S-GODORDER` must not stay in its current state**: a lint demanding artifacts the partition cannot produce is guaranteed lint-thrash, and lint-thrash under a 429 regime is what ended three waves.

### Fix 4 ? publish the pre-satisfied subtraction

S01 lists 23 findings; 18 are on the K6 pre-satisfied list; its plan correctly reduced to 4 tasks. The roadmap should say so:

```
- findings: 23 (5 actionable, 18 pre-satisfied by scaffold)
```

Costs nothing, makes the roadmap agree with the plan, and stops the budget and the human reviewer treating pre-satisfied work as work.

### Fix 5 ? every story needs a checkable completion oracle

S05 owns zero findings while rewriting all ten REST controllers, so M5's findings-delta will report zero resolved for the biggest behavioural change in the wave. Fix 1 partly solves this ? its 14 files become the anchor ? but the story still needs a *behavioural* oracle. Its `done:` line already names the right thing (the `migration.yaml` 400/404/503 error contract); that should be a typed assertion M5 evaluates, not prose.

Generalised: `done:` should be a list of checkable predicates. This is the M2 slice of the architect's typed-model program and it is worth doing in the same pass.

### Fix 6 ? recalibrate the seat brake (carried from W4-172)

`O-SEATSIZE` fixed the under-budget direction but S03 now budgets 100 with debt-freeze at 200. Fix 1 changes the inputs again (real file counts), so recalibrate *after* it lands, not before.

### Sequencing, and the honest cost

Fixes 2 and 4 are small and independent ? land them now. Fix 1 is the structural change and it rewrites how `m2-compose` seeds scope; it needs the plan-corpus and m2-corpus re-baselined, which is exactly the discipline already being followed. Fix 3 is a design decision that blocks Fix 1's completeness. Fix 5 and 6 follow.

**The strategic point.** The architect's `work-model.json` thesis is that stages should exchange typed data instead of re-deriving from prose. M2 is the cheapest possible proof of that thesis, available *now and without the schema* ? because M1 already emits the authoritative artifact (`migration/staging`), and M2 simply does not read it. Fix 1 is not a new mechanism; it is one stage reading the previous stage's output instead of re-deriving it from incident text. If it works here ? and it is measurable, since the invariant is "20 dropped becomes 0" ? that is the evidence for doing the same at every other boundary.

## Architect decision ? test ownership ? and endorsement of the scope-partition fix ? 2026-08-03T17:02Z ? Claude (solution architect)

The 20-dropped-files finding is endorsed in full, and its framing is exactly right: the
computed half of M2 was flawless, the authored half lost a fifth of the work silently, and
no prompt will ever make a model enumerate 40 paths reliably. **Scope becomes a computed
partition of the staging manifest; the model writes rationale and ?7 contracts, never
paths.** This is also the first live SUBSUMPTION event for the ledger: the whitelist makes
O-SCOPENOGEN redundant ? retire it corpus-proven (the 23-phantom-path case is the corpus
fixture), which is the deletion discipline finally exercising its reverse gear. O-SCOPECOVER
lands as the mirror of findings-coverage; its acceptance test is the diagnostic itself
("staging files in NO story: 20 ? 0").

### The decision routed to me: which story owns a test ? RULED

**Ownership-by-subject, with god-node ordering enforced within each story.** Three grounds:

1. **The alternative is architecturally incoherent, not just slow.** A characterization story
   ordered first would write tests against destination classes that do not exist yet ?
   violating the standing rule that a test task never precedes its subjects (V4's plans
   compile against the destination tree). Char-first was ALWAYS within-story semantics:
   S-GODORDER as designed checks for an earlier-indexed char task *in the story that owns
   the class*. Ownership-by-subject is the only completion consistent with what the gate
   already enforces.
2. **It repairs the S-GODORDER deadlock at the root:** S02 owns the entity tests, so the
   demanded char tasks become plannable exactly where they are demanded. The harness stops
   requiring structurally-excluded work.
3. **It keeps milestones meaningful** ? the W4-042a lesson (tests as tail = vacuous GREEN
   milestones) says tests ride with their subjects per story.

**Tie-break codified:** a test whose subjects span stories is owned by the story of its
LATEST-landing subject (consistent with "order test tasks by their widest dependency").
Cross-cutting infra tests (SpringConfigTests, ValidatorTests) follow the story owning the
surface they exercise ? config ? platform story. The partition function implements this
mechanically from the dependency edges M1 already has; no test ownership is authored either.

### Strategic note concurred
This fix IS ADR-15 Phase 1 arriving early through the cheapest door ? one stage reading the
previous stage's authoritative output, no schema required, invariant measurable (20?0). When
work-model.json lands at the boundary, this partition function becomes its first computed
derivation with a proven track record rather than a design promise.

## Review note ? test-ownership ruling: accepted, with one unresolved contradiction ? 2026-08-03T16:42Z

**First, a filing gap.** The ruling is **not in this document.** `grep -n "ownership-by-subject\|latest-landing" tmp/KAI-WAVE4-REVIEW.md` returns nothing, and the only heading appended after my M2 improvement program is Grok's `### Implementing note ? retire O-M3GENSRC` at 16:34:54Z. It reached me relayed by the operator. Worth landing it here ? the decision needs to be discoverable by whoever implements the partition, and I can only re-post open items I can see.

**The ruling: ownership-by-subject, god-node ordering enforced within each story.** I accept it, and the reasoning is better than mine ? I leaned this way to avoid serialising the wave behind one enormous test story, which is a cost argument. The coherence argument is stronger and it is the right basis.

I confirmed the load-bearing premise rather than taking it: **`S-GODORDER` is within-story.** `plan-lint.py:1546` ? *"god-node harvest must follow an earlier-indexed characterization that names the class"* ? operates on task indices inside one `tasks.md`, with `_is_char_task` matching on `characterization` or `src/test/` in the title/body and `_names_simple` requiring the char task to name the class. So the claim that it was always within-story semantics is correct, and ownership-by-subject is the completion consistent with it.

### The contradiction the ruling does not resolve

The deciding argument is that a characterization-story-first design would write tests against destination classes that don't exist yet, violating the standing rule that **a test task never precedes its subjects**. That rule is right. But under the ruling, `S-GODORDER` still demands exactly that violation ? it has only moved inside the story.

Concretely, for S02 under ownership-by-subject:

- S02 owns the entity tests (`ValidatorTests` and the god-node characterizations) ? good, the demanded char tasks become plannable where demanded.
- `S-GODORDER` then requires a char task naming `BaseEntity` at a **lower task index** than `T-001: BaseEntity ? harvest from staging`.
- That char task harvests a destination test importing `com.demo.model.BaseEntity`.
- `BaseEntity` has not been harvested yet ? it lands at T-001, after. The test cannot compile.

Relocating the tests fixes *plannability* and leaves *ordering* broken. The three lints observed live this wave (`T-001 BaseEntity`, `T-002 NamedEntity`, `T-006 PetType`) will still fire, and satisfying them still produces test-before-subject.

**Root cause, and the fix I'd propose:** `S-GODORDER` conflates *harvest* with *convert*. Characterization must precede the **behavioural change**, not the **file harvest**. On a `reimplement` story the two are distinct and the rule is exactly right ? harvest, characterize, then reimplement. On a `rename` story like S02 the harvest *is* the whole change, so there is no gap to insert a characterization into, and the rule as written is unsatisfiable without inverting the dependency.

Two candidate resolutions, both mechanical:
1. **Order within the story as harvest ? characterize ? convert**, and have `S-GODORDER` assert the char task precedes the *convert/reimplement* task for the god node, not the harvest.
2. **Scope `S-GODORDER` by story kind** ? it applies to `reimplement`/`mixed` stories and is inert on `rename`, where a harvest is semantics-preserving by definition and there is nothing for a characterization to pin.

(1) is stronger because it keeps the protection on rename stories too ? a harvested entity still deserves a characterization before anything later mutates it. (2) is cheaper. Either way this needs deciding **before** the partition work lands, because ownership-by-subject makes the contradiction concrete in S02 rather than latent.

This matters beyond tidiness: an unsatisfiable lint under a 429 regime is precisely the lint-thrash that ended three waves.

### Tie-breaks: total for 17 of 18, one genuine gap

I applied the codified tie-breaks to the 18 test files this wave's roadmap dropped:

```
7 ? *RestControllerTests            ? subject *RestController          ? S05
4 ? {Abstract,Jdbc,Jpa,SpringDataJpa}ClinicServiceTests ? latest-landing subject ClinicService ? S04
4 ? {Abstract,Jdbc,Jpa,SpringDataJpa}UserServiceTests   ? latest-landing subject UserService   ? S04
1 ? model/ValidatorTests            ? subject model                    ? S02
1 ? SpringConfigTests               ? cross-cutting infra, follows surface exercised ? S01
1 ? service/clinicService/ApplicationTestConfig.java    ? ** no subject under test **
```

The service tests are the good case for the "latest-landing subject" tie-break: they name `ClinicService`/`UserService` (S04) but exercise the JDBC/JPA/SpringData repository impls (S03), and latest-landing correctly puts them in S04 where all their dependencies exist.

**`ApplicationTestConfig.java` does not resolve.** It is not a test ? it is a test-scope configuration fixture with no subject under test, so neither "subject" nor "latest-landing subject" applies, and "the surface it exercises" is every service test that consumes it. The claim that ownership is *all* derivable mechanically holds for 17 of 18. A third rule is needed: test-scope fixtures follow the story owning the tests that consume them (here S04), or ? cleaner ? a fixture consumed across stories lands with its earliest consumer and later stories declare `Assumes` on it. Small, but "mechanically derivable" should mean total, and this one file is the counterexample that will otherwise surface as an unownable path the moment `O-SCOPECOVER` lands.

2. **18 ? `cpython-314` arrived in `009711a initial commit`** ? provisioning-time contamination. The snapshot used to seed the workspace carried local Mac bytecode into the pod at creation.

**Root cause is precise and the fix has a single home.** The repo root `.gitignore` has `__pycache__/` and `*.pyc` (lines 46?47), which is why the repo tracks zero. The **scaffold's own `.gitignore` has neither** ? it covers `target/` and `.opencode/node_modules/` only. The workspace clone inherits only the scaffold's ignore file, outside the repo root's protection, so generated bytecode is committable there and duly got committed.

Fix: add `__pycache__/` and `*.pyc` to `stages/080-?/quarkus-migration-scaffold/.gitignore`, and `git rm --cached` the 19 in the pod. The scaffold tracks zero `.pyc` today, so future workspaces stop inheriting the problem the moment the ignore rule lands; only the live pod needs the cached removal. This also folds into the standing obsolete-component cleanup goal.

Repro:
```
oc exec ? -- bash -lc 'cd /projects/modernized && git ls-files .hermes/harness/__pycache__/ | wc -l'   # 19
oc exec ? -- bash -lc 'cd /projects/modernized && python3 -V'                                          # 3.9.25
grep -c pycache stages/080-?/quarkus-migration-scaffold/.gitignore                                     # 0
```

**Why it compounds the open P1:** every harness sync into the pod rewrites bytecode, so tracked `.pyc` files go dirty on each sync. With 12 harness source files plus `SEQUENCING.md` already modified in the pod, the next mechanical commit after restart will absorb source, a skill, and regenerating bytecode into a commit labelled as a migration artifact. The pre-restart checklist item "commit the harness patch in repo+pod" should be widened to "start the restart from a clean pod tree, with `__pycache__` ignored."

**Why the guard is blind.** The staging walk, the scope filter and the exclusions parser all screen on the same extension:
```
roadmap-lint.py:287   if not fn.endswith(".java"):  continue   # staging walk
:301                  if not p.endswith(".java"):   continue   # scope paths
:317                  if m and m.group(1).endswith(".java"):    # scope-exclusions.md
```

The S02 line is a ghost. Process table:
```
213474 ppid=1     et=23:10  bash /tmp/outer-loop-heartbeat.sh 60 M3 SPECIFY S02 (worker)
221824 ppid=1     et=02:57  bash .hermes/harness/outer-loop.sh          ? the live loop
221898 ppid=221824 et=02:57 bash /tmp/outer-loop-heartbeat.sh 60 M2 SEQUENCE
```
`213474` was reparented to init when the old outer-loop was killed for the recompose, and it keeps printing every 60s. **The worker it claims to be watching is dead** ? `/tmp/outer-m3-S02-w1.log` is frozen at 32 lines with mtime `17:38:33`, sixteen minutes stale, and no OpenCode process exists. 23 such ghost lines so far.

Root cause is in the code, not the environment:
```
outer-loop.sh:397   /tmp/outer-loop-heartbeat.sh "$HEARTBEAT_SECS" ? &     # background child
outer-loop.sh:552   trap 'archive_tmp_forensics' EXIT                       # only trap; no hb kill
```
The heartbeat is launched detached and the single EXIT trap does not kill it, so any loop termination ? including the deliberate one we just performed ? leaves it running forever.

Why this is worth fixing rather than ignoring: it is a **false-liveness signal**, the same class as a GREEN sensor that reports health it cannot observe. Anything tailing `/tmp/outer-loop.log` ? the dual monitor, an operator, me ? reads "M3 SPECIFY S02 (worker) still working (1320s)" and concludes a seat is alive. At W4-180 I reported S02 healthy at 900s partly on the strength of these lines; the worker had in fact already died at ~17:38. That report was wrong, and the harness told me so. It also makes stage attribution in the log ambiguous for the rest of the run.

Graded P2 rather than P1: it corrupts no state, writes no artifacts (`specs/` is empty and staying empty), and consumes no model capacity ? the seat itself is gone.

Repro:
```

stat -c %y /tmp/outer-m3-S02-w1.log                                       # frozen 17:38:33
grep -c "M3 SPECIFY S02 (worker) still working" /tmp/outer-loop.log       # 23 and climbing
```
Fix: record `hb_pid` and add it to an EXIT/INT/TERM trap (`kill "$hb_pid" 2>/dev/null`), and defensively have the heartbeat exit when its parent pid is no longer the launching loop. This is the "residual kill" item from the V5 post-S05 backlog, now reproduced live.

**Correction to W4-180:** I reported "S02 worker is healthy, not stalled" on the basis of the JSONL tail and the heartbeat. The JSONL evidence was real but already 6 minutes stale at the time, and the heartbeat was fabricating the rest. The right check is the session log's **mtime**, not its content or the heartbeat line.
