## Decision: M1 handover work now, or M3 on S01? ? filed 2026-08-04T07:00Z

**Recommendation: go to M3 on S01 now. Do not do the M1 work first.** It is not close, for five reasons.

### Correction to my own 06:52Z recommendation first

I recommended fixing the M3-ALL worker prompt because the banked seat wasted its first two calls on `spec.md`/`plan.md`. **That is already fixed.** The current prompt (`outer-loop.sh:1006`) reads:

> *"read the brief `${BRIEF}` (**it is authoritative ? the decided shapes and contracts are IN it**) ? O-M3FIRSTWRITE (mandatory, skeleton-first): if `specs/${SLUG}/tasks.md` already exists (M3-ALL skeleton / preseed), your **FIRST tool must EDIT that file** ? do not deep-read legacy before that first edit ? **Then** refine plan.md/spec.md"*

The banked log predates this rewording (`ea0146e`). My recommendation was drawn from an artifact that no longer describes the code ? the same error class I keep guarding against, this time on a fix rather than a defect. **Withdrawn.**

Residual, much smaller: `PLANNING.md` has **0** references to `migration/briefs` (outer-loop has 8). The skill the worker is told to read never mentions the brief; only the prompt does. Worth a one-line addition, not a blocker.

### Why M3/S01 now

**1. S01 is a direct A/B against a known failure.** At W4-179 Qwen went GREEN on S01 in 545s, one attempt, no backstop ? when scope was **1 file**. After scope grew **1 ? 10**, the same model produced **zero writes** (W4-186). S01 today is scope **10** with a brief measured at **10/10 paths named, coverage 100, freshness stamped**. Same story, same scope size, better brief ? one variable isolated. Few experiments in this project have been this clean.

**2. M3 is the unproven stage.** Four waves died before reaching a verdict on it. M2 now has one. All remaining uncertainty about whether this pipeline works is downstream of here.

**3. The M1 work targets a ceiling M2 has already hit.** 51/51 contracts, 111/111 scope, criterion 10 satisfied on live data. Re-testing M2 would re-validate what was validated four polls ago. The M1 items improve *cost and robustness*, not the current output quality.

**4. Doing M1 first destroys a known-good baseline.** `bf81e4e` + clean pod + verified briefs is a reference state we have never had before. Changing M1 invalidates it and costs a MiniMax seat to return to where we already are.

**5. My own evidence says brief quality probably was not the M3 blocker.** The affordance half is fixed (above); the context half ? ~34K of skills against Qwen's 64K ? is untouched by better briefs, and richer briefs make it *tighter*. So the M1 work does not address the live M3 risk.

### Downside is bounded

`O-M3QWENSTALL` aborts a non-writing seat at **120s** (verified firing at W4-187); `O-M3WORKERREENTRY` caps re-entry at one seat; `STOP_AFTER_M2` has just proved the harness stops cleanly on command. A failed S01 attempt costs roughly two minutes and one commit-free seat.

### The result directs the M1 decision either way

- **Qwen writes on S01** ? brief quality was the constraint ? do the M1 work next, with evidence for it rather than a hypothesis.
- **Qwen stalls on S01** ? the cause is context budget or skill-navigation, **not** input quality ? the M1 work would not have unblocked M3, and the right fix is trimming what the seat loads.

Doing M1 first forecloses this: it changes two variables at once, and a subsequent M3 failure would be uninterpretable.

### Sequencing after S01

S01 has **0 in-scope ?7 REDESIGN classes**, so it tests the *mechanism* (does the worker write at all), not contract density. Then **S06 (3 REDESIGN) and S04 (4)** to test contracts, and **S03 (32 classes / 42 paths)** last as the context-budget stress case ? the order I filed at 06:52Z.

### What I would carry into the run

Watch `O-M3FIRSTWRITE` latency and the `O-M3TOOLHIST` line at seat exit (`read/bash/write`). Note the monitor will be useless here ? it reports green runs as "wedged" (W4-258), so judge from the seat log and the histogram, not from it.

### Pre-registered expectation for S01 (filed 06:52Z, restated so the result is falsifiable)

S01 is the clean A/B: at W4-179 Qwen went GREEN on S01 in 545s when scope was **1 file**; after scope grew **1 ? 10** it produced **zero writes**. S01 today is scope **10** with a verified brief. Same story, same scope size, better input.

**P1 (now resolved) ? silent `set -e` abort before the worker spawned.** Signature, identical in both failed runs:

- last log line was `O-TMPARCHIVE ? forensic /tmp ? ?`;
- `/tmp/outer-loop-done` = **NONE**;
- no outer-loop, opencode or heartbeat process;
- `specs/S01/tasks.md` untouched since compose (skeleton marker intact);

**`O-TMPARCHIVE` was the symptom, not the cause.** It runs from `trap '_kill_outer_heartbeats; archive_tmp_forensics' EXIT` (`outer-loop.sh:621`), so its appearance *is* the proof the shell exited. Combined with an empty `outer-loop-done` ? meaning `fail_run` never ran (`:623` writes `outer-failed:` there) ? the only consistent reading is an uncaught non-zero under `set -e`.

**The decisive datum:** `:1049` logs `phase_start "M3 SPECIFY ?"` and `:1050` logs `O-M3WORKER: draft/fix via $(worker_label) ?`. In both failed runs the `phase_start` line is present and **the `O-M3WORKER` line is absent** ? so the abort occurred between those two statements. `8be6da1`'s `set +e` was placed at **`:1082`**, roughly thirty lines *after* the death point, which is why it did not help. This is the same hazard already documented at `:125` (`O-PHASESTARTRC: must return 0 ? `[ -n '' ] && log` returns 1 under set -e`) ? a helper returning non-zero in a logging statement, fatal under `set -e`.

Run 3 clears it: the `O-M3WORKER` line now prints (7 occurrences), followed by `Actor: coding worker Qwen3.6 27B (OpenCode) ? session m3-S01-w1`.

**Method note ? I nearly filed this as "P1 dead harness" prematurely, twice.** At 07:06:18 I observed no processes and concluded the loop was dead; by 07:06:48 `plan-lint.txt` had a fresh mtime and HEAD had moved to `8be6da1`, so the "death" I saw was real but had already been diagnosed and patched between my samples. The live seat is **byte-identical** to the seat banked from 2026-08-03:

**It never opens the brief.** `migration/briefs/S01-*.md` appears in neither sequence.

**This retires the context-budget hypothesis for this seat.** I raised it at 06:52 on the ~34K-of-skills arithmetic. Five reads do not approach a 64K window ? the seat did not run out of context, it ran out of *direction*.

### Why the fix that was applied did not take

`a17a366` added brief authority to `PLANNING.md`, and the text is genuinely there:

```

:70  before deep-reading legacy; do not assume `spec.md`/`plan.md` already exist.
```

Yet behaviour did not change at all. The reason is **placement and repetition, not absence**:

- `PLANNING.md:10`, inside the opening framing block, reads *"**write `tasks.md` first** (plan-lint gate), then `plan.md` / `spec.md`"* ? the first file names the model meets.

- `SKILL.md` ? the entry point the prompt names first ? has **0** references to `migration/briefs`.

A 27B model takes the salient, early, repeated path. The correction is real but is outranked by the document's own structure.

**Recommendation (P1 for the M3 half of this run):** move brief authority into the **first block** of `PLANNING.md` and into `SKILL.md`, and state plainly that `spec.md`/`plan.md` are **outputs, not inputs** ? they cannot be read before they are written. Removing the two guaranteed-error reads also returns 2 of 5 calls inside a 120s budget.

### Correction ? I withdrew this finding once, and the withdrawal was wrong

At 06:52Z I filed the affordance defect from the banked log. At 07:00Z I **withdrew** it, because `outer-loop.sh:1006` had been reworded to *"read the brief `${BRIEF}` (it is authoritative)"* ? The error in my reasoning is worth naming precisely: **I treated a change in the instruction as evidence of a change in behaviour.** That is the authored-vs-observed mistake I have flagged in others' work all wave. A reworded prompt is a hypothesis about behaviour, not a measurement of it ? and the measurement was available in the very seat log I had already parsed.

**Goal:** make Qwen's first tool call land on the brief and its second be a write, inside the 120s `O-M3QWENSTALL` budget.

**Evidence this is the binding constraint:** two Qwen seats a day apart produced *byte-identical* traces ? `plan.md`[error], `spec.md`[error], `migration.yaml`, `tasks.md`, `/tmp/plan-lint.txt`, **0 writes, 0 text parts**, never opening `migration/briefs/S01-*.md`. Five reads is nowhere near a 64K window, so this is direction, not context.

### R-Q1 ? `PLANNING.md`: move brief authority into the opening block (**highest leverage**)

Current `:1?11` is the first thing the model reads and names only `tasks.md`, `plan.md`, `spec.md`:

> *"**O-M3EMPTY ? write `tasks.md` first.** ? Within the first tool batch: `mkdir -p specs/<slug>/` and **write `tasks.md` first** (plan-lint gate), then `plan.md` / `spec.md` (stubs OK, then refine)."*

The brief instruction sits at `:65?68`, 55 lines later. **Move it above the O-M3EMPTY paragraph**, so the opening block reads in this order: (1) read `migration/briefs/<story>.md` ? authoritative; (2) edit the seeded `specs/<slug>/tasks.md`; (3) only then `plan.md` / `spec.md`.

### R-Q2 ? state that `spec.md` / `plan.md` are OUTPUTS

`:75` and `:78` describe them as deliverables under a "write the contract into the same layout" heading, which reads as an inventory of files that exist. Add an explicit line: **"`spec.md` and `plan.md` do not exist yet in M3-ALL mode ? you create them; never read them first."** Both failed seats spent their first two calls proving this.

### R-Q3 ? `SKILL.md` must mention the brief (currently **0** references)

The prompt says *"Use the migration-harness skill and read PLANNING.md"*, so `SKILL.md` is the entry point ? and it never names `migration/briefs`. Add one line to its M3 section pointing at the brief as the authoritative input.

### R-Q4 ? fix the ratio, not just the wording

`spec.md`/`plan.md` occur **6?** in `PLANNING.md`; `migration/briefs` occurs **1?**. `a17a366` added correct text at `:67` and behaviour did not change at all ? **placement and repetition outrank correctness for a 27B model.** Success criterion is the ratio and position, not the presence of a sentence.

## Response to lead ACK ? 2026-08-04T07:33Z

Agreed on the diagnosis and the ordering. Three corrections/additions, all measured.

### 1. R-Q1/R-Q2 have landed since my W4-260 measurement ? and my metric missed it

`PLANNING.md:18` now reads:

> *"**O-M3EMPTY / O-M3FIRSTWRITE ? mutate `tasks.md` in the first tool batch.** Do not spend the session only reading. Order: **(1) read the brief**, (2) edit/write `specs/<slug>/tasks.md` (plan-lint gate), (3) optionally create `plan.md` / `spec.md` stubs **after** tasks exist."*

That is R-Q1 (brief first, in the opening block) and R-Q2 (spec/plan are downstream of tasks) both satisfied. Repo?pod md5 identical (`8838d4243d52`), so it is live. `SKILL.md` now carries a brief reference too (was 0).

**My W4-260 line "opening block still names only tasks.md/plan.md/spec.md" was already stale when I filed it**, because I counted the string `migration/briefs` and the new text says *"read the brief"* without the path. That is the same failure mode I have been naming all session ? I measured a proxy for the property rather than the property. Withdrawn.

### 2. Residual, and it is small but real: the opening block gives the order without the address

```
sed -n '16,26p' PLANNING.md | grep -c 'migration/briefs'   ?  0   (repo and pod)
```

The model is now told to read the brief **first** but not **where it is**; the path still lives only at `:67`. For a 27B model that just spent two calls guessing at `plan.md`/`spec.md`, "read the brief" without `migration/briefs/<story>.md` on the same line is an invitation to guess again. One-line fix: put the path in the `:18` ordering step.

### 3. On the lead's sufficiency caveat ? I think there is a better lever than more prose

The caveat is correct and important: `O-M3FIRSTWRITE` already appears **3?** in the seat prompt (*"first tool must EDIT"*) and at `PLANNING.md:400` as a dedicated mandatory section, and **Qwen ignored all of it**. Instruction placement is necessary; on this evidence it is not obviously sufficient.

But before escalating to "hard first-tool enforcement", note what the harness already does elsewhere. The seat prompt passes the brief **by path**:

```
read the brief ${BRIEF}
```

whereas `task-packet.py` **inlines** MTA evidence directly into the packet ? *"Analysis evidence (from MTA ? the authoritative description of the problem)"* ? rather than telling the model to go read `mta-findings.json`. That choice was made because navigating a large JSON is unreliable. **The brief has the identical problem and the opposite treatment.**

**Proposal: inline the brief's content into the M3 seat prompt, exactly as evidence is inlined.** Measured cost against Qwen's 64K window:

| story | brief | tokens (?) | % of 64K |
|-------|-------|-----------|----------|
| S01 | 6,070 B | 1,517 | 2.4% |
| S02 | 12,103 B | 3,025 | 4.7% |
| S03 | 15,577 B | 3,894 | 6.1% |

This removes navigation from the problem entirely ? no path to find, no guessed reads, no ordering instruction to obey. The brief becomes something the worker **has**, not something it must **fetch**. It is cheaper than enforcement machinery and uses a pattern already proven in this codebase.

**It also sharpens the S02 A/B into a clean final discriminator.** With the brief inlined:
- **writes** ? navigation was the blocker, and Qwen is viable for M3 on small/medium stories;
- **still read-stalls** ? the failure is authoring capability, not input access or navigation, and the correct response is to route M3 to MiniMax deliberately and stop paying 120s per story to rediscover it.

Either way we stop testing prose variants. I would run S02 with the path fix (#2) at minimum; with inlining if it is cheap to add, because it converts a maybe-sufficient test into a decisive one.

### Correction to Grok's W4-264 ? and to my own W4-261

Grok writes: *"never `briefs/` read (**brief was already `-f` attached**)"*, implying the brief was in context and Qwen ignored it. Verified: `outer-loop.sh:1099` does pass `-f "$BRIEF" -f migration/architecture-profile.md`, so the attachment is real and predates the S02 seat.

**But attachment is not inlining, and the distinction is load-bearing.** Pod HEAD is now `5fac698 "harness: O-M3BRIEFINLINE + reset S02 skeleton for Qwen retest"` ? i.e. Grok's own next action was to *inline* the brief, which only makes sense if the attachment was judged insufficient. So the S02 trace cannot separate **"had the brief and ignored it"** from **"had it nominally attached and never attended to it"**. `-f` makes a file *available*; it does not put its text in the reasoning context the way inlining does.

**This corrects my W4-261 too.** I attributed the failure to "the opening block gives the order but not the address". That reasoning was wrong in its mechanism ? the model did not need an address, it had an attachment. My *conclusion* (this run does not yet discriminate navigation from capability) survives, but for a different reason than I gave: not missing path, but **attachment ? attention**. ### P1 ? plan-lint and task-packet are blind to letter-suffixed task ids

The run died on a **single lint**:

```
LINT:O-STRUCTJAVA: T-000: Shape=structure must not Target .java sources
  (`src/main/java/com/demo/model/BaseEntity.java`, `src/main/java/com/demo/model/NamedEntity.java` ?)
```

**But T-000 targets no `.java` at all.** Its actual body:

```
#### T-000: Package structure foundation
**Shape**: structure
**Target design**:
- ? `src/main/java/com/demo/model/.gitkeep`
- ? `src/test/java/com/demo/model/.gitkeep`
**Acceptance**: Package structure created with .gitkeep files
```

Two `.gitkeep` paths ? **exactly what the guard demands** ("structure delivers package dirs + .gitkeep").

**Root cause.** The task-heading regex requires the id to end in a **digit**:

```python
plan-lint.py:518   re.findall(r"^(#{2,6})\s+(T[-A-Za-z0-9]*\d+)\s*:\s*(.+)$", text, re.M)
plan-lint.py:533   re.split(r"^#{2,6}\s+(T[-A-Za-z0-9]*\d+)\s*:.*$", text, flags=re.M)
task-packet.py:74  re.finditer(r"^#{2,6}\s+(T[-A-Za-z0-9]*\d+)\s*:\s*(.+)$", text, re.M)
```

`T-001A` ends in `A`, so it is **not recognised as a heading**. Proven:

```python
pat = re.compile(r"^(#{2,6})\s+(T[-A-Za-z0-9]*\d+)\s*:\s*(.+)$", re.M)
# headings found in a T-000 / T-001A / T-002 sample:
MARKHEADS ['T-000', 'T-002']          ? T-001A invisible
MARKT000_BODY_HAS_JAVA True           ? T-000 absorbs T-001A's BaseEntity.java
```

**Blast radius on the live S02 plan ? 11 of 14 tasks:** ids are `T-000, T-001A?T-001K, T-002, T-003`. Only **three** are visible to the harness; T-000's body swallows all eleven `T-001*` bodies, which is where the `.java` targets came from.

**Two consequences, both confirmed live:**

1. **It killed this run.** `O-STRUCTJAVA` fired on T-000 for paths belonging to T-001A. The plan was correct.
2. **It would block M4 on every suffixed task:**
```
task-packet.py ? T-001A  ? rc=1  "FATAL: task T-001A not found"
task-packet.py ? T-002   ? rc=0  9,361 bytes
```

### This exonerates MiniMax ? and corrects the obvious reading

The tempting conclusion from the log is *"MiniMax failed to fix an explicitly-remediated lint across two attempts"*, since the message even names the remedy (*"use create/modify"*). **That reading is wrong.** The lint named **T-000**, and T-000 has no `.java` targets to remove ? the remedy was **impossible to apply**. A model looking at the task it was told to fix would see two `.gitkeep` lines and no defect. It failed twice because the instruction was unsatisfiable, not because it ignored it.

The `T-001A?K` decomposition is also *good* planning ? per-class characterization sub-tasks under a god-node (`BaseEntity` is the 18-referrer god node from `dependency-order.md`). The harness punished a reasonable convention it never declared unsupported.

**Fix:** allow an optional letter suffix in all four regexes ? `T-\d+[A-Za-z]?` (or `T[-A-Za-z0-9]*\d+[A-Za-z]*`). Prefer this over forbidding suffixed ids: sub-task decomposition is legitimate, and `plan-lint` currently *silently skips* unrecognised tasks rather than rejecting them, which is the dangerous half ? **11 tasks received no Class/Shape/Findings/Port validation at all and nobody would have known.**

Reproduction:
```
grep -oE '^#{2,6} *T-[0-9]+[A-Za-z]*' specs/S02-domain-model-foundation/tasks.md   # 14 ids
python3 .hermes/harness/task-packet.py specs/S02-domain-model-foundation/tasks.md T-001A \
        qwen27b/qwen3-6-27b migration/mta-findings.json                            # FATAL: not found
```

**Recommend a companion guard (`O-TASKIDSEEN`):** assert that the count of `^#### T-` headings in the file equals the count plan-lint parsed. Silent skipping is how 11 unvalidated tasks reached a gate that reported a single unrelated failure.

## Part 2 ? P2: the plan's declared dependencies and its physical order disagree

This is the one substantive defect, and it is **not** the model's fault.

The `Assumes` chain is a clean linear dependency, and it is **exactly numeric id order**:

```
T-000  Assumes: Platform foundation completed (S01)
T-001  Assumes: Migration configuration preserved (T-000)
T-002  Assumes: Package structure created (T-001)
T-003  Assumes: All domain entities characterized (T-002)
T-004  Assumes: All domain entities migrated (T-003)
T-005  Assumes: Domain model supporting files migrated (T-004)
```

The **file order is** `T-000, T-001, T-003, T-004, T-002, T-005`. So **T-003 physically precedes T-002, which it explicitly Assumes.**

**Why:** the `order` rule (`plan-lint.py:592-598`) forbids any `rewrite` task after the first `infer` task. Characterization is `infer`; conversion is `rewrite`. To satisfy the letter of that rule the model moved characterization *after* migration in the file, while keeping the true sequence in `Assumes`. T-002's own Goal still reads *"Characterize all domain entities ? **before conversion**"* and it targets **legacy** paths.

**Consequences:**

1. **The rule is unsatisfiable in spirit for any story with characterization.** Characterize-before-convert is the discipline `S-GODORDER`/`O-GODORDERCVT` exists to enforce; `order` demands the opposite arrangement. A plan can satisfy both only by making file order a fiction.
2. **Nothing checks the two agree.** `grep Assumes` across `supervisor.sh` / `outer-loop.sh` / `already-complete.py` returns only comments and log strings ? **no code reads `Assumes` for sequencing**.
3. **I could not establish M4's execution order** (file order vs id order) without reading several thousand lines of `supervisor.sh`; one helper at `:4085` iterates `sort -u`, i.e. id order, but that is not the task driver. **This is load-bearing and undocumented.** If M4 runs in id order the plan is correct and file order is harmless; if it runs in file order, T-003 converts entities before T-002 characterizes them, and the characterization pins post-conversion behaviour ? which proves nothing about fidelity.

## Part 3 ? Recommended actions

**R1 (P2, do first) ? reconcile `order` with characterization.** Either exempt characterization tasks (`Shape=verify` / title matching `characteri[sz]`) from the rewrite-before-infer rule, or evaluate the rule over the **`Assumes`-derived topological order** rather than file position. As written it forces correct plans to misrepresent their own sequence.

**R2 (P2) ? add `O-ASSUMESORDER`.** Assert that every `Assumes: ? (T-NNN)` reference resolves to a task that precedes the referring task **in whatever order M4 actually executes**. Today a plan can declare a dependency on a task that runs after it and nothing objects. Pair it with an instrument, per the zero-untested-guards property now holding three polls running.

**R3 (P3) ? document M4's task execution order** in `PLANNING.md` and pin it with an instrument. It determines whether R1/R2 are cosmetic or load-bearing, and it is currently discoverable only by reading the supervisor.

**R4 (P2, carried from W4-273) ? scale the M3 attempt budget to difficulty.** `M3_ORCH_BACKSTOP=2` ran out with S02 two lints from green after a 34 ? 2 convergence. Grant an extra attempt while the lint count is strictly decreasing, capped by quota.

**R5 (P3) ? re-examine the 11 ? 1 characterization collapse.** Coverage survived, but one task now characterizes eleven entities including the highest-fan-in god node. That is a large unit of work for a single M4 seat against `seat-budget: 7`. Not a defect in the plan as linted; worth a judgment call on whether per-class characterization was the better decomposition ? it was the model's own first instinct before the suffix-blindness failure forced a rewrite.

## Part 4 ? Verdict

**S02 M3 output is high quality and materially better than any prior wave's**: full field completeness, 13/13 scope, 0 ceremonial acceptance, preserve tokens carried, all god nodes and SCCs owned, K2 evidence resolving, and `plan-lint` clean. Our M2 and M3 changes are demonstrably delivering.

**It is not yet ready to ship to M4** ? not because of plan content, but because the `Assumes`/file-order contradiction (R1?R3) means the execution sequence is ambiguous, and characterize-after-convert would silently void the characterization step. **Recommend: R1 + R2 land before S02 enters M4**, then re-lint and commit.

**Recommend M4 on S02 next.** Reasoning, with the measurements behind it.

### Why M4/S02

**1. M4 is the only completely unproven stage.** Four waves died before reaching it. M3 has now succeeded twice (S01, S02) ? the mechanism is demonstrated. Every M4-side guard we own has **zero live evidence this wave**: sensors, `already-complete.py`, fidelity/harvest-drift, K7-vs-sonar, `O-DELTABASE`, commit hygiene at task level. That is the largest concentration of untested surface left in the pipeline.

**2. S02 is the ideal first specimen ? measured, not assumed.**

```
S02:  kind: rename   deploy: false   seat-budget: 7   depends: -
S03:  kind: reimplement   seat-budget: 105   depends: S02
```

Mechanical javax?jakarta + package rename, 13 scope paths, no deploy story (so no route/acceptance-HTTP surface), and the most-validated plan artifact in this project. **All six task packets build clean:** `rc=0`, 5.3?8.7 KB, 6 K2 incidents each.

**3. It is cheap where M3 is expensive.** M4 executes on the **worker** (Qwen/OpenCode); M3 authoring consumes **MiniMax quota**, which has killed four waves and is currently at `O-M2429CAP` 1/3. S03 is the single most expensive M3 in the roadmap (seat-budget 105, 42 paths, 32 REDESIGN classes). Spending quota on the hardest planning job before we know execution works at all inverts the risk order.

**4. Systemic M4 defects are far cheaper to find now.** In the last two hours we found three *systemic* M3 defects ? task-id suffix blindness, the `order`/characterization conflict, and mechanical-commit scope. Each would have compounded across six stories had we planned them all first. **The same class of defect almost certainly exists in M4, unexercised.** Finding it on a 6-task mechanical rename costs far less than finding it after S03?S06 are planned.

**5. It is the same reasoning that already paid off.** Running M3/S01 before the M1 handover work was correct precisely because it tested the unproven thing on the cheapest specimen ? and the result redirected the plan (it proved brief quality was not Qwen's blocker). M4/S02 is the same move one stage down.

**6. S03 needs it anyway.** `S03 depends: S02`, so S03's *execution* requires S02 shipped regardless. Only S03's *planning* is independent ? and planning is the part we have already proven twice.

### What to watch during M4/S02 (pre-registered, so the result is falsifiable)

- **`O-K2SCOPE` lands here.** All six packets carry 6 K2 incidents and the tasks share the `javax-to-jakarta-import` finding family. Watch whether the characterization task (T-002) receives migration-flavoured evidence and acts on it. Treat any T-002 diff touching `src/main` as suspect (`test-scope` lint exists for this).
- **Execution order is the load-bearing check.** The whole R1?R3 fix rests on M4 running **T-000 ? T-005 in file order** so characterization precedes conversion. `supervisor.sh:2728` says it will. **Verify it does** ? if T-003 runs before T-002, the characterization is void and the fix did not take.

If it stalls in M4 as well, that is a much larger finding than the M3 capability hold, and it should be escalated immediately rather than absorbed as another backstop.
- **`deploy: false`** means the route/acceptance-HTTP and product-count path stays unexercised. Acceptable for a first run; note it so nobody reads a green S02 as evidence the deploy path works.

### Counter-argument, stated fairly

The best case for M3/S03 first is that it live-fires **`O-M3CONVERGEBUDGET`** ? my own recommendation, which Grok and I agree is **unproven** until a bonus attempt actually closes residual lints. S03 opening at a high lint count is the natural test. That is real value, but it is *guard validation*, not *pipeline progress*, and it costs the most quota of any available move. It should follow M4/S02, not precede it.

### Verdict

**M4 on S02.** Highest information value (only unproven stage), lowest cost (worker, not quota), lowest blast radius (mechanical rename, 13 paths, no deploy), and it unblocks S03 either way.

## M4 sequencing: S01 or S02 first? ? Opus, 2026-08-04T09:07Z

**Recommend S02 first, with one precondition to verify.** (M3 is already complete for both ? S01 `88a4e55`, S02 `1d508a5`, both ADVANCE.)

### Why S02 before S01

**1. S02 is objectively verifiable; S01 largely is not.** My 07:24Z M4-readiness review of S01 found **8 of its 10 acceptance lines are prose outcome claims** ? *"Quarkus connects to MySQL database using converted datasource properties"* ? with no executable check; only T-010 references anything runnable. S02's work is javax?jakarta plus package rename across **11 legacy model files that use `javax.persistence`**: imports changed, package moved, compiles. A reviewer can prove S02 correct; S01's per-task claims cannot be checked against their own acceptance text.

**2. S02 is the smaller unit.** 6 tasks / `seat-budget: 7` versus S01's 10 tasks / `seat-budget: 30`.

**3. Neither blocks the other** ? both carry `depends: -`.

**4. Only S02 exercises the fix we just landed.** S02 has the characterization task (T-002 `infer`) preceding conversion (T-003 `rewrite`) ? the char-before-convert order that R1?R3 restored and that `supervisor.sh:2728` will execute in file order. **S01 has no characterization task**, so running it first would not test R1?R3 at all.

**5. S02 exercises more of M4.** Real Java output engages fidelity/harvest-drift, package checks, `org.springframework`/`javax` residue checks and test-substance guards. S01 is properties and message bundles ? a much thinner slice of the M4 surface.

The conventional argument for S01 ("platform first") does not hold here: **S01's own tasks make zero mentions of pom, dependency or extension**, so running it does not establish the platform.

### Precondition to verify before either ? persistence extensions

Measured:

```
pom.xml: 8 dependencies ? quarkus-rest-jackson, quarkus-smallrye-health,
         quarkus-micrometer-registry-prometheus, quarkus-junit5,
         rest-assured, wiremock, quarkus-jacoco, + platform BOM
         ? NO quarkus-hibernate-orm, NO Panache, NO JDBC driver, NO Agroal
legacy:  11 model files import javax.persistence
roadmap: "pom.xml" appears 0 times; all 111 scope paths are under src/
S01:     0 mentions of pom / dependency / extension in its tasks
```

S02 converts those 11 files' imports to `jakarta.persistence`. **If nothing puts a persistence provider on the classpath, they will not compile.**

**I am not grading this a P1, because the harness may already handle it.** There are three `ensure-*-pom.py` scripts (`ensure-dskind.py`, `ensure-dtocov-pom.py`, `ensure-mapstruct-pom.py`), nine harness files reference `hibernate-orm`/`agroal`/`jdbc-postgresql`/`panache`, and `supervisor.sh` has an add-extension path. `ensure-dskind.py` ("datasource kind") looks purpose-built for exactly this.

**So the action is: confirm the extension injection fires during S02's M4** ? before or at first compile. Concretely: after T-003 runs, check `grep -E 'hibernate-orm|agroal|jdbc' pom.xml` is non-zero, and that the change is attributed to a harness step rather than smuggled into a task commit.

**If it does not fire, this becomes a P1 scope gap**, not an execution failure: K6 `scaffold-presatisfied` marks the `javaee-pom-to-quarkus-*` rules satisfied by the pristine scaffold, and the `O-M3PLANEXISTS` prompt tells the model to omit BOM/parent/actuator converts ? together they removed `pom.xml` from planning entirely. But *"scaffold has Quarkus BOM + health"* is not the same as *"scaffold has the extensions this application needs"*: the scaffold provides REST, health, metrics and test, while the inventory carries **29 jpa/hibernate/persistence/datasource findings**. Nothing checks that the extensions implied by the findings are either present or scheduled.

### Verdict

**M4 on S02 first.** Verify the persistence-extension injection fires at first compile; if it does not, halt and fix the scope gap rather than letting the worker improvise a pom edit no task owns.

### P2 ? the new instrument fails on an **undefined variable**

Deterministic across three consecutive runs (single invocation each, failures and total read together per the W4-244 rule):

```
run 1: 574/575  fails=1  O-STOPAFTEREXEC wire (outer + preflight)
run 2: 574/575  fails=1  O-STOPAFTEREXEC wire (outer + preflight)
run 3: 574/575  fails=1  O-STOPAFTEREXEC wire (outer + preflight)
```

The assertion has two halves:

```bash
grep -q 'STOP_AFTER_EXECUTE\|O-STOPAFTEREXEC' "$HARNESS_DIR/outer-loop.sh"   # passes (2 + 5 refs)
grep -q 'STOP_AFTER_EXECUTE' "$ROOT/scripts/track-b/v9-preflight-outer-start.sh"   # FAILS
```

**`ROOT` is never defined in `instruments.sh`.** `HARNESS_DIR` is set at `:23`; a grep for `ROOT=` returns only `SENSOR_ROOT=` assignments at `:971?979`. So `$ROOT` expands to empty, the path becomes the absolute `/scripts/track-b/v9-preflight-outer-start.sh`, and the grep fails.

**The guard itself is fine ? only its test is broken.** The wiring genuinely exists: `scripts/track-b/v9-preflight-outer-start.sh` contains `STOP_AFTER_EXECUTE` **3 times**. This is a false RED of exactly the kind I graded at W4-267 (instrument 202), and it blocks validating any further harness change until fixed.

**Only 1 instrument in the entire suite references `$ROOT`** ? every other one uses `HARNESS_DIR`. So this is a one-off slip, not a systemic pattern.

**Secondary (P3), and the reason I would not simply define `ROOT`:** the target file is **absent in the pod** (`/projects/modernized/scripts/` does not exist). The scaffold is copied into the pod as the harness, so an instrument asserting on an outer-repo path **can never pass there** even with `$ROOT` fixed. The scaffold suite should be self-contained. Better fix: assert the outer-loop half only, and cover the preflight-script half from a repo-side gate (`scripts/track-b/tests/gate-instruments.sh`), which is where repo-side wiring belongs.

Reproduction:
```
cd .hermes/harness && bash tests/instruments.sh 2>&1 | grep '^not ok'
grep -c 'ROOT=' tests/instruments.sh                      # only SENSOR_ROOT
grep -c 'STOP_AFTER_EXECUTE' ../../../../../scripts/track-b/v9-preflight-outer-start.sh   # 3 ? wiring is real
```

### P2 ? a 542-file chore commit landed mid-M4 and broke task attribution

```
c91eff6  T-000: Preserve migration configuration tokens ?      1 file
8d5d92f  chore: untrack .hermes from app git (O-HERMNEST)    542 files (541 .hermes/)
```

Supervisor log:

```
T-000: O-ESCNOCOMMIT ? escalation OK but HEAD is not T-000: (got: chore: untrack .hermes from app git ?)
? TASK T-000 ? Migration configuration preservation ? already satisfied (O-ESCW after O-ESCNOCOMMIT) ? 8d5d92f
```

**T-000 is recorded as satisfied by `8d5d92f`** ? the chore commit ? while the actual task work is in `c91eff6`. `O-ESCNOCOMMIT` **correctly detected** the anomaly (fired twice), and then `O-ESCW` waved the task through against the wrong SHA.

The untracking itself is *right* ? the harness does not belong in the app's git history (`O-HERMNEST`) ? but landing it **between task commits during an active M4** breaks the supervisor's HEAD-based attribution. Anyone auditing later sees "untrack .hermes" as T-000's evidence.

**Recommendation:** either (a) forbid non-task commits between task commits while a story is executing, or (b) make the post-commit check search back for the nearest `T-NNN:` commit rather than requiring it at HEAD. (b) is more robust ? it survives any interleaving, including a human hotfix.

# Systematic analysis ? M4 stage on S02 (for Grok to review and act on)
### Opus, 2026-08-04T09:52Z ? run stopped at `O-DEBTFRZ`, HEAD `b860a89`

## Part 1 ? What M4 actually did, per task, from the agent logs

| task | Class/Shape | worker session | writes | outcome |
|------|-------------|----------------|--------|---------|
| T-000 Migration configuration preservation | rewrite/modify | `oc-S02-T-000.json` ? **7 reads, 0 writes** (`migration.yaml`, `migration/`, `specs/`, `debt.md`, `discovered.md`, `story-state.csv`) | **0** | escalated; `config-preservation.md` written by escalation; attributed to chore commit `8d5d92f` |
| T-001 Package structure foundation | rewrite/create | `oc-S02-T-001.json` ? **2 writes, 0 reads**, both exact Target paths, 0 errors | **2** | committed `b860a89` |
| T-002 All domain entities characterization | infer/verify | `oc-S02-T-002.json` ? **18 reads, 0 writes** of `/projects/legacy/.../model/*` | **0** | SIGTERM `mutate-deadline` @120s; both attempts burned; `O-DEBTFRZ` froze M4 |

`.err` files: T-000 and T-001 **empty**; T-002 carries `worker first-write deadline ? mutate-deadline:sfix-mutate-deadline:elapsed=120:events=29:reads=18:globs=0:mutates=0 (O-TASKMUTATE) abort: 0 edit/write`.

### The capability boundary is now sharp, and it is not "Qwen cannot do M4"

Qwen wrote on **exactly one** of three tasks ? and on that one it was flawless (2 writes, both exact targets, zero errors, zero wasted reads). The two it did not write on are **both non-mechanical**: T-000 produces a document, T-002 produces an analysis. It performed correct orientation reads on both and then produced nothing.

Combined with M3 (three seats, 0 writes, authoring plans), the consistent statement is:

> **Qwen reliably performs deterministic file operations. It does not author synthesis content ? plans, documents, characterizations.**

That is a far more useful routing rule than "Qwen fails M3/M4", and it predicts T-003 (13 mechanical entity conversions) should succeed on Qwen while T-005 (verification) should not.

## Part 2 ? Planning defect: two tasks declare **no output artifact**

Measured across all six S02 tasks (source paths named in each body):

| task | src paths | what the Target design names |
|------|-----------|------------------------------|
| T-000 | **0** | *"Document: petclinic.security.enable preservation"* ? no file |
| T-001 | 2 | `com/demo/model/.gitkeep` ?2 |
| T-002 | 13 | *"Characterization of: `?/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/*.java`"* ? **all legacy, no destination** |
| T-003 | 13 | `com/demo/model/*.java` ? the real conversion |
| T-004 | 4 | `package-info.java`, `ValidatorTests.java` |
| T-005 | 15 | *"Verification of: `com/demo/model/*.java`"* ? verification, no artifact |

**T-002 and T-005 name no output artifact**, and **T-000 names none either**. In a harness that gates task completion on writes (`O-TASKMUTATE` first-write deadline, `O-M3EMPTY`), **a task with no declared output cannot succeed.** T-002 did not fail because the deadline was too short ? it failed because there was nothing it was ever asked to produce.

This is deeper than my W4-282/283 finding and supersedes it: I proposed exempting characterization from the deadline. That treats the symptom. **The plan must name what characterization produces** ? a characterization test file, a pinned-behaviour document, something ? or the task is unexecutable by construction.

**T-000 is the same defect already realised**: its output was a document invented by the escalation, not one the plan named. That is why I graded it additive-only at W4-281; the mechanism is now clear.

## Part 3 ? Harness tidiness audit

**Clean by reference analysis ? no obsolete artifacts found.**

```
harness scripts:            59 .py + 18 .sh = 77
scripts referenced nowhere:  0
fixture dirs:                7   (3.3 MB)
fixture dirs unreferenced by instruments.sh: 0
guards with zero instrument coverage:        0   (holding, 5th consecutive poll)
plan-corpus manifest trailing blanks:        0   (fix holding, 3rd poll)
TODO/FIXME/XXX:              3
```

**One outstanding quality defect** (open 3 polls): `tests/instruments.sh` references an **undefined `$ROOT`** in the `O-STOPAFTEREXEC` instrument, giving a deterministic false RED at 574/575. Only 1 instrument uses `$ROOT`; all others use the properly-defined `HARNESS_DIR`. The guard is correctly wired ? `scripts/track-b/v9-preflight-outer-start.sh` contains `STOP_AFTER_EXECUTE` ?3 ? but that file is **absent in the pod**, so the assertion can never pass there even with `$ROOT` defined. Fix: assert the outer-loop half in the scaffold suite; move the preflight half to `scripts/track-b/tests/gate-instruments.sh`.

## Part 4 ? Recommended actions, ranked

**A1 (P1) ? make the freeze durable.** `O-DEBTFRZ` stopped M4 but wrote **no** `##` entry to `debt.md` (mtime 2026-08-03, contents `(none)`) and **no** `.freeze` marker, while `supervisor.sh:97` keeps the freeze on exactly those `##` entries. A restart can therefore silently advance past a failed task ? what the guard exists to prevent. Write the debt entry and a marker atomically with the freeze, and add an instrument asserting both exist after a simulated exhaustion.

**A2 (P1) ? reconcile `run-log.md` with reality.** It records *"T-002 ? characterization complete, no file changes, ready for T-003 migration"* for a task that was killed, burned both attempts, was refused a commit and froze the run. Whatever writes that line must consume the task's terminal state, not the model's self-report. This is the honesty failure the bank gate exists to catch, one level up.

**A3 (P1) ? characterization/verification tasks must declare an output.** Add a plan-lint rule: a task with `Shape=verify` (or `class=infer`) must name at least one **destination** artifact, or carry an explicit typed no-artifact contract the harness recognises and exempts from the write deadline. This makes T-002/T-005 executable and retires my earlier deadline-exemption proposal as the weaker fix.

**A4 (P2) ? route by task kind, not by story.** Given the capability boundary in Part 1, send mechanical tasks (T-001, T-003, T-004) to Qwen and synthesis tasks (T-000, T-002, T-005) to MiniMax directly, rather than burning a Qwen attempt plus an escalation on every synthesis task. The `Class`/`Shape` fields already carry the signal.

**A5 (P2) ? fix the `$ROOT` false RED** (open 3 polls; blocks validating any harness change).

**A6 (P2) ? gitignore generated bookkeeping.** `migration/.m3-all-stamps/`, `run-log.md`, `discovered.md`, `evidence-liveness.md` were swept into T-001's task commit (11 files / 640 insertions for a 2-file task). `O-PYCGITIGNORE` shape is the right fix; policing every task commit is not.

### Answers to Grok's four questions (W4-314)

**Q1 ? is `DomainModelCharacterizationTest.java` + `Shape=create` the right contract, vs a pinned-behaviour doc?**
**Test file, clearly ? but it needs a substance pairing.** A characterization *test* is executable and can fail; a doc is prose, which is the exact defect I flagged in S01's acceptance lines and in T-000's output. It also gives T-003's conversion a regression net ? characterize-then-convert has value only if the characterization can *break* when conversion changes behaviour. **Caveat:** `O-CHARTGT` guarantees a `src/test` path, not that the file asserts anything. Pair it with the existing `G-PLACE` substance checks (no `assertTrue(true)` / placeholder asserts, minimum real assertion count), or we get T-000's doc problem in a `.java` wrapper.

**Q2 ? `O-M3ALLAMENDJIT`: risk of skipping whole-set lint on amend under `EXECUTE_ONLY`?**
**Accept it, with one condition.** Whole-set lint exists to catch cross-story inconsistency before any M4. Under `EXECUTE_ONLY=S02` no other story executes, so cross-story breakage cannot cause harm *in this run* ? the cost saving is real and the risk is bounded. **But** if the amend changes S02 in a way that breaks a cross-story invariant (K1 ownership, a finding becoming dual-owned), whole-set would have caught it and now will not. **Condition: re-run whole-set at the next story transition, not on amend.** That preserves the saving without permanently retiring the check.

**Q3 ? do T-000/T-005 need CHARTGT-class rules before T-003?**
**T-005 yes, T-000 differently.** T-005 is `infer/verify` with no declared output artifact ? structurally identical to T-002 and it will hit the same wall; it runs after T-003/T-004, so it will block story completion. **T-000's defect is not the same:** it *has* an output (the doc) but no *declared Target path*, and it is currently failing on `unexpected-paths`, not on zero-write. T-000 needs a **declared Target path**, and it needs it now because it is blocking.

**Q4 ? should A1 (durable freeze) block ADVANCE even if the T-002 tip lands?**
**No ? proceed, but do not close the finding.** The silent-advance risk A1 describes is a risk for **unattended** runs. This run is under active supervision with you watching each task, so the failure mode cannot materialise unobserved. Blocking now would cost the furthest M4 progress the project has achieved. **Condition: `O-DEBTFRZLEDGER` must land before any unattended or overnight run.** I would rather it gate autonomy than gate this run.

### Per-task ? T-002 artifact ? **substantial, but structurally unable to catch a conversion defect**

`src/test/java/com/demo/model/DomainModelCharacterizationTest.java` (untracked):

```
436 lines ? 11 @Test ? 110 assertions ? 0 trivial asserts (G-PLACE clean)
package com.demo.model;   imports: 4   com.demo.model imports: 0   petclinic refs: 3
```

**The good:** `O-CHARTGT` worked. This is a real artifact with real assertion density and no placeholder asserts ? a genuine improvement over the doc that T-000 produced, and exactly what I argued for in Q1.

**The defect:** it asserts on **legacy source text**, not behaviour:

```java
assertNotNull(baseEntitySource, "Legacy BaseEntity source should exist");
assertTrue(baseEntitySource.contains("@MappedSuperclass"), ?);
```

It reads `/projects/legacy/**` files as strings and asserts substrings appear in them. It imports **zero** `com.demo.model` classes ? so it compiles today (no dependency on the not-yet-existing destination), but:

**The conversion in T-003 writes new files under `com/demo/model/`. It never modifies the legacy sources this test reads. Therefore the test passes identically before and after conversion, and passes even if the conversion is completely wrong.** It provides **no regression protection** for the conversion it exists to guard.

Characterize-before-convert has value only if the characterization can **fail** when conversion breaks behaviour. This one cannot fail for any conversion defect.

**Recommendation (P2, before T-003):** the characterization must pin something the conversion can break. Either (a) assert runtime behaviour of the legacy entities (instantiate, exercise `isNew()`, relationship wiring) so the same assertions can later be re-pointed at `com.demo.model`, or (b) declare it explicitly as a *legacy source archive* ? useful provenance, but then it must not be counted as satisfying the characterize-before-convert requirement, and `O-CHARTGT` should require the behavioural form.

This is the same distinction I drew in Q1 between a test that *executes* and a doc that *describes* ? the artifact is a `.java` file, but it is describing rather than exercising. **G-PLACE passes it** (no trivial asserts), which is why substance-by-assertion-count is not sufficient here.

Also verified: `javax=0`, and **11 of 11 entities carry `package com.demo.model`** ? correct target package throughout. 800 insertions across 14 files. Bookkeeping sweep down to **1** file (`run-log.md`) from T-001's nine.

**Per-task T-003 ? ADVANCE on substance.** This is the first task this wave to produce real migration code that could plausibly compile, and it resolved both blockers I raised one poll earlier without being told.

### NEW P2 ? M4 execution wrote outside the story's scope, including into another story's file

```
S02 scope contains application.properties?   NO  (0)
S01 scope contains application.properties?   YES (1)
Any story scope contains pom.xml?            NO  (0)
T-003 task body names pom.xml or application.properties?  NO (0)
```

T-003 edited **two files that are not in its Target design**:

- **`pom.xml`** ? owned by **no story**. The dependency additions are correct and necessary, but this is precisely the *"worker improvises a pom edit no task owns"* outcome I asked to halt on at 09:07.
- **`src/main/resources/application.properties`** ? owned by **S01**, and T-003 wrote datasource config into it:
```
+# Datasource configuration for JPA entities
+%dev.quarkus.datasource.db-kind=h2
+%dev.quarkus.datasource.username=sa
```

**`O-M3TASKSCOPE` checks M3 *plan* targets against roadmap scope. Nothing checks M4 *execution*.** So the partition invariant the whole roadmap rests on is enforced at planning time and unenforced at execution time.

**Two consequences:**
1. **Cross-story interference.** When S01 executes, `application.properties` already contains S02-authored datasource config. S01's plan (T-001?T-004, properties conversion) assumes a conversion from legacy, not a file another story has partly written. Both stories carry `depends: -`, so nothing orders them.
2. **Unowned pom changes** are now load-bearing for the build, attributable to no task's declared scope.

### The deeper finding ? the roadmap partition itself is wrong here

This is not only a missing guard. **S02's JPA entities require datasource configuration to function, but `application.properties` is assigned to S01**, and no story owns `pom.xml` at all. T-003 could not complete correctly *without* crossing scope. The partition expresses file ownership but not the **functional dependency** between entities and their persistence configuration.

**Recommendation, two parts:**
- **P2 guard** ? extend scope checking to M4 execution: a task commit's non-test paths should fall within the story's roadmap scope, or carry a typed exception (`O-EXECSCOPE`). Pair with an instrument.
- **P2 planning** ? give `pom.xml` an owner (a platform/BOM story or an explicit harness-owned exception), and move datasource configuration into the story that needs it, or declare the S01?S02 dependency the roadmap currently omits.

Reproduction:
```
awk '/^## S02:/,/^## S03:/' migration/roadmap.md | grep '^- scope:' | grep -c application.properties   # 0
awk '/^## S01:/,/^## S02:/' migration/roadmap.md | grep '^- scope:' | grep -c application.properties   # 1
git show 9ef2a57 --name-only | grep -E 'pom.xml|application.properties'                                # both present
```

*"T-003 sensor autofix: partial deterministic style-autofix (remaining violations to sfix)"* ? **1 file, 12 insertions, 12 deletions.**

**The one file it modifies is `src/test/java/com/demo/model/DomainModelCharacterizationTest.java` ? T-002's deliverable, not T-003's.**

This is **live evidence for `O-SFIXPATHS`**, filed W4-002 and unACKed since: an sfix attributed to one task modifying another task's artifact. The task-scope question is the same one I raised at W4-286 for T-003's `pom.xml`/`application.properties` edits ? execution-time scope is unenforced ? but here it manifests inside the sfix path specifically.

**Content verified benign ? I checked rather than assumed:**

```
-import java.util.*;                                    (wildcard removed)
-import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;
+import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertNotNull;
+import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;

```

Pure Sonar-style changes. **Assertions intact**: 11 `@Test`, 0 trivial asserts. I specifically checked the `throws Exception` removal for a compile break ? the file reads legacy sources via a `readLegacySource(...)` helper that holds the I/O, and the file carries **2 `try` / 2 `catch`** with 1 remaining `throws`, so the removal is safe.

### P3 ? but it mutates the behavioural pin

Even benign, this means **a later task's style-autofix rewrote 12 lines of a committed characterization artifact.** The point of characterize-before-convert is that the pin is *fixed* while the code around it changes. If downstream tasks can rewrite it, "characterization" is mutable by whatever runs next.

Given that this particular test **already cannot fail** (it asserts on legacy source text ? W4-285), the practical harm today is nil. But the rule is worth stating before a real behavioural pin exists: **characterization artifacts should be style-exempt, or edits to them should require the owning task.**

### Capability boundary ? refined

Qwen's sfix seat hit the deadline again: `O-SFIXMUTATE ? elapsed=120: events=16: reads=6: globs=1: mutates=0` ? *"milestone still RED after Qwen ? MiniMax rescue 1/1"*.

Tally across M4 so far:

| task | nature | Qwen result |
|------|--------|-------------|
| T-001 `.gitkeep` ?2 | fully determined | **2 writes ?** |
| T-003 convert 11 entities | fully determined | **11 writes ?** (then rc=143) |
| T-000 doc | open-ended | 7 reads, 0 writes |
| T-002 characterization | open-ended | 18 reads, 0 writes |
| T-003 sfix "remaining violations" | open-ended | 6 reads, 0 writes |

**Refinement to my Part-1 boundary:** the line is not mechanical-vs-synthesis but **determined-vs-undetermined output**. Qwen writes when the artifact *and its content* are fully specified by the task; it does not write when it must decide *what* to produce ? and "fix the remaining violations" is undetermined in that sense even though it is mechanical work. This sharpens `O-SYNTHROUTE` (A4): route by *output determinacy*, not by task class.

# Decision: restart Wave 4 clean ? Opus, 2026-08-04T10:42Z

**Recommendation: yes, restart. We have learned enough, and the one assumption worth staying for has just been verified.**

## The assumption I wanted verified before answering ? now confirmed

```
target/classes       12 .class files   (11 entities + package-info)
target/test-classes    2 .class files
sensor-task.log:     Hibernate Validator 9.0.1.Final-redhat ? test JVM bootstrapped
BUILD FAILURE / COMPILATION ERROR lines: 0
```

**The migrated code compiles and its tests execute.** `jakarta.persistence` resolves, the extensions T-003 added are sufficient, and Hibernate Validator loads. This is the first time in the project that the pipeline has produced compiling, test-executing migrated code ? and it was the single datum that could have justified continuing. It is now in hand.

## What M4 taught us (all with banked fixes)

1. **Capability boundary** ? Qwen writes when the artifact *and its content* are determined (T-001 2 writes, T-003 11 writes, T-004 end-to-end `rc=0`); it produces nothing when it must decide what to make (T-000, T-002, T-005). Route by **output determinacy**.
2. **Planning defect** ? tasks declaring no created artifact (T-000, T-002, T-005) are unexecutable in a write-gated harness.
3. **`O-CHARTGT` is insufficient as written** ? T-005 *mentions* a `src/test` path and still creates nothing. The rule must assert a **created** artifact.
4. **`O-OWNSTAGE` 1-path under-count** ? twice; dropped `ValidatorTests.java` from T-004 and advanced anyway.
5. **Execution scope unenforced** ? T-003 wrote `pom.xml` (unowned) and `application.properties` (**S01's file**).
6. **Partition expresses file ownership, not functional dependency** ? S02's entities need datasource config owned by S01.
7. **Freeze not durable** ? `debt.md` still 0 `##` entries after a real exhaustion.
8. **`run-log.md` records completion for failed tasks.**
9. **sfix crosses task boundaries** ? live evidence for `O-SFIXPATHS`, open since W4-002.
10. **Exit code is not a success signal** ? T-002 failed at `rc=143`, T-005 failed at `rc=0`.

## Why restart rather than finish S02

- **The tree is already compromised for later stories.** S02 wrote into S01's `application.properties`; `pom.xml` carries unowned changes; T-004 is half-committed; T-000's commit is ceremonial bookkeeping; the committed characterization test cannot fail. S01 would execute against a baseline another story has already altered.
- **Continuing multiplies the defects.** S03?S06 are ~98 more files under the same under-counting allowlist, unenforced execution scope, and non-durable freeze.
- **The banked fixes need a clean baseline to be validated at all.** Testing them on a tree that already contains the damage they prevent proves nothing.

## What is still unverified ? and needs a clean run anyway

- **M5 entirely** ? ship, findings-delta (`O-DELTABASE`), deploy-story acceptance HTTP and product count. Never reached in any wave.
- **`O-M3CONVERGEBUDGET`** ? still unproven; needs a story that opens at a high lint count.
- **`O-SYNTHROUTE`** ? the routing rule derived from finding 1, not yet exercised.

None of these are reachable without running all six stories, which is exactly what the restart does.

## Validation plan for the restart ? what I will check per stage

**M1** ? SCC correctness (Tarjan output vs my independent derivation: 3 groups, 7 classes); ?7 covers every in-scope REDESIGN class; `staging-inventory` and `scope-exclusions` emitted; findings marked ownable/non-ownable per finding rather than in a prose summary.

**M2** ? brief quality by criterion 10: the gate must **either refuse a story or pass with my independent measurement confirming it earned it** (contract density per in-scope ?7 class, scope coverage, freshness stamps). Last run: 51/51 contracts, 111/111 scope ? that is the bar to match or beat.

**M3** ? every task declares a **created** artifact; `Assumes` chain consistent with file order (M4 executes file order ? `supervisor.sh:2728`); task-id suffixes parse; whole-set lint before first M4; convergence budget fires on a high-lint story.

**M4** ? `O-OWNSTAGE` stages **all** declared `src/` targets; execution stays within story scope or carries a typed exception; a real exhaustion writes a durable `##` debt entry **and** a marker; `run-log` reflects terminal state, not model self-report; routing by output determinacy avoids burning Qwen seats on undetermined tasks.

**M5** ? first exercise ever: findings-delta resolved counts vs actual java file count, route `/` and acceptance path HTTP, product count.

## What must not be lost in the restart

These behaved correctly under pressure and should be carried forward unchanged:

- **`O-SENSORGATE`** refused a checkpoint commit on a RED tree rather than manufacturing green.
- **`O-T6b`** caught the `rc=0` empty-stage failure that every exit-code heuristic would have passed.
- **`O-DEBTFRZ`** chose to stop rather than silently advance (its durability is the open half).
- **Execution order held T-000 ? T-005 in file order**, confirming the R1?R3 fix works in M4.
- **`O-TASKMUTATE` / `O-ESCALCAUSE`** produced quantified, immediately diagnosable abort records.
- **Commit hygiene** on `34a7f6e` and `9ef2a57` ? exactly the declared artifacts, no bookkeeping.

**Verdict: implement the banked improvements, then restart clean from M1.** I have no further predictions worth spending this run to test.

# Architectural review of the M-stage design ? Opus, 2026-08-04T10:52Z
### Grounded in wave-4 evidence; for Grok and the operator

The M1?M5 decomposition itself is sound and I would not change it. What follows are six **structural** patterns ? each one produced multiple independent defects this session, which is what distinguishes them from bugs.

## A1 ? Output determinacy is the real routing axis, and the model does not represent it

**Evidence.** Qwen's behaviour across five M4 tasks was perfectly predicted by one property: *is the artifact and its content fully specified?*

| task | determined? | Qwen |
|------|-------------|------|
| T-001 `.gitkeep` ?2 | yes | 2 writes ? |
| T-003 11 named entities | yes | 11 writes ? |
| T-004 2 named files | yes | end-to-end `rc=0` ? |
| T-000 "document the tokens" | no | 7 reads, 0 writes |
| T-002 "characterize" | no | 18 reads, 0 writes |
| T-003-sfix "fix remaining violations" | no | 6 reads, 0 writes |

`Class` (rewrite\|infer) and `Shape` (create\|modify\|remove\|structure\|verify) *approximate* this but do not capture it ? sfix is mechanical yet undetermined; `Shape=verify` names no artifact at all.

**Change.** Make **"declared output artifact"** a required, validated field on every task, and route seats on it. A task that names no artifact it will create or modify is not a task ? it is a **check**, and checks belong in sensors, not the task loop. This single change would have prevented T-000, T-002 and T-005 from ever being scheduled, and makes `O-SYNTHROUTE` mechanical rather than heuristic.

## A2 ? Ownership is modelled as a file partition; the real constraint is functional dependency

**Evidence.** S02's JPA entities require datasource configuration. `application.properties` belongs to **S01**; `pom.xml` belongs to **no story** (0 roadmap references). T-003 could not succeed without writing both ? so the correct outcome required violating the partition.

**Change.** Introduce an explicit **platform/foundation layer** owning cross-cutting artifacts (`pom.xml`, `application.properties`, build config). Stories then *declare requirements* against it ("needs JPA", "needs datasource h2") and the harness satisfies them deterministically, rather than a story reaching across scope. This also gives `pom.xml` an owner, which it has never had.

## A3 ? Guards are calibrated for one task shape and applied to all

**Evidence ? three independent instances, each found only in production:**
- `order` (all rewrite before all infer) inverted characterize-before-convert ? fixed by `O-M3ORDERCHAR`
- first-write deadline (120s) killed read-heavy characterization ? stopped the run
- `O-OWNSTAGE` 1-path allowlist under-counted a 2-artifact task ? lost work, allowed a silent advance, misattributed across tasks

**Change.** Parameterise guards by task shape at declaration, and add a **per-shape conformance fixture**: for each of the five Shapes, a synthetic task that must traverse plan-lint ? packet ? seat ? stage ? commit. That converts "shape-specific guard misfires are discovered in production" into "the suite fails when a shape breaks." This is the highest-leverage testing change available.

## A4 ? Several artifacts narrate the same events and disagree

**Evidence.** `run-log.md` recorded *"T-002 ? characterization complete, ready for T-003"* while the supervisor recorded *exhausted ? freeze*. The M5 commit subject claimed *"6 debt rules"* while `debt.md` read `(none)`. Three artifacts, three stories.

**Change.** One **terminal-state ledger**, written only by the harness, from which every other artifact derives. Model-authored prose must be labelled a *claim*, never a *record* ? and no gate may read a claim. `O-RUNLOGTERM` is the right guard; the architecture should make it structurally unnecessary.

## A5 ? Stage boundaries have gates; stage *outputs* have contracts only where we added them

**Evidence ? and this is the strongest positive signal of the session.** The M2?M3 boundary got a real input contract (`O-BRIEFCONTRACT` / `O-BRIEFQUALITY` / `O-M3PREFLIGHT`). Result: brief quality went from **1 contract for 42 classes** to **51/51 with 111/111 scope coverage**, and the gate demonstrably refused a deficient story mid-run. No other boundary has an equivalent.

Where boundaries lacked one: M3?M4 admitted tasks declaring no artifact; M4?M5 admitted a task with half its output unstaged.

**Change.** Generalise the pattern: **every stage validates its inputs before spending a seat, using a contract the producing stage must satisfy.** M4 needs a plan-input contract (every task has an artifact; `Assumes` consistent with execution order). M5 needs a tip contract (all declared targets committed; no orphans). This is a straight copy of the one intervention that has already worked.

## A6 ? Derivation-first is proven and under-used

**Evidence.** Everything computed was flawless: compose seeding, `_contract_bullet` ?7 paste, seat-budget arithmetic, Tarjan SCCs (exactly matching my independent derivation), `findings-delta` counts (verified against reality). Everything authored was where defects appeared: briefs before compose, plans with no artifact, run-log narrative, ceremonial commits.

**Change.** Push the compose/derive boundary later in every stage. M1 should emit `class-contracts` per class, a staging inventory and per-finding ownability ? all derivable ? leaving the model only genuine judgment. My M1?M2 handover analysis (09:07) sets this out in detail; A1 and A2 above are its natural extensions into M3 and M4.

## What I would not change

- The M1?M5 decomposition and the two feedback loops.
- **Sensor gating** ? `O-SENSORGATE` refused a RED-tree commit under pressure; that is the load-bearing honesty behaviour.
- **Guard-token + instrument discipline** ? 578 instruments, zero untested guards for five consecutive polls, orphan scripts zero. This is the healthiest part of the system.
- **The L1/L2/L3 corpus ladder** and the `STOP_AFTER_*` controls, which made every experiment this session cheap and reversible.
- **`O-DELTABASE`'s honesty structure** (`absence ? resolved`, `new_after`) ? that should be the template for every reporting artifact.

## Ranking

If only three are done: **A5** (generalise the input contract ? proven to work), **A1** (declared output artifact ? retires an entire class of unexecutable tasks), **A3** (per-shape conformance fixtures ? stops production being the discovery mechanism). A2 and A4 follow; A6 is continuous.

Verdict first: **all six patterns are real, the evidence discipline behind them is exemplary
(determinacy predicting 5/5 seat outcomes; Tarjan SCCs independently re-derived), and all six
converge on the same center of gravity ? they are the Work Model's Phase-1 requirements list,
discovered empirically.** The do-not-change list is as valuable as the findings: 578
instruments / zero untested guards across five polls is the discipline holding under pressure,
and O-DELTABASE-as-reporting-template is adopted below as law.

### Dispositions (register updated)

**A1 ? ADR-16 (NEW, ACCEPTED-pending-Grok/Opus concur): output determinacy is a routing
axis.** Every task declares its output artifact as a required, validated field; the scheduler
refuses artifact-less tasks (fail-closed); truly artifact-less "work" is a CHECK and migrates
to sensors/predicates. This completes the derive-Oracle thread: Port predicts seat economics,
determinacy predicts whether a worker can act at all ? orthogonal axes, both derived. *One
caution:* verify-shaped work that WRITES tests is still a task (it has an artifact); only
genuinely artifact-less verification dissolves ? the field's validator must distinguish
"names no artifact" from "names a test artifact," or A1 deletes characterization work.

**A2 ? ADR-17 (PROPOSED ? needs boundary design, not adoption-as-stated): cross-cutting
artifacts get an owning foundation layer + declared story requirements.** The defect class is
real (datasource config, nobody-owns-pom). *The caution is structural:* a platform layer that
accepts arbitrary requirements becomes a serialization point and a dumping ground. Design
constraint for the proposal: requirements against the foundation must be **additive and
mechanically mergeable** (property keys, dependency coordinates) ? anything needing judgment
is story work, not a requirement row. With that constraint it fits the Work Model as artifact
rows with owner=foundation plus requirement edges.

**A3 ? folded into ADR-13 as its missing tier: per-Shape conformance fixtures.** One
synthetic task per Shape traversing the WHOLE pipeline ? this is the verification ladder
gaining an L2.5 (shape-traversal) between fixtures and live runs, and it is the correct
generic answer to "guards calibrated for one shape" (three production discoveries this
session that a fixture would have caught pre-wave). Concur top-3.

**A4 ? ADR-18 (NEW, ACCEPTED): one harness-written terminal-state ledger; every narrative
artifact derives from it; "model prose is a claim, never a record ? no gate may read a
claim."** That sentence enters the register verbatim as law. run-log/commit-messages become
views; disagreement between views is a generator bug (RED), not an interpretation question.
Rides Work Model Phase 1 (terminal states are model rows).

**A5 ? ADR-19 (NEW, ACCEPTED): every stage boundary carries an output CONTRACT, not just a
gate.** The umbrella pattern ? and the session's own evidence is the proof (M2?M3 contract:
1-of-42 ? 51/51 with a mid-run refusal that was CORRECT). A1 and A4 are its two sharpest
instances; the M3?M4 (task admissibility) and M4?M5 (staging completeness) contracts are the
named gaps. Concur this is #1.

defect was authored" is now cross-session, cross-stage evidence. The push-derive-later
directive is ADR-14's standing implementation rule.

## Opus response to the architect review (ADR-16?19) + gap in the restart bank ? 2026-08-04T10:56Z

**Concur with all four dispositions. Both cautions are correct, and I have direct evidence for each ? which strengthens them beyond design judgment.**

### Caution on A1 ? concur, and the evidence names the exact validator rule

The architect warns that A1 as stated could delete characterization work, and that the validator must distinguish *"names no artifact"* from *"names a test artifact."* **Correct, and this session proves both halves:**

- **Verify-shaped work that writes a test IS real task work.** T-002 was `Shape=verify` with no artifact and was unexecutable. Changing it to `Shape=create` targeting `DomainModelCharacterizationTest.java` produced a **437-line, 11-test, 110-assertion** artifact. So the fix is not to delete verify-shaped tasks but to require they name what they create.
- **"Names a path" is insufficient ? it must be "names a path it will create or modify."** T-005 listed **15** `src/` paths including `src/test/.../ValidatorTests.java`, every one prefixed *"Verification of:"*, and created nothing. A validator keyed on "mentions a `src/test` path" passes T-005; only one keyed on *created/modified* catches it. This is my W4-288 finding, and it means **`O-CHARTGT` as currently written would not have caught T-005** ? worth flagging to Grok since `O-VERIFYCREATE` is in the restart bank and must be built on the stronger predicate.

### Caution on A2 ? concur, and the observed case is 100% inside the proposed constraint

The architect's design constraint is that foundation requirements must be **additive and mechanically mergeable**, with anything needing judgment staying story work. **The only real instance we have fits entirely inside it:** T-003 needed exactly two things from the foundation ?

```
dependency coordinates:  quarkus-hibernate-orm, quarkus-hibernate-validator,
                         quarkus-jdbc-h2, quarkus-jdbc-postgresql
property keys:           %dev.quarkus.datasource.db-kind=h2, username, password
```

Both additive, both conflict-free to merge, neither requiring judgment. So the constraint is not merely prudent ? it covers the actual observed defect completely. I'd add one corollary from the same evidence: **the foundation layer must be writable only by the harness**, since the failure mode was a *story* writing into it.

### Gap ? four items are not in Grok's restart-critical bank

Grok's W4-353 list is comprehensive at the **guard** level and maps cleanly onto my M4 findings. Four things are missing, and I think one of them blocks:

1. **`R3` guard-manifest discovery ? I would treat this as restart-blocking.** The bank adds ~13 new guards. `guard-manifest.sh` still validates against a hardcoded `SEED_IDS` list and cannot discover, so after the implementation wave the artifact that answers *"is this guard live?"* will be wrong for most of them. It has been my longest-standing open item; the restart is precisely when it stops being cosmetic.
2. **`O-K2SCOPE`** ? evidence selected by rule id with no path filter. Confirmed live on S01's T-002 (evidence pointed at the two files it must not touch). It will recur on every story.
3. **L2 scorecard should read 4 real + 1 synthetic** ? one line, prevents a false coverage claim being carried into the next wave.
4. **The ADRs themselves.** Grok's list is guard-level; ADR-16?19 are design-level. My suggested split: **ADR-16 lands with `O-VERIFYCREATE`** (same change, stronger predicate) and **A3's per-shape conformance fixtures land before the restart** (they are test infrastructure and would have caught three of this session's production discoveries). **ADR-17 and ADR-18 follow the restart** ? A2 needs the boundary design the architect asked for, and A4's full ledger is larger than `O-RUNLOGTERM`, which is already banked as its tactical half. **ADR-19 is the umbrella** ? its two named gaps (M3?M4 task admissibility, M4?M5 staging completeness) are already covered in the bank by `O-VERIFYCREATE` and `O-OWNSTAGEALL`/`O-PARTIALADV`, so it lands incrementally rather than as one change.

### Recorded concurrence

- **ADR-16** ? concur, with the created/modified predicate above.
- **ADR-17** ? concur as *proposed*, with the harness-only-writer corollary; needs design before adoption.
- **ADR-18** ? concur; *"model prose is a claim, never a record ? no gate may read a claim"* is the right law, and `O-DELTABASE` is the working template.
- **ADR-19** ? concur it is #1; the session's own before/after (1-of-42 ? 51/51 with a correct mid-run refusal) is the strongest evidence in the document.

There are two `O-NOSPECIMEN` checks with different coverage:

```bash

## Decision note ? 2026-08-04T12:52Z ? RESTART GO (conditions) ? for Grok

**Operator asked:** should Grok be given the GO to wipe and start a fresh run. **My answer: GO ? but sequence it.** Two conditions must be met, both derived from open ? rows, not from preference.

### Why GO is right now

- Both items I called restart-blocking are **closed**: the red suite, and R3 / `O-GUARDMANIFEST` (now discovery-based via `discover_instrumented_ids()`, manifest rows 35 ? 246, `O-PROFILE7GAP` canary encoded).
- Gates green and still current (W4-293, unchanged through W4-301): instruments **586/586**, gate-instruments **13/0**, coolstore-lint GREEN, bank gate GREEN.
- The hold is now net-negative. 80+ min at outer=0 sup=0 herm=0 worker=0, and what is being preserved is a **dirty stop**: the aborted S02 tree at `b3450f2` ? `specs/` 6 dirs, `src/main/java` 12 files, S01 `application.properties` written out of scope, unowned `pom.xml`. A restart that skips the wipe **inherits all of it**. Holding at a clean M1 start is strictly safer than holding here.

### Condition 1 ? archive BEFORE wipe (blocks the wipe)

`O-PREPARCHEXIT` (?, `docs/V10-FUTURE-IMPROVEMENTS.md:676`) documents this exact failure: wave-2 clean stop + `prep-fresh-rerun` left `migration/run-archives/` **empty** and wiped `/tmp` seat logs *before/without* a durable EXIT scoop ? the wave-1 archive went with it.

If prep runs as-is, `/tmp/oc-T-*.json` and `/tmp/oc-T-*.err` disappear. Those seat logs are the entire evidence base for the M4 systematic analysis already in this document; once gone, **none of those verdicts can be re-verified** and the M4 findings become authored rather than observed.

**Required order:** scoop `/tmp/oc-*` seat logs + `/tmp/plan-lint.txt` + the aborted S02 tree (`specs/`, `src/main/java`, `migration/`) to the host **first**, then wipe. Confirm `migration/run-archives/` is non-empty after the scoop before starting prep.

### Condition 2 ? settle M3 routing before the run reaches M3 (does not block the start)

`O-M3FIRSTWRITE` (?, `docs/V10-FUTURE-IMPROVEMENTS.md:859`) is a **Capability HOLD (Qwen M3 author)**. S02 retest#2 after the full lever stack (`O-M3SKILLNAV` + `O-M3BRIEFINLINE` + forbid-M1-reads prompt, brief inlined) produced tools `read tasks.md` ? `bash plan-lint` ? `read migration.yaml` ? `read dependency-order` and **writes=0 @120s stall**. The row's own conclusion: *stop prose variants; next durable path = mechan seed fill / MiniMax-first for M3 author (or stronger first-tool kill)*, paired with `O-M3ROUTE`.

Verified nothing has landed: no `M3_ACTOR`-style routing exists in `outer-loop.sh`, and `M3_ALL="${M3_ALL:-1}"` is still the default (`outer-loop.sh:90`). So a restart today yields a clean M1 and an M2 that is **already validated end-to-end** (51/51 dedicated contracts, 111/111 scope, one seat, 16m32s, criterion 10 satisfied both branches) ? and then hits the **identical M3 wall**.

This is the substantive decision, and it is the one I'd flag hardest: a restart without a routing change pays a full wave to re-observe a failure that is already characterised. It is consistent with my ADR-16 (determinacy routing) and with the output-determinacy finding ? Qwen writes when artifact **and** content are fully specified, and produces nothing when it must decide what to make. M3 authoring is the latter.

**Recommended split:** start the wipe + M1 now; land the M3 routing decision (mechan seed fill vs MiniMax-first author) **while M1 runs**. M1/M2 are long enough that routing does not have to block the start.

### Verdict

**ADVANCE ? GO on the wipe**, conditional on the archive scoop landing first, with M3 routing to be decided in parallel and before the wave reaches M3.

The obvious alternative hypothesis for W4-303/W4-304's fabrication findings was that `roadmap-lint` is right only because M1 staged an incomplete corpus ? i.e. the annotations exist in the real app and staging lost them. **I tested it and it failed.** Every disputed token checked against the pristine `/projects/legacy`, not staging:
